150: #: Declaration-protocol version stamped into the genesis payload. A foreign
151: #: lineage carrying an unsupported version is treated as entirely inert
152: #: (never partially interpreted) — see SPEC §9.2 / build plan.
153: DECLARATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2
154: 
155: #: The frozen tombstone vocabulary (SPEC §9.2): which ``*-defined`` kind each
156: #: subject removal is expressed as. A ``*-defined`` kind ABSENT from this map
157: #: is a **singleton with no tombstone** — ``_decl.lens-defined`` (spec:
158: #: "replaced by re-definition") and ``_decl.vertex-defined`` (it IS identity).
159: #: Removing such a subject is inexpressible in the code-frozen vocabulary; the
160: #: edit ceremony (S4) refuses it rather than mint a new kind unilaterally
161: #: (thread:decl-lens-tombstone-vocab-gap — a later coordinated vocab change
162: #: with the loops-go oracle). This is the single home for the mapping; the
163: #: engine resolver imports its inverse.
164: DEFINED_TO_TOMBSTONE: dict[str, str] = {
165:     DECL_KIND_DEFINED: DECL_KIND_RETIRED,
166:     DECL_OBSERVER_DEFINED: DECL_OBSERVER_RETIRED,
167:     DECL_MEMBER_DEFINED: DECL_MEMBER_REMOVED,
168:     DECL_SOURCE_DEFINED: DECL_SOURCE_RETIRED,
169: }
170: 
171: 
172: def is_internal_kind(kind: str) -> bool:
173:     """True if ``kind`` is in the reserved declaration namespace (``_decl.*``).
174: 
175:     The single predicate every read/emit/filter site should route through
176:     (SPEC §9.4 costs; build-plan "SQL wildcard trap"). Dependency-free — a
177:     plain prefix test — because engine and apps import it directly.
178:     """
179:     return kind.startswith(DECL_PREFIX)
180: 
181: 
182: class Document(NamedTuple):
183:     """One subject-scoped declaration document: (kind, subject, payload).
184: 
185:     ``kind`` is a reserved ``_decl.*`` vocabulary constant; ``subject`` is the
186:     stable identifier of the thing described (kind name, observer name, source
187:     name, or the vertex name for singletons); ``payload`` is the complete
188:     current definition as a JSON-safe dict.
189:     """
190: 
191:     kind: str
192:     subject: str
193:     payload: dict[str, Any]
194: 
195:     def as_json(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
196:         """Flat JSON-safe form: ``{"kind", "subject", "payload"}``."""
197:         return {"kind": self.kind, "subject": self.subject, "payload": self.payload}
198: 
199: 
200: def _ensure_json_safe(obj: Any, path: str) -> None:
201:     """Assert ``obj`` is strictly JSON-safe, or raise ``ValueError`` with path.
202: 
203:     Enforced at serialization so a bad value (a non-finite float, a non-str
204:     dict key, a copied-through tuple/set/Path) is caught here — with a field
205:     path pointing at it — rather than surfacing later at JCS canonicalization.
206:     ``bool`` is allowed (a JSON scalar); every ``float`` must be finite.
207:     """
208:     # bool is an int subclass, so (str, int) already covers True/False.
209:     if obj is None or isinstance(obj, (str, int)):
210:         return
211:     if isinstance(obj, float):
212:         if not math.isfinite(obj):
213:             raise ValueError(f"non-finite float at {path}: {obj!r}")
214:         return
215:     if isinstance(obj, dict):
216:         for k, v in obj.items():
217:             if not isinstance(k, str):
218:                 raise ValueError(f"non-str dict key at {path}: {k!r}")
219:             _ensure_json_safe(v, f"{path}.{k}")
220:         return
221:     if isinstance(obj, list):
222:         for i, v in enumerate(obj):
223:             _ensure_json_safe(v, f"{path}[{i}]")
224:         return
225:     raise ValueError(f"non-JSON type {type(obj).__name__} at {path}")
226: 
227: 
228: # ===========================================================================
229: # Union serializers — AST → JSON.  Every member carries an explicit type tag.
230: # ===========================================================================
231: 
232: 
233: def _fold_op_to_json(op: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
234:     """FoldOp → ``{"op": <tag>, ...}``. Enumerates all nine members."""
235:     if isinstance(op, FoldBy):
236:         return {"op": "by", "key_field": op.key_field}
237:     if isinstance(op, FoldCount):
238:         return {"op": "count"}
239:     if isinstance(op, FoldSum):
240:         return {"op": "sum", "field": op.field}
241:     if isinstance(op, FoldLatest):
242:         return {"op": "latest"}
243:     if isinstance(op, FoldCollect):
244:         return {"op": "collect", "max_items": op.max_items}
245:     if isinstance(op, FoldMax):
246:         return {"op": "max", "field": op.field}
247:     if isinstance(op, FoldMin):
248:         return {"op": "min", "field": op.field}
249:     if isinstance(op, FoldAvg):
250:         return {"op": "avg", "field": op.field}
251:     if isinstance(op, FoldWindow):
252:         return {"op": "window", "field": op.field, "size": op.size}
253:     raise TypeError(f"unknown FoldOp member: {type(op).__name__}")
254: 
255: 
256: def _fold_op_from_json(d: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
257:     tag = d["op"]
258:     if tag == "by":
259:         return FoldBy(key_field=d["key_field"])
260:     if tag == "count":
261:         return FoldCount()
262:     if tag == "sum":
263:         return FoldSum(field=d["field"])
264:     if tag == "latest":
265:         return FoldLatest()
266:     if tag == "collect":
267:         return FoldCollect(max_items=d["max_items"])
268:     if tag == "max":
269:         return FoldMax(field=d["field"])
270:     if tag == "min":
271:         return FoldMin(field=d["field"])
272:     if tag == "avg":
273:         return FoldAvg(field=d["field"])
274:     if tag == "window":
275:         return FoldWindow(field=d["field"], size=d["size"])
276:     raise ValueError(f"unknown fold op tag: {tag!r}")
277: 
278: 
279: def _fold_decl_to_json(decl: FoldDecl) -> dict[str, Any]:
280:     return {"target": decl.target, "op": _fold_op_to_json(decl.op)}
281: 
282: 
283: def _fold_decl_from_json(d: dict[str, Any]) -> FoldDecl:
284:     return FoldDecl(target=d["target"], op=_fold_op_from_json(d["op"]))
285: 
286: 
287: def _transform_op_to_json(op: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
288:     """TransformOp → ``{"t": <tag>, ...}``. Enumerates all five members."""
289:     if isinstance(op, Strip):
290:         return {"t": "strip", "chars": op.chars}
291:     if isinstance(op, LStrip):
292:         return {"t": "lstrip", "chars": op.chars}
293:     if isinstance(op, RStrip):
294:         return {"t": "rstrip", "chars": op.chars}
295:     if isinstance(op, Replace):
296:         return {"t": "replace", "old": op.old, "new": op.new}
297:     if isinstance(op, Coerce):
298:         return {"t": "coerce", "type": op.type}
299:     raise TypeError(f"unknown TransformOp member: {type(op).__name__}")
300: 
301: 
302: def _transform_op_from_json(d: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
303:     tag = d["t"]
304:     if tag == "strip":
305:         return Strip(chars=d["chars"])
306:     if tag == "lstrip":
307:         return LStrip(chars=d["chars"])
308:     if tag == "rstrip":
309:         return RStrip(chars=d["chars"])
310:     if tag == "replace":
311:         return Replace(old=d["old"], new=d["new"])
312:     if tag == "coerce":
313:         return Coerce(type=d["type"])
314:     raise ValueError(f"unknown transform op tag: {tag!r}")
315: 
316: 
317: def _parse_step_to_json(step: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
318:     """ParseStep → ``{"step": <tag>, ...}``. Enumerates all nine members."""
319:     if isinstance(step, Skip):
320:         return {"step": "skip", "pattern": step.pattern}
321:     if isinstance(step, Split):
322:         return {"step": "split", "delimiter": step.delimiter}
323:     if isinstance(step, Pick):
324:         return {
325:             "step": "pick",
326:             "indices": list(step.indices),
327:             "names": list(step.names) if step.names is not None else None,
328:         }
329:     if isinstance(step, Select):
330:         return {"step": "select", "fields": list(step.fields)}
331:     if isinstance(step, Transform):
332:         return {
333:             "step": "transform",
334:             "field": step.field,
335:             "operations": [_transform_op_to_json(o) for o in step.operations],
336:         }
337:     if isinstance(step, Explode):
338:         return {
339:             "step": "explode",
340:             "path": step.path,
341:             "carry": dict(step.carry) if step.carry is not None else None,
342:         }
343:     if isinstance(step, Project):
344:         return {"step": "project", "fields": dict(step.fields)}
345:     if isinstance(step, Where):
346:         return {
347:             "step": "where",
348:             "path": step.path,
349:             "op": step.op,
350:             "value": step.value,
351:             "values": list(step.values),
352:         }
353:     if isinstance(step, Flatten):
354:         return {
355:             "step": "flatten",
356:             "field": step.field,
357:             "into": step.into,
358:             "extract": list(step.extract),
359:         }
360:     raise TypeError(f"unknown ParseStep member: {type(step).__name__}")
361: 
362: 
363: def _parse_step_from_json(d: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
364:     tag = d["step"]
365:     if tag == "skip":
366:         return Skip(pattern=d["pattern"])
367:     if tag == "split":
368:         return Split(delimiter=d["delimiter"])
369:     if tag == "pick":
370:         names = d["names"]
371:         return Pick(
372:             indices=tuple(d["indices"]),
373:             names=tuple(names) if names is not None else None,
374:         )
375:     if tag == "select":
376:         return Select(fields=tuple(d["fields"]))
377:     if tag == "transform":
378:         return Transform(
379:             field=d["field"],
380:             operations=tuple(_transform_op_from_json(o) for o in d["operations"]),
381:         )
382:     if tag == "explode":
383:         carry = d["carry"]
384:         return Explode(path=d["path"], carry=dict(carry) if carry is not None else None)
385:     if tag == "project":
386:         return Project(fields=dict(d["fields"]))
387:     if tag == "where":
388:         return Where(
389:             path=d["path"],
390:             op=d.get("op", "equals"),
391:             value=d.get("value"),
392:             values=tuple(d.get("values", ())),
393:         )
394:     if tag == "flatten":
395:         return Flatten(field=d["field"], into=d["into"], extract=tuple(d["extract"]))
396:     raise ValueError(f"unknown parse step tag: {tag!r}")
397: 
398: 
399: def _parse_steps_to_json(steps: tuple[Any, ...]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
400:     return [_parse_step_to_json(s) for s in steps]
401: 
402: 
403: def _parse_steps_from_json(items: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
404:     return tuple(_parse_step_from_json(d) for d in items)
405: 
406: 
407: def _boundary_condition_to_json(c: BoundaryCondition) -> dict[str, Any]:
408:     return {"target": c.target, "op": c.op, "value": c.value}
409: 
410: 
411: def _boundary_condition_from_json(d: dict[str, Any]) -> BoundaryCondition:
412:     return BoundaryCondition(target=d["target"], op=d["op"], value=d["value"])
413: 
414: 
415: def _boundary_to_json(b: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
416:     """Boundary → ``{"type": <tag>, ...}``. Enumerates all three members."""
417:     if isinstance(b, BoundaryWhen):
418:         return {
419:             "type": "when",
420:             "kind": b.kind,
421:             "match": [[k, v] for (k, v) in b.match],
422:             "conditions": [_boundary_condition_to_json(c) for c in b.conditions],
423:             "run": b.run,
424:         }
425:     if isinstance(b, BoundaryAfter):
426:         return {"type": "after", "count": b.count, "run": b.run}
427:     if isinstance(b, BoundaryEvery):
428:         return {"type": "every", "count": b.count, "run": b.run}
429:     raise TypeError(f"unknown Boundary member: {type(b).__name__}")
430: 
431: 
432: def _boundary_from_json(d: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
433:     tag = d["type"]
434:     if tag == "when":
435:         return BoundaryWhen(
436:             kind=d["kind"],
437:             match=tuple((k, v) for k, v in d.get("match", ())),
438:             conditions=tuple(
439:                 _boundary_condition_from_json(c) for c in d.get("conditions", ())
440:             ),
441:             run=d.get("run"),
442:         )
443:     if tag == "after":
444:         return BoundaryAfter(count=d["count"], run=d.get("run"))
445:     if tag == "every":
446:         return BoundaryEvery(count=d["count"], run=d.get("run"))
447:     raise ValueError(f"unknown boundary type tag: {tag!r}")
448: 
449: 
450: def _trigger_to_json(t: Trigger | None) -> list[str] | None:
451:     return list(t.kinds) if t is not None else None
452: 
453: 
454: def _trigger_from_json(v: list[str] | None) -> Trigger | None:
455:     return Trigger(kinds=tuple(v)) if v is not None else None
456: 
457: 
458: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
459: # LoopDef  ↔  _decl.kind-defined payload
460: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
461: 
462: 
463: def _loop_def_to_payload(loop: LoopDef) -> dict[str, Any]:
464:     return {
465:         "folds": [_fold_decl_to_json(f) for f in loop.folds],
466:         "boundary": _boundary_to_json(loop.boundary)
467:         if loop.boundary is not None
468:         else None,
469:         "search": list(loop.search),
470:         "parse": _parse_steps_to_json(loop.parse),
471:         "preview": list(loop.preview_fields),
472:         "edges": [{"field": e.field, "target": e.target} for e in loop.edges],
473:         "lifecycle": (
474:             {"field": loop.lifecycle.field, "active": list(loop.lifecycle.active)}
475:             if loop.lifecycle is not None
476:             else None
477:         ),
478:     }
479: 
480: 
481: def _loop_def_from_payload(p: dict[str, Any]) -> LoopDef:
482:     boundary = p.get("boundary")
483:     # `.get()` default keeps §9.2 forward/backward compat: a kind-defined
484:     # document minted before the lifecycle facet existed simply lacks the key
485:     # and projects to `lifecycle=None`. DECLARATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION is unbumped
486:     # (additive field — arbiter S5-F3).
487:     lc = p.get("lifecycle")
488:     return LoopDef(
489:         folds=tuple(_fold_decl_from_json(f) for f in p.get("folds", ())),
490:         boundary=_boundary_from_json(boundary) if boundary is not None else None,
491:         search=tuple(p.get("search", ())),
492:         parse=_parse_steps_from_json(p.get("parse", [])),
493:         preview_fields=tuple(p.get("preview", ())),
494:         edges=tuple(
495:             EdgeDecl(field=e["field"], target=e["target"]) for e in p.get("edges", ())
496:         ),
497:         lifecycle=(
498:             LifecycleDecl(field=lc["field"], active=tuple(lc["active"]))
499:             if lc is not None
500:             else None
501:         ),
502:     )
503: 
504: 
505: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
506: # ObserverDecl  ↔  _decl.observer-defined payload
507: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
508: 
509: 
510: def _observer_to_payload(o: ObserverDecl) -> dict[str, Any]:
511:     grant = (
512:         {"potential": sorted(o.grant.potential)} if o.grant is not None else None
513:     )
514:     return {
515:         "name": o.name,
516:         "identity": o.identity,
517:         "grant": grant,
518:         "key": o.key,
519:     }
520: 
521: 
522: def _observer_from_payload(p: dict[str, Any]) -> ObserverDecl:
523:     grant_d = p.get("grant")
524:     grant = (
525:         GrantDecl(potential=frozenset(grant_d["potential"]))
526:         if grant_d is not None
527:         else None
528:     )
529:     return ObserverDecl(
530:         name=p["name"],
531:         identity=p.get("identity"),
532:         grant=grant,
533:         key=p.get("key"),
534:     )

563: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
564: # Sources  ↔  _decl.source-defined payloads
565: #
566: # Three variants share the source-defined kind, discriminated by "form":
567: #   - "path":     a bare .loop path entry in VertexFile.sources
568: #   - "template": a TemplateSource entry in VertexFile.sources
569: #   - "inline":   an InlineSource inside a VertexFile.sources_blocks group;
570: #                 carries "block" (group index) + "mode" so the SourcesBlock
571: #                 grouping and execution mode reconstruct exactly.
572: #
573: # Source Paths (host-bound wiring) stay inside these payloads by design —
574: # this is the Ingress / provenance stratum (SPEC §9.2), not portable config.
575: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
576: 
577: 
578: def _source_params_to_json(sp: SourceParams) -> dict[str, Any]:
579:     return {"values": dict(sp.values)}
580: 
581: 
582: def _source_params_from_json(d: dict[str, Any]) -> SourceParams:
583:     return SourceParams(values=dict(d["values"]))
584: 
585: 
586: def _content_sha256(path: Path, base: Path | None) -> str | None:
587:     """SHA-256 of a referenced file's bytes, or None if unreadable.
588: 
589:     Pins WHAT the referenced ``.loop``/template said at absorb time so later
590:     drift is detectable (surfaced at ``absorb -n``, never auto-absorbed).
591:     Content capture as a portable document form is deferred — embedding raw
592:     text would re-leak env values the indirection rule just excluded.
593:     """
594:     import hashlib
595: 
596:     candidate = path if path.is_absolute() else ((base / path) if base else path)
597:     try:
598:         return hashlib.sha256(candidate.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
599:     except OSError:
600:         return None
601: 
602: 
603: def _template_source_to_payload(
604:     t: TemplateSource, *, base: Path | None = None
605: ) -> dict[str, Any]:
606:     return {
607:         "form": "template",
608:         "template": str(t.template),
609:         "content_sha256": _content_sha256(t.template, base),
610:         "params": [_source_params_to_json(sp) for sp in t.params],
611:         "from": {
612:             "strategy": "file",
613:             "path": str(t.from_.path),
614:             # Pin the params file too — its rows parameterize the template,
615:             # so silent drift is the same auto-enactment hazard as the
616:             # template itself (closing re-review #3).
617:             "params_sha256": _content_sha256(Path(t.from_.path), base),
618:         }
619:         if t.from_ is not None
620:         else None,
621:         "loop": _loop_def_to_payload(t.loop) if t.loop is not None else None,
622:     }
623: 
624: 
625: def _template_source_from_payload(p: dict[str, Any]) -> TemplateSource:
626:     # "content_sha256" is provenance (drift pin), not AST state — ignored here.
627:     from_d = p.get("from")
628:     loop_d = p.get("loop")
629:     return TemplateSource(
630:         template=Path(p["template"]),
631:         params=tuple(_source_params_from_json(sp) for sp in p.get("params", ())),
632:         from_=FromFile(path=Path(from_d["path"])) if from_d is not None else None,
633:         loop=_loop_def_from_payload(loop_d) if loop_d is not None else None,
634:     )
635: 
636: 
637: def _inline_source_to_payload(
638:     s: InlineSource, *, block: int, mode: str
639: ) -> dict[str, Any]:
640:     return {
641:         "form": "inline",
642:         "block": block,
643:         "mode": mode,
644:         "command": s.command,
645:         "kind": s.kind,
646:         "observer": s.observer,
647:         "every": s.every,
648:         "on": _trigger_to_json(s.on),
649:         "format": s.format,
650:         "timeout": s.timeout,
651:         "origin": s.origin,
652:         # Env VALUES are ingress (SPEC §9.5 secrets-indirection): the
653:         # declaration records the key SET (shape — adding/removing a key is a
654:         # real edit); values live in the file and are re-attached at
655:         # resolution (load_declaration), never absorbed into payloads.
656:         "env": [k for (k, _v) in s.env],
657:         "parse": _parse_steps_to_json(s.parse),
658:         "path": s.path,
659:     }
660: 
661: 
662: def _inline_source_from_payload(p: dict[str, Any]) -> InlineSource:
663:     return InlineSource(
664:         command=p["command"],
665:         kind=p["kind"],
666:         observer=p.get("observer", ""),
667:         every=p.get("every", ""),
668:         on=_trigger_from_json(p.get("on")),
669:         format=p.get("format", "lines"),
670:         timeout=p.get("timeout", "60s"),
671:         origin=p.get("origin", ""),
672:         # Tolerant reader: new form is a key list (values are ingress,
673:         # re-attached from the file at resolution); legacy pre-indirection
674:         # rows carried [key, value] pairs — honor their recorded values.
675:         env=tuple(
676:             (e, "") if isinstance(e, str) else (e[0], e[1])
677:             for e in p.get("env", ())
678:         ),
679:         parse=_parse_steps_from_json(p.get("parse", [])),
680:         path=p.get("path", ""),
681:     )
682: 
683: 
684: def _source_subject(entry: Any) -> str:
685:     """Stable subject for a source-defined document."""
686:     if isinstance(entry, TemplateSource):
687:         return str(entry.template)
688:     if isinstance(entry, InlineSource):
689:         return entry.command
690:     # bare path entry
691:     return str(entry)
692: 
693: 
694: # ===========================================================================
695: # Public API — decompose and project
696: # ===========================================================================
697: 
698: 
699: def vertex_to_documents(ast: VertexFile) -> list[Document]:
700:     """Decompose a ``VertexFile`` AST into per-subject declaration documents.
701: 
702:     Emission order (deterministic): the ``_decl.vertex-defined`` singleton,
703:     then ``_decl.kind-defined`` per loop, ``_decl.observer-defined`` per
704:     observer, ``_decl.member-defined`` per combine entry, ``_decl.source-defined``
705:     per source (bare/template entries first, then inline sources per block),
706:     and ``_decl.lens-defined`` if a lens is declared.
707: 
708:     Each multi-instance document carries an ``order`` field (encounter
709:     position) and a subject deduplicated per kind (see module docstring:
710:     "Order is meaning", "Subject uniqueness"). Residence (``store`` locator,
711:     ``path``) is excluded. Every payload is validated JSON-safe before return.
712:     """
713:     docs: list[Document] = []
714:     order = 0  # global encounter position across all multi-instance documents
715: 
716:     # Per-kind subject deduplication. Allocate against the SET of subjects
717:     # already issued for this kind (not a per-base counter) so a suffix never
718:     # lands on a naturally-occurring subject: bases ["base", "base", "base#2"]
719:     # → ["base", "base#2", "base#3"], all distinct. Identity only — projection
720:     # reconstructs every value from the payload, never from the subject.
721:     issued: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
722: 
723:     def _subject(kind: str, base: str) -> str:
724:         seen = issued.setdefault(kind, set())
725:         candidate = base
726:         n = 1
727:         while candidate in seen:
728:             n += 1
729:             candidate = f"{base}#{n}"
730:         seen.add(candidate)
731:         return candidate
732: 
733:     def _emit(kind: str, base: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
734:         nonlocal order
735:         payload["order"] = order
736:         order += 1
737:         docs.append(Document(kind=kind, subject=_subject(kind, base), payload=payload))
738: 
739:     # vertex-defined singleton — subject is the vertex name (self); no order.
740:     docs.append(
741:         Document(
742:             kind=DECL_VERTEX_DEFINED,
743:             subject=ast.name,
744:             payload={
745:                 "name": ast.name,
746:                 "strict": ast.strict,
747:                 "observer_scoped": ast.observer_scoped,
748:                 "discover": ast.discover,
749:                 "emit": ast.emit,
750:                 "routes": dict(ast.routes) if ast.routes is not None else None,
751:                 "vertices": [str(p) for p in ast.vertices]
752:                 if ast.vertices is not None
753:                 else None,
754:                 "boundary": [_boundary_to_json(b) for b in ast.boundary],
755:                 # sources live in their own documents; this flag preserves the
756:                 # None-vs-empty-tuple distinction of VertexFile.sources.
757:                 "sources_present": ast.sources is not None,
758:                 # authoritative block structure (index + mode); None when there
759:                 # are no sources_blocks. Members are the inline source docs.
760:                 "source_blocks": [
761:                     {"index": i, "mode": b.mode}
762:                     for i, b in enumerate(ast.sources_blocks)
763:                 ]
764:                 if ast.sources_blocks is not None
765:                 else None,
766:             },
767:         )
768:     )
769: 
770:     # kind-defined per loop (dict preserves insertion order).
771:     for kind_name, loop in ast.loops.items():
772:         _emit(DECL_KIND_DEFINED, kind_name, _loop_def_to_payload(loop))
773: 
774:     # observer-defined per observer.
775:     for obs in ast.observers or ():
776:         _emit(DECL_OBSERVER_DEFINED, obs.name, _observer_to_payload(obs))
777: 
778:     # member-defined per combine entry.
779:     for entry in ast.combine or ():
780:         _emit(DECL_MEMBER_DEFINED, entry.name, _combine_to_payload(entry))
781: 
782:     # source-defined — bare/template entries from VertexFile.sources ...
783:     base = ast.path.parent if ast.path is not None else None
784:     for entry in ast.sources or ():
785:         if isinstance(entry, TemplateSource):
786:             payload = _template_source_to_payload(entry, base=base)
787:         else:
788:             payload = {
789:                 "form": "path",
790:                 "path": str(entry),
791:                 "content_sha256": _content_sha256(Path(entry), base),
792:             }
793:         _emit(DECL_SOURCE_DEFINED, _source_subject(entry), payload)
794: 
795:     # ... then inline sources from VertexFile.sources_blocks, tagged with
796:     # their block index so projection can rebuild block grouping.
797:     for block_idx, block in enumerate(ast.sources_blocks or ()):
798:         # ast.py's custom frozen decorator rebuilds classes dynamically, so
799:         # Pyright can't resolve SourcesBlock.sources' type (infers Never).
800:         for src in block.sources:  # pyright: ignore[reportGeneralTypeIssues]
801:             _emit(
802:                 DECL_SOURCE_DEFINED,
803:                 _source_subject(src),
804:                 _inline_source_to_payload(src, block=block_idx, mode=block.mode),
805:             )
806: 
807:     # lens-defined singleton (whole-vertex fold/stream selection).
808:     if ast.lens is not None:
809:         _emit(DECL_LENS_DEFINED, ast.name, _lens_to_payload(ast.lens))
810: 
811:     # Enforce JSON safety (finite floats, str keys, JSON scalars) at the source.
812:     for d in docs:
813:         _ensure_json_safe(d.payload, f"{d.kind}:{d.subject}")
814: 
815:     return docs
816: 
817: 
818: def genesis_payload(ast: VertexFile) -> dict[str, Any]:
819:     """The genesis event payload: the whole document set + protocol version.
820: 
821:     ``genesis`` opens a store's lineage by absorbing the initial declaration
822:     whole (SPEC §9.2). JSON-safe; residence excluded like every document.
823:     """
824:     return {
825:         # Ordinary initialization remains v1. Protocol 2 is reserved for an
826:         # explicitly selected fresh runtime epoch at migration adoption.
827:         "protocol": 1,
828:         "documents": [d.as_json() for d in vertex_to_documents(ast)],
829:     }
830: 
831: 
832: def _as_triple(item: Any) -> tuple[str, str, dict[str, Any]]:
833:     """Normalize a document to (kind, subject, payload).
834: 
835:     Accepts :class:`Document` namedtuples and plain mappings with
836:     ``kind``/``subject``/``payload`` keys (e.g. from a genesis payload).
837:     """
838:     if isinstance(item, Document):
839:         return item.kind, item.subject, item.payload
840:     return item["kind"], item["subject"], item.get("payload", {})
841: 
842: 
843: def _rebuild_sources_blocks(
844:     source_blocks_decl: list[dict[str, Any]] | None,
845:     inline_items: list[tuple[int, int, str, str, InlineSource]],
846: ) -> tuple[SourcesBlock, ...] | None:
847:     """Reassemble ``sources_blocks`` from the singleton's block structure.
848: 
849:     ``source_blocks_decl`` is the authoritative ``[{"index", "mode"}, ...]``
850:     recorded on the vertex-defined singleton; ``inline_items`` are the inline
851:     source docs as ``(order, block_index, mode, subject, InlineSource)``. Each
852:     inline source drops into its block by index, block members ordered by
853:     ``(order, subject)`` — subject breaks ties deterministically when duplicate
854:     ``order`` values appear (possible in edit-era document sets). An empty block
855:     survives as a member-less entry.
856: 
857:     Falls back to inferring blocks from inline tags (mode carried on each
858:     inline doc) when the singleton has no ``source_blocks`` — tolerating
859:     documents from an emitter predating the structural record (forward compat).
860:     """
861:     ordered = sorted(inline_items, key=lambda t: (t[0], t[3]))  # (order, subject)
862:     by_block: dict[int, list[InlineSource]] = {}
863:     for _order, block_idx, _mode, _subject, src in ordered:
864:         by_block.setdefault(block_idx, []).append(src)
865: 
866:     if source_blocks_decl is not None:
867:         return tuple(
868:             SourcesBlock(
869:                 mode=entry["mode"],
870:                 sources=tuple(by_block.get(entry["index"], ())),
871:             )
872:             for entry in source_blocks_decl
873:         )
874: 
875:     if not inline_items:
876:         return None
877: 
878:     # Fallback: no structural record — group by block index in first-seen
879:     # order, taking each block's mode from its first inline source's doc.
880:     mode_by_block: dict[int, str] = {}
881:     order_seen: list[int] = []
882:     for _order, block_idx, mode, _subject, _src in ordered:
883:         if block_idx not in mode_by_block:
884:             order_seen.append(block_idx)
885:             mode_by_block[block_idx] = mode
886:     return tuple(
887:         SourcesBlock(mode=mode_by_block[i], sources=tuple(by_block[i]))
888:         for i in order_seen
889:     )
890: 
891: 
892: def documents_to_vertex(
893:     documents: Any,
894:     *,
895:     path: Path | None = None,
896:     store: Path | None = None,
897:     store_backend: BackendDecl | None = None,
898:     store_location: str | None = None,
899: ) -> VertexFile:
900:     """Project declaration documents back to a ``VertexFile`` AST.
901: 
902:     ``path``, ``store``, ``store_backend`` and ``store_location`` are residence, supplied by the
903:     caller — they are not present in the documents. Pure inverse of
904:     :func:`vertex_to_documents` modulo those four fields.
905: 
906:     ``store_backend`` is residence for the same reason the locator is: which
907:     adapter opens a store is an operational choice about where the vertex
908:     lives, and putting an adapter name into signed declaration history would
909:     make it part of the vertex's absorbed identity. It is threaded rather
910:     than defaulted because a caller that drops it does not get an error — it
911:     gets a vertex whose backend arm has silently reverted to inference.
912: 
913:     Forward-compatible (normative, SPEC §9.2): unknown ``_decl.*`` kinds are
914:     skipped, and unknown fields inside a known document are ignored, so a
915:     newer protocol's documents project safely under this reader.
916:     """
917:     name: str | None = None
918:     strict = False
919:     observer_scoped = False
920:     discover: str | None = None
921:     emit: str | None = None
922:     routes: dict[str, str] | None = None
923:     vertices: tuple[Path, ...] | None = None
924:     boundary: tuple[Any, ...] = ()
925:     sources_present = False
926:     # authoritative block structure from the vertex-defined singleton.
927:     source_blocks_decl: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None
928: 
929:     # Collect multi-instance docs as (order, subject, value) so structure is
930:     # restored by sorting on (order, subject) — encounter order is meaning.
931:     kind_items: list[tuple[int, str, LoopDef]] = []
932:     observer_items: list[tuple[int, str, ObserverDecl]] = []
933:     member_items: list[tuple[int, str, CombineEntry]] = []
934:     lens_items: list[tuple[int, str, LensDecl]] = []
935:     bare_items: list[tuple[int, str, Any]] = []  # path / template entries
936:     # (order, block_index, mode, subject, InlineSource)
937:     inline_items: list[tuple[int, int, str, str, InlineSource]] = []
938: 
939:     def _order(p: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
940:         return p.get("order", 0)
941: 
942:     for item in documents:
943:         kind, subject, payload = _as_triple(item)
944: 
945:         if kind == DECL_VERTEX_DEFINED:
946:             name = payload["name"]
947:             strict = payload.get("strict", False)
948:             observer_scoped = payload.get("observer_scoped", False)
949:             discover = payload.get("discover")
950:             emit = payload.get("emit")
951:             r = payload.get("routes")
952:             routes = dict(r) if r is not None else None
953:             v = payload.get("vertices")
954:             vertices = tuple(Path(p) for p in v) if v is not None else None
955:             boundary = tuple(_boundary_from_json(b) for b in payload.get("boundary", ()))
956:             sources_present = payload.get("sources_present", False)
957:             source_blocks_decl = payload.get("source_blocks")
958: 
959:         elif kind == DECL_KIND_DEFINED:
960:             kind_items.append((_order(payload), subject, _loop_def_from_payload(payload)))
961: 
962:         elif kind == DECL_OBSERVER_DEFINED:
963:             observer_items.append((_order(payload), subject, _observer_from_payload(payload)))
964: 
965:         elif kind == DECL_MEMBER_DEFINED:
966:             member_items.append((_order(payload), subject, _combine_from_payload(payload)))
967: 
968:         elif kind == DECL_LENS_DEFINED:
969:             lens_items.append((_order(payload), subject, _lens_from_payload(payload)))
970: 
971:         elif kind == DECL_SOURCE_DEFINED:
972:             form = payload.get("form")
973:             if form == "path":
974:                 bare_items.append((_order(payload), subject, Path(payload["path"])))
975:             elif form == "template":
976:                 bare_items.append(
977:                     (_order(payload), subject, _template_source_from_payload(payload))
978:                 )
979:             elif form == "inline":
980:                 inline_items.append(
981:                     (
982:                         _order(payload),
983:                         payload["block"],
984:                         payload.get("mode", "sequential"),
985:                         subject,
986:                         _inline_source_from_payload(payload),
987:                     )
988:                 )
989:             # unknown form → skip (forward compat)
990: 
991:         # unknown _decl.* kind → skip (forward compat)
992: 
993:     if name is None:
994:         raise ValueError("documents missing a _decl.vertex-defined singleton")
995: 
996:     # kind-defined: dict rebuilt in (order, subject) order.
997:     loops: dict[str, LoopDef] = {}
998:     for _o, subject, loop in sorted(kind_items, key=lambda t: (t[0], t[1])):
999:         loops[subject] = loop
1000: 
1001:     observers = [o for _o, _s, o in sorted(observer_items, key=lambda t: (t[0], t[1]))]
1002:     combine = [c for _o, _s, c in sorted(member_items, key=lambda t: (t[0], t[1]))]
1003:     lens = (
1004:         sorted(lens_items, key=lambda t: (t[0], t[1]))[0][2] if lens_items else None
1005:     )
1006: 
1007:     # Reassemble VertexFile.sources (bare/template entries) in (order, subject).
1008:     bare_sorted = [e for _o, _s, e in sorted(bare_items, key=lambda t: (t[0], t[1]))]
1009:     sources: tuple[Any, ...] | None
1010:     if bare_sorted:
1011:         sources = tuple(bare_sorted)
1012:     elif sources_present:
1013:         sources = ()  # empty `sources {}` block — the one reachable empty tuple
1014:     else:
1015:         sources = None
1016: 
1017:     sources_blocks = _rebuild_sources_blocks(source_blocks_decl, inline_items)
1018: 
1019:     return VertexFile(
1020:         name=name,
1021:         loops=loops,
1022:         store=store,
1023:         store_backend=store_backend,
1024:         store_location=store_location,
1025:         discover=discover,
1026:         sources=sources,
1027:         vertices=vertices,
1028:         routes=routes,
1029:         emit=emit,
1030:         combine=tuple(combine) if combine else None,
1031:         sources_blocks=sources_blocks,
1032:         observers=tuple(observers) if observers else None,
1033:         lens=lens,
1034:         boundary=boundary,
1035:         observer_scoped=observer_scoped,
1036:         strict=strict,
1037:         path=path,
1038:     )
1039: 
1040: 
1041: # ===========================================================================
1042: # Subject-granular diff — the edit ceremony's grammar half (SPEC §9.2, S4)
1043: # ===========================================================================
1044: #
1045: # Re-absorbing an edited ``.vertex`` diffs its freshly-parsed document set
1046: # against the store's fold head (Latest per (kind, subject), self-lineage) and
1047: # re-emits ONLY the changed subjects as whole documents. This module supplies
1048: # the pure-grammar half: comparing two document sets. The store half (stamping
1049: # lineage, signing, appending atomically) lives in ``engine.sqlite_store``.
1050: #
1051: # Whole-document only (SPEC §9.2): a subject is "changed" iff its complete
1052: # payload — INCLUDING the ``order`` field — differs by value. There are no
1053: # facet deltas. This makes the round-trip exact (the resolver's overlay fold,
1054: # applied over the head, reproduces the edited file's document set) and
1055: # idempotence exact (an unchanged file re-parses to identical payloads, so the
1056: # diff is empty). ``order`` is a dense global counter, so a structural insert
1057: # shifts downstream subjects' ``order`` and honestly re-emits them — "order is
1058: # meaning" (see module docstring).
1059: 
1060: 
1061: #: Inverse of :data:`DEFINED_TO_TOMBSTONE`: which ``*-defined`` subject a
1062: #: tombstone kind removes. Used by :func:`apply_changes` to fold a removal.
1063: _TOMBSTONE_TO_DEFINED: dict[str, str] = {v: k for k, v in DEFINED_TO_TOMBSTONE.items()}
1064: 
1065: 
1066: class EditRefused(ValueError):
1067:     """A re-absorb edit is inexpressible in the frozen declaration vocabulary.
1068: 
1069:     Two cases, both structural refusals rather than silent lies:
1070: 
1071:     - **Singleton removal.** Dropping a ``_decl.lens-defined`` has no tombstone
1072:       in the code-frozen vocabulary (SPEC §9.2 — a lens is "replaced by
1073:       re-definition"), so removal cannot be recorded. Rather than mint a new
1074:       kind unilaterally (thread:decl-lens-tombstone-vocab-gap, a later
1075:       coordinated change with the loops-go oracle), the ceremony refuses.
1076: 
1077:     - **Identity change.** The ``_decl.vertex-defined`` singleton's subject is
1078:       the vertex name; a rename would surface as remove-old + add-new. The name
1079:       is meaning-critical self-description, so a post-genesis rename is a
1080:       deliberate identity ceremony, never a routine edit — refused.
1081:     """
1082: 
1083: 
1084: class Change(NamedTuple):
1085:     """One subject-granular declaration change (SPEC §9.2, S4).
1086: 
1087:     ``kind`` is the FINAL event kind: a ``_decl.*-defined`` kind for an
1088:     add/modify, or the paired ``_decl.*-retired``/``-removed`` tombstone for a
1089:     removal. ``payload`` is the whole document payload for a definition, or
1090:     ``None`` for a removal. ``annotation`` is the ``change=`` legibility label —
1091:     ``"added"``, ``"modified"``, or ``"removed"`` (SPEC §9.2: "MAY carry a
1092:     ``change`` annotation"). Emitters ride ``annotation`` on the row as
1093:     ``change=``; the resolver ignores it.
1094:     """
1095: 
1096:     kind: str
1097:     subject: str
1098:     payload: dict[str, Any] | None
1099:     annotation: str
1100: 
1101: 
1102: def diff_documents(head: Any, new: Any) -> list[Change]:
1103:     """Diff a fold head against a freshly-parsed document set → changes.
1104: 
1105:     ``head`` and ``new`` are each an iterable of documents — :class:`Document`
1106:     namedtuples or plain ``{"kind", "subject", "payload"}`` mappings (the
1107:     resolver returns the latter). Both are keyed by ``(kind, subject)``.
1108: 
1109:     Yields (in a deterministic order — additions/modifications in ``new``'s
1110:     iteration order, then removals in ``head``'s iteration order):
1111: 
1112:     - ``"added"`` — a ``(kind, subject)`` in ``new`` but not ``head``.
1113:     - ``"modified"`` — present in both, payloads differ by value.
1114:     - ``"removed"`` — in ``head`` but not ``new``; emitted as the paired
1115:       tombstone kind.
1116: 
1117:     Raises :class:`EditRefused` if a removal targets a singleton with no
1118:     tombstone (``_decl.lens-defined`` → vocabulary gap; ``_decl.vertex-defined``
1119:     → identity/rename). Unchanged subjects yield nothing.
1120:     """
1121:     head_map: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}
1122:     for item in head:
1123:         k, s, p = _as_triple(item)
1124:         head_map[(k, s)] = p
1125: 
1126:     new_map: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}
1127:     changes: list[Change] = []
1128:     for item in new:
1129:         k, s, p = _as_triple(item)
1130:         new_map[(k, s)] = p
1131:         prev = head_map.get((k, s))
1132:         if prev is None:
1133:             changes.append(Change(kind=k, subject=s, payload=p, annotation="added"))
1134:         elif prev != p:
1135:             changes.append(Change(kind=k, subject=s, payload=p, annotation="modified"))
1136:         # else unchanged → nothing
1137: 
1138:     for (k, s), _p in head_map.items():
1139:         if (k, s) in new_map:
1140:             continue
1141:         tombstone = DEFINED_TO_TOMBSTONE.get(k)
1142:         if tombstone is None:
1143:             if k == DECL_VERTEX_DEFINED:
1144:                 raise EditRefused(
1145:                     f"vertex identity change: the vertex-defined subject "
1146:                     f"{s!r} was removed (a rename). The vertex name is "
1147:                     "meaning-critical identity — a post-genesis rename is a "
1148:                     "deliberate ceremony, not an edit; not supported by "
1149:                     "re-absorb."
1150:                 )
1151:             raise EditRefused(
1152:                 f"cannot remove singleton {k!r} (subject {s!r}): the frozen "
1153:                 "declaration vocabulary has no tombstone for it "
1154:                 "(SPEC §9.2 — a lens is replaced by re-definition, never "
1155:                 "removed). Re-add the lens, or edit it in place; removal is a "
1156:                 "pending coordinated vocabulary change "
1157:                 "(thread:decl-lens-tombstone-vocab-gap)."
1158:             )
1159:         changes.append(Change(kind=tombstone, subject=s, payload=None, annotation="removed"))
1160: 
1161:     return changes
1162: 
1163: 
1164: def apply_changes(head: Any, changes: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1165:     """Fold ``changes`` over ``head`` → the resulting document set (pure).
1166: 
1167:     Mirrors the store resolver's overlay/tombstone fold
1168:     (``engine.declaration.resolve_declaration_documents``) at the grammar tier,
1169:     with NO store: a ``*-defined`` change replaces its ``(kind, subject)``
1170:     document; a tombstone removes the paired ``*-defined`` subject. Returned
1171:     documents are ``{"kind", "subject", "payload"}`` dicts in insertion order
1172:     (definitions keep position across replacement).
1173: 
1174:     This is the reconstruction oracle for the diff property test:
1175:     ``apply_changes(head, diff_documents(head, new))`` equals ``new`` as a
1176:     document set. It intentionally re-implements the fold independently of the
1177:     engine resolver so the two agree by construction, not by shared code.
1178:     """
1179:     docs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}
1180:     for item in head:
1181:         k, s, p = _as_triple(item)
1182:         docs[(k, s)] = {"kind": k, "subject": s, "payload": p}
1183: 
1184:     for ch in changes:
1185:         kind, subject, payload, _annotation = (
1186:             (ch.kind, ch.subject, ch.payload, ch.annotation)
1187:             if isinstance(ch, Change)
1188:             else (ch["kind"], ch["subject"], ch.get("payload"), ch.get("change"))
1189:         )
1190:         defined = _TOMBSTONE_TO_DEFINED.get(kind)
1191:         if defined is not None:
1192:             docs.pop((defined, subject), None)
1193:         else:
1194:             docs[(kind, subject)] = {
1195:                 "kind": kind,
1196:                 "subject": subject,
1197:                 "payload": payload if payload is not None else {},
1198:             }
1199: 
1200:     return list(docs.values())

=== libs/lang/tests/test_document.py ===
1: """Round-trip and forward-compat tests for the declaration document form.
2: 
3: The AST classes are frozen dataclasses with a generated structural ``__eq__``
4: (see ``ast.py`` ``_frozen``), so ``==`` compares field tuples recursively —
5: we can assert projected-AST equality directly. Residence (``path``, ``store``)
6: is stripped from documents, so round-trip tests supply the *original*
7: residence back at projection time; the projected AST then equals the original

346: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
347: # JSON safety — payloads are strictly JSON types (no tuples/sets/NaN)
348: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
349: 
350: def _assert_json_pure(obj: object, where: str) -> None:
351:     if isinstance(obj, bool) or obj is None or isinstance(obj, (str, int)):
352:         return
353:     if isinstance(obj, float):
354:         assert obj == obj and obj not in (float("inf"), float("-inf")), (
355:             f"non-finite float at {where}"
356:         )
357:         return
358:     if isinstance(obj, dict):
359:         for k, v in obj.items():
360:             assert isinstance(k, str), f"non-str dict key at {where}: {k!r}"
361:             _assert_json_pure(v, f"{where}.{k}")
362:         return
363:     if isinstance(obj, list):
364:         for i, v in enumerate(obj):
365:             _assert_json_pure(v, f"{where}[{i}]")
366:         return
367:     raise AssertionError(f"non-JSON type {type(obj).__name__} at {where}")
368:

370: @pytest.mark.parametrize("name", sorted(ALL_CASES))
371: def test_payloads_are_json_safe(name: str) -> None:
372:     ast = parse_vertex(ALL_CASES[name])
373:     for doc in vertex_to_documents(ast):
374:         assert isinstance(doc.kind, str) and is_internal_kind(doc.kind)
375:         assert isinstance(doc.subject, str)
376:         _assert_json_pure(doc.payload, f"{doc.kind}:{doc.subject}")
377:         # json.dumps must succeed with no tolerance for NaN/Infinity.
378:         json.dumps(doc.payload, allow_nan=False)
379:     # Whole genesis payload dumps too.
380:     json.dumps(genesis_payload(ast), allow_nan=False)

433: def test_backend_survives_the_document_round_trip() -> None:
434:     """The arm the declaration round-trip would otherwise silently drop.
435: 
436:     ``loops add`` / ``loops rm`` re-project a vertex through its documents.
437:     Residence is caller-supplied, so any residence field not threaded comes
438:     back None — and a store whose backend arm came back None falls straight
439:     back to suffix inference, which is the failure explicit declaration
440:     exists to end. No pre-existing test would have caught it.
441:     """
442:     ast = parse_vertex(BACKEND_DECLARED)
443:     assert ast.store_backend == BackendDecl(name="duckdb")
444:     docs = vertex_to_documents(ast)
445:     projected = documents_to_vertex(
446:         docs, path=ast.path, store=ast.store, store_backend=ast.store_backend,
447:         store_location=ast.store_location,
448:     )
449:     assert projected.store_backend == BackendDecl(name="duckdb")
450:     assert projected.store == ast.store

603: def test_nested_unknown_field_ignored() -> None:
604:     """Unknown fields inside nested union dicts (fold op, boundary, parse step,
605:     source payload) are ignored, not fatal."""
606:     ast = parse_vertex(KITCHEN_SINK)
607:     docs = vertex_to_documents(ast)
608:     patched: list[Document] = []
609:     for d in docs:
610:         p = json.loads(json.dumps(d.payload))  # deep copy
611:         if d.kind == DECL_KIND_DEFINED and p.get("folds"):
612:             p["folds"][0]["op"]["future_op_field"] = "x"  # inside a fold op
613:             if p.get("boundary") is not None:
614:                 p["boundary"]["future_boundary_field"] = "y"  # inside a boundary
615:             if p.get("parse"):
616:                 p["parse"][0]["future_step_field"] = "z"  # inside a parse step
617:         if d.kind == DECL_SOURCE_DEFINED:
618:             p["future_source_field"] = "s"
619:         patched.append(Document(d.kind, d.subject, p))
620:     projected = documents_to_vertex(patched, path=ast.path, store=ast.store)
621:     assert projected == _ingress_stripped(ast)

857: # Helpers

860: 
861: def _vertex_kwargs(ast: VertexFile) -> dict:
862:     """Extract the constructor kwargs of a VertexFile (for rebuilding copies)."""
863:     return {
864:         "name": ast.name,
865:         "loops": ast.loops,
866:         "store": ast.store,
867:         "store_backend": ast.store_backend,
868:         "store_location": ast.store_location,
869:         "discover": ast.discover,
870:         "sources": ast.sources,
871:         "vertices": ast.vertices,
872:         "routes": ast.routes,
873:         "emit": ast.emit,
874:         "combine": ast.combine,
875:         "sources_blocks": ast.sources_blocks,
876:         "observers": ast.observers,
877:         "lens": ast.lens,
878:         "boundary": ast.boundary,
879:         "observer_scoped": ast.observer_scoped,
880:         "strict": ast.strict,
881:         "path": ast.path,
882:     }
883: 
884: 
885: def _edit(ast: VertexFile, **overrides: object) -> VertexFile:
886:     """A copy of ``ast`` with the given fields replaced (an in-memory edit)."""
887:     return VertexFile(**{**_vertex_kwargs(ast), **overrides})
888: 
889: 
890: def _residence_stripped(ast: VertexFile) -> VertexFile:
891:     """``ast`` with the store locator and the backend arm cleared.
892: 
893:     What :func:`_reproject` produces: it projects documents with no residence
894:     supplied, and residence is exactly what documents do not carry. ``path``
895:     is residence too but is not cleared here — every caller builds ``ast``
896:     with :func:`parse_vertex` on text, so it is already None and clearing it
897:     would state a transformation that never happens.
898: 
899:     Named rather than spelled inline at each assertion so the cleared set
900:     stays in one place: it grew from ``store`` alone to include
901:     ``store_backend``, and an assertion that cleared only some of it would
902:     pass while proving less.
903:     """
904:     return _edit(ast, store=None, store_backend=None, store_location=None)
905: 
906: 
907: def _ingress_stripped(ast: VertexFile) -> VertexFile:
908:     """``ast`` with ingress-class values blanked (env values, SPEC §9.5).
909: 
910:     Env VALUES are residence/ingress — excluded from declaration payloads and
911:     re-attached from the file at resolution (load_declaration). Projection
912:     therefore yields them as "": round-trip equality is asserted modulo this,
913:     exactly as it already is for ``path``/``store`` residence.
914:     """
915:     from lang.ast import InlineSource, SourcesBlock
916: 
917:     if not ast.sources_blocks:
918:         return ast
919: 
920:     def _strip(s: InlineSource) -> InlineSource:
921:         # ast.py's custom frozen decorator defeats dataclasses.replace —
922:         # rebuild through the constructor instead.
923:         return InlineSource(
924:             command=s.command, kind=s.kind, observer=s.observer, every=s.every,
925:             on=s.on, format=s.format, timeout=s.timeout, origin=s.origin,
926:             env=tuple((k, "") for k, _ in s.env), parse=s.parse, path=s.path,
927:         )
928: 
929:     blocks = tuple(
930:         SourcesBlock(mode=b.mode, sources=tuple(_strip(s) for s in b.sources))
931:         for b in ast.sources_blocks
932:     )
933:     return _edit(ast, sources_blocks=blocks)
934: 
935:

949: 
950: def _reproject(head_docs, changes) -> VertexFile:
951:     """Apply changes over a head document set and project back to an AST.
952: 
953:     Mirrors the store round-trip at the grammar tier: ``apply_changes`` folds
954:     the changes (overlay/tombstone) like the resolver, then ``documents_to_vertex``
955:     projects — so ``_reproject`` equals the edited file's AST (modulo residence).
956:     """
957:     return documents_to_vertex(apply_changes(head_docs, changes))
958:

960: @pytest.mark.parametrize("name", sorted(ALL_CASES))
961: def test_diff_apply_roundtrip_add_kind(name: str) -> None:
962:     """absorb(edit) then resolver ≡ parse(edited): adding a kind reconstructs B."""
963:     a = parse_vertex(ALL_CASES[name])
964:     b = _edit(a, loops={
965:         **a.loops,

1105: def test_apply_changes_accepts_mapping_form() -> None:
1106:     """apply_changes folds both Change tuples and plain row mappings (the store
1107:     persists rows as dicts, so the resolver-parity oracle must accept both)."""
1108:     head = [{"kind": DECL_KIND_DEFINED, "subject": "c", "payload": {"folds": [], "order": 0}}]
1109:     # dict-form changes: one modify, expressed as a row mapping.
1110:     modified = apply_changes(head, [
1111:         {"kind": DECL_KIND_DEFINED, "subject": "c",
1112:          "payload": {"folds": [{"target": "n", "op": {"op": "count"}}], "order": 0},
1113:          "change": "modified"},
1114:     ])
1115:     assert modified[0]["payload"]["folds"]  # the new definition replaced the old
1116:     # dict-form tombstone removes the subject.
1117:     removed = apply_changes(head, [
1118:         {"kind": DECL_KIND_RETIRED, "subject": "c", "change": "removed"},
1119:     ])
1120:     assert removed == []

=== libs/sdk/src/sdk/adopt.py ===
1: """Explicit adoption of a reviewed declaration into an Arrival history.
2: 
3: This is deliberately a narrow wrapper around the engine ceremony.  It does
4: not read migration sidecar inputs, mint keys, import legacy material, or infer
5: a reviewed declaration from the locator cache.  Callers bring the reviewed
6: snapshot, the published authority cache, and the selected, already-verified
7: Arrival head.
8: """
9: 
10: from __future__ import annotations
11: 
12: import hashlib
13: from collections.abc import Sequence
14: from pathlib import Path
15: from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Literal
16: 
17: from custody.signing import ARRIVAL_DOMAIN, FACT_DOMAIN
18: from engine.arrival_contract import Head, Profile
19: from engine.arrival_registry import BackendRegistry
20: from engine.credentials import CredentialProvider, WriteCredentials
21: 
22: from .types import (
23:     ArrivalAdoptionResult,
24:     SdkValueError,
25:     StoreDescriptorInfo,
26:     TargetUnsupported,
27: )
28: 
29: if TYPE_CHECKING:
30:     from engine.arrival_adoption import ArrivalAdoptionResult as EngineArrivalAdoptionResult
31:     from engine.arrival_maintenance import ProjectionSyncResult
32:     from engine.credentials import CredentialBindingEvidence
33: 
34: __all__ = ["adopt_arrival", "recover_arrival_adoption"]
35: 
36: 
37: def _mapped_adoption_credentials(
38:     vertex_path: Path,
39:     credentials: CredentialProvider | WriteCredentials | None,
40: ) -> WriteCredentials:
41:     """Resolve only an already-created mapped binding for the adoption author."""
42:     if credentials is None:
43:         raise SdkValueError("Arrival adoption requires a pre-created mapped credential binding")
44:     if isinstance(credentials, WriteCredentials):
45:         supplied = credentials
46:     else:
47:         provider = getattr(credentials, "for_write", None)
48:         if not callable(provider):
49:             raise SdkValueError("Arrival adoption requires a mapped credential provider")
50:         try:
51:             supplied = provider(vertex_path)
52:         except SdkValueError:
53:             raise
54:         except Exception as exc:
55:             raise SdkValueError(
56:                 "Arrival adoption could not resolve its mapped credential binding"
57:             ) from exc
58:     if not isinstance(supplied, WriteCredentials):
59:         raise SdkValueError("credential provider did not return WriteCredentials")
60:     if not supplied.mapped:
61:         raise SdkValueError("Arrival adoption requires a pre-created mapped credential binding")
62:     return supplied
63: 
64: 
65: def _domain_verifier(domain: str):
66:     """Verify a public signature in one explicit protocol domain."""
67:     from sign import ed25519
68: 
69:     def verify(key: str, signature: str, digest: str) -> bool:
70:         try:
71:             public = ed25519.public_key_from_b64(key)
72:         except ValueError:
73:             return False
74:         return ed25519.verify(public, signature, digest.encode(), domain=domain)
75: 
76:     return verify
77: 
78: 
79: def _head_dict(head: Head | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
80:     if head is None:
81:         return None
82:     return {
83:         "lineage": head.lineage,
84:         "ordinal": head.ordinal,
85:         "record_hash": head.record_hash,
86:     }
87: 
88: 
89: def _projection_dict(projection: ProjectionSyncResult | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
90:     if projection is None:
91:         return None
92:     return {
93:         "captured_head": _head_dict(projection.captured_head),
94:         "target": _head_dict(projection.target),
95:         "projected_before": _head_dict(projection.projected_before),
96:         "projected_after": _head_dict(projection.projected_after),
97:         "view_generation": projection.view_generation,
98:         "changed": projection.changed,
99:         "rebuilt": projection.rebuilt,
100:     }
101: 
102: 
103: def _binding_dicts(bindings: Sequence[CredentialBindingEvidence]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
104:     """Copy public mapped evidence without retaining provider-private state."""
105:     result: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
106:     for evidence in bindings:
107:         request = evidence.request
108:         result.append(
109:             {
110:                 "request": {
111:                     "namespace": request.namespace,
112:                     "observer": request.observer,
113:                     "domain": request.domain.value,
114:                     "purpose": request.purpose.value,
115:                 },
116:                 "key_ref": evidence.key_ref,
117:                 "algorithm": evidence.algorithm,
118:                 "public_key": evidence.public_key,
119:                 "provenance": evidence.provenance,
120:             }
121:         )
122:     return result

125: def _result(
126:     raw: EngineArrivalAdoptionResult,
127:     *,
128:     reviewed_sha256: str | None = None,
129:     declaration_sha256: str | None = None,
130: ) -> ArrivalAdoptionResult:
131:     """Project the engine outcome into the stable SDK result shape."""
132:     descriptor = raw.descriptor
133:     lineage = raw.lineage
134:     fact_id = getattr(raw, "fact_id", lineage)
135:     intent_path = raw.intent_path
136:     return ArrivalAdoptionResult(
137:         status=raw.status,
138:         target_path=str(raw.target_path),
139:         store=StoreDescriptorInfo.from_descriptor(descriptor),
140:         basis=raw.basis,
141:         lineage=lineage,
142:         captured_head=raw.captured_head,
143:         head=raw.head,
144:         commit=raw.commit,
145:         fact_id=fact_id,
146:         intent_path=None if intent_path is None else str(intent_path),
147:         phase=raw.phase,
148:         file_written=raw.file_written,
149:         reviewed_sha256=reviewed_sha256,
150:         declaration_sha256=declaration_sha256,
151:         projection=_projection_dict(raw.projection),
152:         credential_bindings=_binding_dicts(raw.credential_bindings),
153:         observed_head=raw.observed_head,
154:         runtime_epoch=raw.runtime_epoch,
155:     )

157: 
158: def adopt_arrival(
159:     target: Path | str,
160:     *,
161:     selected_head: Head,
162:     reviewed_text: str,
163:     reviewed_sha256: str,
164:     declaration_text: str,
165:     observer: str,
166:     credentials: CredentialProvider | WriteCredentials,
167:     runtime_epoch: Literal["strict", "fresh"] = "strict",
168:     registry: BackendRegistry | None = None,
169: ) -> ArrivalAdoptionResult:
170:     """Append one reviewed declaration anchor at an explicit migration head.
171: 
172:     ``reviewed_text`` and ``reviewed_sha256`` name the pre-migration snapshot
173:     the caller approved. ``declaration_text`` is the separately captured,
174:     currently published authority cache that will be anchored only after the
175:     engine proves their declaration meanings agree. The target must resolve to
176:     an authority descriptor and the mapped binding must already exist.
177:     """
178:     from .errors import normalize_exception
179:     from .target import _arrival_descriptor
180: 
181:     try:
182:         if runtime_epoch not in ("strict", "fresh"):
183:             raise SdkValueError("runtime_epoch must be 'strict' or 'fresh'")
184:         vertex_path = Path(target).resolve()
185:         resolved = _arrival_descriptor(vertex_path)
186:         if resolved is None:
187:             raise TargetUnsupported(
188:                 f"adopt_arrival requires an explicit Arrival .vertex target: {vertex_path}"
189:             )
190:         _path, _ast, descriptor = resolved
191:         if descriptor.role is not Profile.AUTHORITY:
192:             raise SdkValueError("Arrival adoption requires an authority descriptor")
193:         write_credentials = _mapped_adoption_credentials(vertex_path, credentials)
194:         active_registry = (
195:             registry if registry is not None else BackendRegistry.with_builtin_backends()
196:         )
197:         from engine.arrival_adoption import apply_arrival_adoption, prepare_arrival_adoption
198: 
199:         plan = prepare_arrival_adoption(
200:             active_registry,
201:             descriptor,
202:             target=vertex_path,
203:             selected_head=selected_head,
204:             reviewed_text=reviewed_text,
205:             reviewed_sha256=reviewed_sha256,
206:             declaration_text=declaration_text,
207:             observer=observer,
208:             credentials=write_credentials,
209:             fact_verify=_domain_verifier(FACT_DOMAIN),
210:             arrival_verify=_domain_verifier(ARRIVAL_DOMAIN),
211:             runtime_epoch=runtime_epoch,
212:         )
213:         raw = apply_arrival_adoption(active_registry, plan)
214:     except Exception as exc:
215:         normalized = normalize_exception(exc, context={"captured_head": selected_head})
216:         if normalized is exc:
217:             raise
218:         raise normalized from exc
219:     return _result(
220:         raw,
221:         reviewed_sha256=reviewed_sha256,
222:         declaration_sha256=hashlib.sha256(declaration_text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
223:     )
224: 
225: 
226: def recover_arrival_adoption(
227:     intent: Path | str,
228:     *,
229:     registry: BackendRegistry | None = None,
230: ) -> ArrivalAdoptionResult:
231:     """Recover a retained adoption intent without resolving or re-signing keys."""
232:     from engine.arrival_adoption import recover_arrival_adoption as recover
233: 
234:     from .errors import normalize_exception
235: 
236:     active_registry = registry if registry is not None else BackendRegistry.with_builtin_backends()
237:     try:
238:         raw = recover(
239:             active_registry,
240:             intent,
241:             fact_verify=_domain_verifier(FACT_DOMAIN),
242:             arrival_verify=_domain_verifier(ARRIVAL_DOMAIN),
243:         )
244:     except Exception as exc:
245:         normalized = normalize_exception(exc)
246:         if normalized is exc:
247:             raise
248:         raise normalized from exc
249:     return _result(raw)

2: 
3: This module deliberately owns no legacy reader or store path.  Every
4: descriptor occurrence is captured through ``engine.arrival_aggregate`` and
5: composition consumes only those retained snapshots plus frozen definitions.

39: def _loops_home() -> Path:
40:     if home := os.environ.get("LOOPS_HOME"):
41:         return Path(home)
42:     return Path(os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", str(Path.home() / ".config"))) / "loops"

54:     return tuple((step.relation, step.ordinal, step.label) for step in path)

76: class _Resolver:
77:     """Exact-byte local planner invoked from each frozen effective AST."""
78: 
79:     def _node(
80:         self, path: Path, occurrence: tuple[OccurrenceStep, ...], role: str = "member"
81:     ) -> AggregatePlanNode:
82:         resolved = path.resolve()
83:         try:
84:             raw = resolved.read_bytes()
85:         except OSError as exc:
86:             raise AggregateCaptureRefused(f"aggregate member is unavailable: {resolved}") from exc
87:         try:
88:             ast = parse_vertex(raw.decode("utf-8"), path=resolved)
89:         except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
90:             raise AggregateCaptureRefused(f"aggregate member is not UTF-8: {resolved}") from exc
91:         return AggregatePlanNode(
92:             path=occurrence,
93:             locator=resolved,
94:             local_ast=ast,
95:             definition=DefinitionEvidence(
96:                 locator=str(resolved),
97:                 sha256="sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
98:             ),
99:             descriptor=descriptor_for(ast, resolved),
100:             role=role,
101:         )
102: 
103:     def root(self, path: Path) -> AggregatePlanNode:
104:         return self._node(path, (), role="root")
105: 
106:     def children(
107:         self, node: AggregatePlanNode, effective_ast: Any
108:     ) -> tuple[AggregatePlanNode, ...]:
109:         if effective_ast.combine is not None:
110:             children: list[AggregatePlanNode] = []
111:             for ordinal, entry in enumerate(effective_ast.combine):
112:                 member = resolve_vertex(entry.name, _loops_home())
113:                 if not member.is_absolute():
114:                     member = node.locator.parent / member
115:                 if not member.exists():
116:                     raise AggregateCaptureRefused(
117:                         f"declared aggregate member is missing: {member.resolve()}"
118:                     )
119:                 children.append(
120:                     self._node(
121:                         member,
122:                         node.path
123:                         + (OccurrenceStep("combine", ordinal, entry.alias or entry.name),),
124:                     )
125:                 )
126:             return tuple(children)
127:         if effective_ast.discover is not None:
128:             return tuple(
129:                 self._node(
130:                     child,
131:                     node.path + (OccurrenceStep("discover", ordinal, child.name),),
132:                 )
133:                 for ordinal, child in enumerate(
134:                     sorted(node.locator.parent.glob(effective_ast.discover))
135:                 )
136:                 if child.suffix == ".vertex" and child.resolve() != node.locator.resolve()
137:             )
138:         return ()
