385: def run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, Any]:
386:     root = Path(args.sandbox).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)
387:     if not root.is_dir():
388:         raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused("sandbox must be an existing directory")
389:     if any((parent / ".git").exists() for parent in (root, *root.parents)):
390:         raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused(
391:             "sandbox must be outside every repository checkout"
392:         )
393:     evidence_path = _inside(root, Path(args.evidence), "evidence", exists=True)
394:     output = _inside(root, Path(args.output), "recovery output", exists=False)
395:     if output.exists() or any(
396:         output in item.parents or item in output.parents for item in (evidence_path,)
397:     ):
398:         raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused(
399:             "recovery output must be a fresh sandbox directory"
400:         )
401:     evidence, source_log, source_vertex, reviewed_path, selected = _load_evidence(
402:         root, evidence_path
403:     )
404:     credentials = _inside(
405:         root,
406:         Path(str(evidence["output"])) / "credentials",
407:         "mapped credentials",
408:         exists=True,
409:     )
410:     adoption = evidence.get("adoption")
411:     if not isinstance(adoption, dict) or not isinstance(
412:         evidence.get("migration"), dict
413:     ):
414:         raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused("evidence lacks adoption metadata")
415:     observer = args.observer
416:     if not isinstance(observer, str) or not observer:
417:         raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused("observer must be explicit")
418:     namespace = args.namespace
419:     runtime_epoch = adoption.get("runtime_epoch", "strict")
420:     if runtime_epoch not in ("strict", "fresh"):
421:         raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused("adoption runtime epoch is malformed")
422:     prefix_size = evidence["migration"]["prefix_byte_count"]
423:     prefix_hash = evidence["migration"]["prefix_sha256"]
424:     assert isinstance(prefix_size, int) and isinstance(prefix_hash, str)
425:     output.mkdir(mode=0o700)
426:     results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
427:     for phase in ("after-intent", "after-append"):
428:         fork = output / phase
429:         vertex, log, fork_credentials = _fork_prefix(
430:             source_log=source_log,
431:             prefix_size=prefix_size,
432:             prefix_hash=prefix_hash,
433:             source_vertex=source_vertex,
434:             reviewed_path=reviewed_path,
435:             selected=selected,
436:             credentials=credentials,
437:             fork=fork,
438:         )
439:         print(
440:             f"[arrival-recovery] {phase}: synchronizing fork at S",
441:             file=sys.stderr,
442:             flush=True,
443:         )
444:         os.environ.update(_runtime_env(fork))
445:         from sdk import SdkError, read_summary, sync_target
446: 
447:         synced = sync_target(vertex)
448:         if synced.projected_after != _head_value(selected):
449:             raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused("fork projection did not synchronize at S")
450: 
451:         try:
452:             read_summary(vertex)
453:         except SdkError as exc:
454:             if type(exc) is not SdkError or "no adopted declaration" not in str(exc):
455:                 raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused(
456:                     "pre-adoption read did not refuse for the missing declaration anchor"
457:                 ) from exc
458:             preadoption_error = type(exc).__name__
459:         else:
460:             raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused(
461:                 "read_summary unexpectedly accepted unadopted S"
462:             )
463:         before = log.read_bytes()
464:         print(
465:             f"[arrival-recovery] {phase}: stopping child at {phase}",
466:             file=sys.stderr,
467:             flush=True,
468:         )
469:         child = _child_adopt(
470:             vertex,
471:             fork_credentials,
472:             namespace,
473:             fork / "reviewed.vertex",
474:             selected,
475:             observer,
476:             phase,
477:             runtime_epoch,
478:             _runtime_env(fork),
479:         )
480:         if child.returncode != EXIT_DURABLE_STOP:
481:             raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused(
482:                 f"{phase} child did not stop at durable boundary: {child.stderr}"
483:             )
484:         intent = _intent_path(vertex)
485:         if not intent.is_file() or _sha256(log, limit=prefix_size) != prefix_hash:
486:             raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused(
487:                 "durable stop changed the selected S prefix or omitted intent"
488:             )
489:         reserved = json.loads(intent.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["drafts"][0]
490:         _reserved_anchor(log, selected, reserved, required=phase == "after-append")
491:         offline = fork / "credentials-offline"
492:         fork_credentials.rename(offline)
493:         print(
494:             f"[arrival-recovery] {phase}: recovering without credentials",
495:             file=sys.stderr,
496:             flush=True,
497:         )
498:         recovered = _child_recover(intent, _runtime_env(fork))
499:         if recovered.returncode != 0:
500:             raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused(
501:                 f"{phase} public recovery failed: {recovered.stderr}{recovered.stdout}"
502:             )
503:         result = json.loads(recovered.stdout)
504:         head = _head(result.get("head"), "recovery head")
505:         if (
506:             result.get("captured_head") != selected
507:             or result.get("commit_before") != selected
508:             or result.get("commit_after") != head
509:             or result.get("summary_head") != head
510:             or result.get("runtime_epoch") != runtime_epoch
511:         ):
512:             raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused(
513:                 "recovery did not report Commit(S,A) and a current summary"
514:             )
515:         final = log.read_bytes()
516:         if (
517:             not final.startswith(before)
518:             or _sha256(log, limit=prefix_size) != prefix_hash
519:         ):
520:             raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused("recovery changed pre-existing fork bytes")
521:         _reserved_anchor(log, selected, reserved, required=True)
522:         second = _child_recover(intent, _runtime_env(fork))
523:         if second.returncode != 3 or log.read_bytes() != final:
524:             raise RecoveryRehearsalRefused(
525:                 "second recovery did not refuse without changing bytes"
526:             )
527:         results.append(
528:             {
529:                 "phase": phase,
530:                 "pre_adoption_error": preadoption_error,
531:                 "selected_head": selected,
532:                 "head": head,
533:                 "prefix_sha256": prefix_hash,
534:                 "runtime_epoch": runtime_epoch,
535:                 "second_recovery_error": json.loads(second.stdout)["error"],
536:             }
537:         )
538:     result = {
539:         "schema": "loops.rehearsal/arrival-recovery/v1",
540:         "status": "complete",
541:         "forks": results,
542:     }
543:     (output / "recovery-evidence.json").write_text(
544:         json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n",
545:         encoding="utf-8",
546:     )
547:     return result
548: 
549: 
550: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
551:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
552:     parser.add_argument("--sandbox", type=Path)
553:     parser.add_argument("--evidence", type=Path)
554:     parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
555:     parser.add_argument("--observer")
556:     parser.add_argument("--namespace", default="arrival-rehearsal")
557:     parser.add_argument(
558:         "--child-adopt",
559:         nargs=8,
560:         metavar=(
561:             "VERTEX",
562:             "ROOT",
563:             "NAMESPACE",
564:             "REVIEWED",
565:             "HEAD",
566:             "OBSERVER",
567:             "PHASE",
568:             "RUNTIME_EPOCH",
569:         ),
570:     )
571:     parser.add_argument("--child-recover", metavar="INTENT")
572:     args = parser.parse_args(argv)
573:     if args.child_adopt is not None:
574:         return _child_adopt_main(args.child_adopt)
575:     if args.child_recover is not None:
576:         return _child_recover_main(args.child_recover)
577:     try:
578:         result = run(args)
579:     except (RecoveryRehearsalRefused, OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
580:         print(f"refused: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
581:         return 2
582:     print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
583:     return 0
584: 
585: 
586: if __name__ == "__main__":
587:     raise SystemExit(main())

148: class _StaticCredentials:
149:     def __init__(self, pair) -> None:
150:         self.pair = pair
151: 
152:     def for_write(self, _vertex: Path) -> WriteCredentials:
153:         return WriteCredentials(
154:             fact_signer=lambda _observer, digest: ed25519.sign(
155:                 self.pair, digest.encode(), domain=FACT_DOMAIN
156:             ),
157:             arrival_signer=lambda _observer, digest: ed25519.sign(
158:                 self.pair, digest.encode(), domain=ARRIVAL_DOMAIN
159:             ),
160:         )

165:         pair, digest.encode(), domain=ARRIVAL_DOMAIN
166:     )

168: 
169: def _verifier(key: str, signature: str, digest: str) -> bool:
170:     try:
171:         public = ed25519.public_key_from_b64(key)
172:     except ValueError:
173:         return False
174:     return ed25519.verify(public, signature, digest.encode(), domain=ARRIVAL_DOMAIN)

224: def _write_sqlite(path: Path) -> None:
225:     with sqlite3.connect(path) as conn:

402: @pytest.mark.parametrize("source_format", ["jsonl", "sqlite"])
403: def test_copied_migration_adoption_and_mapped_write(
404:     tmp_path: Path, source_format: str
405: ) -> None:
406:     """Rehearse the explicit source-copy -> migration -> adoption boundary.
407: 
408:     All originals here are synthetic. SQLite is copied through its backup API;
409:     the quiescent JSONL fixture is copied byte-for-byte. Report verification is
410:     deliberately performed at S, before adoption advances the ledger.
411:     """
412:     from sdk import MappedCredentialProvider, adopt_arrival, export_target, read_state
413: 
414:     original = tmp_path / "original"
415:     (original / "data").mkdir(parents=True)
416:     source = original / "data" / f"legacy.{source_format}"
417:     (_write_jsonl if source_format == "jsonl" else _write_sqlite)(source)
418:     provider = MappedCredentialProvider(
419:         tmp_path / "rehearsal-credentials",
420:         namespace="adoption-rehearsal",
421:         receipt_observer="alice",
422:     )
423:     binding = provider.create_binding("alice", token="rehearsal-alice")
424:     original_vertex = original / "alice.vertex"
425:     _write_vertex(original_vertex, binding.public_key, source.name)
426:     original_bytes = source.read_bytes()
427:     reviewed_bytes = original_vertex.read_bytes()
428:     reviewed_hash = hashlib.sha256(reviewed_bytes).hexdigest()
429: 
430:     rehearsal = tmp_path / "rehearsal"
431:     (rehearsal / "data").mkdir(parents=True)
432:     copied_source = rehearsal / "data" / source.name
433:     if source_format == "sqlite":
434:         with sqlite3.connect(source) as src, sqlite3.connect(copied_source) as dst:
435:             src.backup(dst)
436:     else:
437:         shutil.copyfile(source, copied_source)
438:     vertex = rehearsal / "alice.vertex"
439:     vertex.write_bytes(reviewed_bytes)
440:     copied_bytes = copied_source.read_bytes()
441:     registry_binding = provider.resolve(CredentialRequest(
442:         provider.namespace, "alice", SigningDomain.ARRIVAL,
443:         CredentialPurpose.INITIALIZATION,
444:     ))
445:     assert registry_binding is not None
446: 
447:     def migration_signer(observer: str, digest: str) -> str:
448:         assert observer == "alice"
449:         return registry_binding.sign_digest(digest)
450: 
451:     migrated = run_migration(
452:         copied_source, vertex, store_dir=rehearsal / "data", signer=migration_signer,
453:     )
454:     assert verify_migration_report(
455:         migrated.report_path, binding.public_key, verify=_verifier,
456:         target_path=migrated.target_path,
457:     )
458:     report_bytes = migrated.report_path.read_bytes()
459:     # External provenance stays outside the declaration's protocol payload.
460:     evidence = {
461:         "reviewed_sha256": reviewed_hash,
462:         "report_sha256": hashlib.sha256(report_bytes).hexdigest(),
463:         "report_verified_at": migrated.head.record_hash,
464:     }
465:     prefix = migrated.target_path.read_bytes()
466:     descriptor = resolve_arrival_target(vertex).store
467:     published_text = vertex.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
468:     sync_target(vertex)
469:     with pytest.raises(SdkError, match="adopted declaration|historized"):
470:         read_summary(vertex)
471: 
472:     # A caller cannot silently pass revised bytes under the reviewed hash.
473:     with pytest.raises(SdkError):
474:         adopt_arrival(
475:             vertex, selected_head=migrated.head,
476:             reviewed_text=reviewed_bytes.decode() + "\n// unreviewed\n",
477:             reviewed_sha256=reviewed_hash, declaration_text=published_text,
478:             observer="alice", credentials=provider,
479:         )
480:     assert migrated.target_path.read_bytes() == prefix
481: 
482:     adopted = adopt_arrival(
483:         vertex, selected_head=migrated.head, reviewed_text=reviewed_bytes.decode(),
484:         reviewed_sha256=reviewed_hash, declaration_text=published_text,
485:         observer="alice", credentials=provider,
486:     )
487:     assert adopted.commit is not None
488:     assert adopted.commit.before == migrated.head
489:     assert adopted.head == adopted.commit.after
490:     assert adopted.head.ordinal == migrated.head.ordinal + 1
491:     assert adopted.fact_id == migrated.lineage
492:     assert resolve_arrival_target(vertex).store == descriptor
493:     after_adoption = migrated.target_path.read_bytes()
494:     assert after_adoption.startswith(prefix)
495:     assert len(after_adoption.splitlines()) == len(prefix.splitlines()) + 1
496:     assert migrated.report_path.read_bytes() == report_bytes
497:     assert hashlib.sha256(report_bytes).hexdigest() == evidence["report_sha256"]
498: 
499:     for result in (
500:         inspect_declaration(vertex), read_summary(vertex), read_facts(vertex),
501:         read_ticks(vertex), read_state(vertex),
502:     ):
503:         assert result.basis is not None
504:         assert result.basis.captured_head == adopted.head
505:         json.dumps(result.as_dict(), allow_nan=False)
506:     facts = read_facts(vertex, include_internal=True, order="oldest", limit=100)
507:     anchors = [row for row in facts.items if row["kind"] == "_decl.genesis"]
508:     assert len(anchors) == 1 and anchors[0]["id"] == migrated.lineage
509:     original_fact = read_fact_by_id(vertex, "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FA0")
510:     assert original_fact.fact is not None
511: 
512:     receipt = emit_fact(
513:         vertex, "concept", {"text": "after adoption"}, observer="alice",
514:         id_override="adoption-rehearsal-followup", credentials=provider,
515:     )
516:     assert receipt.stored and receipt.signed and receipt.witnessed
517:     assert receipt.commit is not None and receipt.commit.before == adopted.head
518:     final = verify_target(vertex)
519:     assert final.verified_through == receipt.commit.after
520:     exported = rehearsal / "captured.jsonl"
521:     export = export_target(vertex, exported)
522:     assert export.head == receipt.commit.after
523:     assert exported.read_bytes() == migrated.target_path.read_bytes()
524:     for result in (adopted, receipt, final, export):
525:         json.dumps(result.as_dict(), allow_nan=False)
526:     assert source.read_bytes() == original_bytes
527:     assert original_vertex.read_bytes() == reviewed_bytes
528:     assert copied_source.read_bytes() == copied_bytes

531: @pytest.mark.parametrize("stop_phase", ["after-intent", "after-append"])
532: @pytest.mark.parametrize("runtime_epoch", ["strict", "fresh"])
533: def test_adoption_process_exit_recovers_reserved_draft_without_credentials(
534:     tmp_path: Path, stop_phase: str, runtime_epoch: str, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
535: ) -> None:
536:     """Exit a real child process at a durable boundary, then reconcile once."""
537:     from sdk import MappedCredentialProvider, recover_arrival_adoption
538: 
539:     data = tmp_path / "data"
540:     data.mkdir()
541:     source = data / "legacy.jsonl"
542:     _write_jsonl(source)
543:     provider = MappedCredentialProvider(
544:         tmp_path / "credentials", namespace="interrupted-adoption", receipt_observer="alice",
545:     )
546:     created = provider.create_binding("alice", token="create-alice")
547:     vertex = tmp_path / "alice.vertex"
548:     _write_vertex(vertex, created.public_key, source.name)
549:     reviewed = vertex.read_text()
550:     signed = provider.resolve(CredentialRequest(
551:         provider.namespace, "alice", SigningDomain.ARRIVAL, CredentialPurpose.INITIALIZATION,
552:     ))
553:     assert signed is not None
554:     migrated = run_migration(
555:         source, vertex, store_dir=data, signer=lambda _observer, digest: signed.sign_digest(digest),
556:     )
557:     prefix = migrated.target_path.read_bytes()
558:     script = r'''
559: import hashlib, json, os, sys
560: from pathlib import Path
561: import engine.arrival_adoption as engine_adoption
562: from engine.arrival_contract import Head
563: from sdk import MappedCredentialProvider, adopt_arrival
564: target, root, namespace, reviewed, head_json, stop, runtime_epoch = sys.argv[1:]
565: original_apply = engine_adoption.apply_arrival_adoption
566: def stop_at(phase):
567:     if phase == stop:
568:         os._exit(86)
569: def interrupted(registry, plan):
570:     return original_apply(registry, plan, failure_hook=stop_at)
571: engine_adoption.apply_arrival_adoption = interrupted
572: provider = MappedCredentialProvider(Path(root), namespace=namespace, receipt_observer="alice")
573: adopt_arrival(
574:     target, selected_head=Head(**json.loads(head_json)), reviewed_text=reviewed,
575:     reviewed_sha256=hashlib.sha256(reviewed.encode()).hexdigest(),
576:     declaration_text=Path(target).read_text(), observer="alice", credentials=provider,
577:     runtime_epoch=runtime_epoch,
578: )
579: raise AssertionError("durable stop phase was not reached")
580: '''
581:     run = subprocess.run(
582:         [sys.executable, "-c", script, str(vertex), str(provider.root), provider.namespace,
583:          reviewed, json.dumps({"lineage": migrated.head.lineage,
584:                                "ordinal": migrated.head.ordinal,
585:                                "record_hash": migrated.head.record_hash}), stop_phase, runtime_epoch],
586:         capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30, check=False,
587:     )
588:     assert run.returncode == 86, run.stderr
589:     intent = vertex.with_name(vertex.name + ".arrival-adopt.intent")
590:     assert intent.exists()
591:     reserved = json.loads(intent.read_text())["drafts"][0]
592:     before_recovery = migrated.target_path.read_bytes()
593:     expected_extra = 1 if stop_phase == "after-append" else 0
594:     assert len(before_recovery.splitlines()) == len(prefix.splitlines()) + expected_extra
595: 
596:     # Recovery cannot depend on the original private-key location or provider.
597:     provider.root.rename(tmp_path / "credentials-offline")
598:     def refuse_credentials(*_args, **_kwargs):
599:         raise AssertionError("recovery resolved signing credentials")
600:     monkeypatch.setattr(MappedCredentialProvider, "for_write", refuse_credentials)
601:     monkeypatch.setattr(MappedCredentialProvider, "resolve", refuse_credentials)
602:     authentic_intent = intent.read_bytes()
603:     mutations = ["binding", "inner-signature", "outer-signature"]
604:     if runtime_epoch == "fresh":
605:         mutations.append("epoch-downgrade")
606:     for mutation in mutations:
607:         changed = json.loads(authentic_intent)
608:         if mutation == "binding":
609:             changed["bindings"][0]["public_key"] = "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA="
610:         elif mutation == "inner-signature":
611:             changed["drafts"][0]["body"]["signature"] = "bogus"
612:         elif mutation == "epoch-downgrade":
613:             payload = json.loads(changed["drafts"][0]["body"]["payload"])
614:             payload["protocol"] = 1
615:             payload.pop("runtime_epoch")
616:             changed["drafts"][0]["body"]["payload"] = json.dumps(
617:                 payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
618:             )
619:         else:
620:             changed["drafts"][0]["signature"] = "bogus"
621:         # Keep the duplicate draft representations consistent: consistency
622:         # alone must not stand in for signature and captured-key verification.
623:         changed["exact_drafts"] = json.dumps(
624:             changed["drafts"], ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
625:         )
626:         intent.write_text(json.dumps(changed))
627:         with pytest.raises(SdkError):
628:             recover_arrival_adoption(intent)
629:         assert migrated.target_path.read_bytes() == before_recovery
630:         assert intent.exists()
631:     intent.write_bytes(authentic_intent)
632:     recovered = recover_arrival_adoption(intent)
633:     assert recovered.runtime_epoch == runtime_epoch
634:     assert recovered.head is not None
635:     assert recovered.head.ordinal == migrated.head.ordinal + 1
636:     assert recovered.captured_head == migrated.head
637:     assert recovered.commit is not None
638:     assert recovered.commit.before == migrated.head
639:     assert recovered.commit.after == recovered.head
640:     final = migrated.target_path.read_bytes()
641:     assert final.startswith(prefix)
642:     assert len(final.splitlines()) == len(prefix.splitlines()) + 1
643:     record = json.loads(final.splitlines()[-1])
644:     assert record["body"] == reserved["body"]
645:     assert record["sig"] == reserved["signature"]
646:     assert not intent.exists()
647:     assert read_summary(vertex).basis.captured_head == recovered.head
648:     with pytest.raises(SdkError):
649:         recover_arrival_adoption(intent)
650:     assert migrated.target_path.read_bytes() == final

710: def test_adoption_verifies_actual_binding_when_observer_has_two_valid_keys(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
711:     from engine.admission import fact_commitment_hash
712:     from engine.arrival import content_commitment
713:     from engine.arrival_contract import RecordDraft
714:     from sdk import MappedCredentialProvider, adopt_arrival
715: 
716:     provider, original, vertex, reviewed, migration = _mapped_migration_fixture(tmp_path)
717:     selected = MappedCredentialProvider(
718:         tmp_path / "second-credentials", namespace="selected-key", receipt_observer="alice",
719:     )
720:     second = selected.create_binding("alice", token="create-second-key")
721:     signer = provider.resolve(CredentialRequest(
722:         provider.namespace, "alice", SigningDomain.ARRIVAL, CredentialPurpose.KEY_INTRODUCTION,
723:     ))
724:     assert signer is not None
725:     body = {"observer": "alice", "key": second.public_key}
726:     digest = content_commitment("key", 1002.0, "alice", "", body)
727:     registry = BackendRegistry.with_builtin_backends()
728:     descriptor = descriptor_for(parse_vertex_file(vertex), vertex)
729:     assert descriptor is not None
730:     ledger, query = registry.open(descriptor)
731:     try:
732:         introduction = ledger.append(migration.head, (
733:             RecordDraft("key", 1002.0, "alice", "", body, signer.sign_digest(digest)),
734:         ))
735:     finally:
736:         query.close()
737:         ledger.close()
738:     result = adopt_arrival(
739:         vertex, selected_head=introduction.after, reviewed_text=reviewed,
740:         reviewed_sha256=hashlib.sha256(reviewed.encode()).hexdigest(),
741:         declaration_text=vertex.read_text(), observer="alice", credentials=selected,
742:     )
743:     assert result.commit is not None and result.commit.before == introduction.after
744:     record = result.commit.records[0]
745:     fact = record["body"]
746:     inner = fact_commitment_hash(

=== docs/scratch/arrival-break/adoption-fresh-runtime-epoch-design-2026-09-18.md ===
1: # Explicit fresh runtime epoch at adoption
2: 
3: ## Decision and scope
4: 
5: The real loops-store rehearsal (`2a75980c`) preserved 121 old ticks, including
6: owned vertex-period ticks before the new declaration anchor. C6 correctly
7: refuses consuming those ticks without proven declaration continuity. The user
8: selected “Start a new boundary epoch at adoption; define its initial state.”
9: This design adds an explicit opt-in execution cutover. It does not invent
10: historical declarations or reinterpret old ticks as proven boundary events.
11: 
12: ## Initial state
13: 
14: Let S be the reviewed migrated head and A the own declaration anchor appended
15: at S+1. For a fresh epoch:
16: 
17: - Each runtime fold starts at its declared identity/initial value. No old fact
18:   seeds its mutable execution state. Static declarations and pinned source
19:   configuration still apply.
20: - Boundary counters start at zero; one-shot boundaries are not exhausted;
21:   there are no pending old boundaries, old loop resets, or old vertex-period
22:   timestamps. The normal first post-A event starts period context.
23: - Runtime replay consumes only facts/ticks whose physical Arrival ordinal is
24:   strictly greater than A. A backdated post-A event remains in this epoch;
25:   wall-clock/event timestamps never select the execution floor.
26: - Post-A declarations and ticks retain all existing C6 continuity/refusal
27:   checks. A fresh marker is not permission to ignore later corruption, name
28:   reuse, unknown generated roles, or declaration discontinuities.
29: 
30: ## Execution state versus custody evidence
31: 
32: Filtering applies to runtime hydration, count/reset/period interpretation,
33: source cadence and pending work, and the public current `read_state` view.
34: Aggregate current state applies each member's own floor independently.
35: 
36: Filtering does **not** apply to source preservation, raw fact/tick queries,
37: summary counts, Full verification, exact export, or global ID/idempotency checks.
38: An old ID cannot be reused merely because it predates the epoch.
39: 
40: The physical tick chain also remains global: `prev_hash`, fact cursors, and
41: window hashes continue the custody chain across A, using all required historical
42: rows. An old tick can remain the cryptographic predecessor without becoming
43: a runtime reset/count/period edge. Resetting that chain would be a different
44: wire/audit change and is excluded.
45: 
46: ## Signed representation and compatibility
47: 
48: SDK adoption receives `runtime_epoch="strict" | "fresh"`, default `strict`.
49: Strict emits the current protocol-1 genesis without an epoch marker and keeps
50: the current behavior. Initialization continues to emit protocol 1.
51: 
52: Fresh emits declaration protocol 2 with the exact payload marker
53: `"runtime_epoch": "fresh-after-anchor-v1"` alongside the reviewed documents.
54: The existing FACT and ARRIVAL signatures cover this payload. Protocol 2 is
55: required so protocol-1 readers refuse instead of silently replaying old state.
56: The physical Arrival wire grammar is unchanged.
57: 
58: Central payload validation accepts the supported combinations only: v1 has no
59: epoch marker; v2 requires the exact marker. Unsupported/malformed combinations
60: refuse. No declaration edit can invent or move this immutable genesis floor.
61: The own store-local anchor must match physical lineage, fact identity/kind and
62: its actual receipt ordinal; foreign merged genesis facts cannot select a floor.
63: No mutable locator flag or free-standing projection metadata grants this mode.
64: At runtime the projected anchor is compared with the exact physical anchor from
65: the attested custody read, including its payload and signatures; both inventing
66: and stripping the marker in the projection refuse. This is not a new claim to
67: independently reverify every historical signature on every read. The supported
68: SDK prepare/recovery paths independently verify both domains before publishing
69: the anchor; deliberately false low-level injected verifiers/raw ledger writes
70: remain the existing trusted low-level API boundary.
71: 
72: Recovery takes no caller-supplied epoch override. It derives the reserved mode
73: from the authenticated exact draft, reconstructs the same canonical payload,
74: and independently verifies both signature domains. Marker tampering cannot
75: change the epoch while retaining authentic signatures. Results expose the mode
76: and anchor; `head` and Commit(S,A) retain their existing meanings.
77: 
78: ## Rehearsal and acceptance
79: 
80: Keep the strict rehearsal and its refusal evidence unchanged. Run a fresh
81: rehearsal on a separate copied descriptor and output, using the same audited
82: prepared source. Preserve the original and prepared source hashes.
83: 
84: Required coverage:
85: 
86: 1. Default strict mode still refuses consumed pre-genesis owned ticks.
87: 2. Fresh mode starts empty/declared state at A while historical query counts
88:    and exact export retain all old rows and signatures.
89: 3. Ordinary signed writes and a new boundary tick succeed; current state sees
90:    post-A facts only, including backdated arrivals.
91: 4. Tick-chain audit remains valid across the execution epoch; global duplicate
92:    detection still sees pre-A IDs.
93: 5. Post-A reset/count/period behavior, declaration continuity, source cadence,
94:    and aggregate state follow the same floor without weakening later checks.
95: 6. Malformed/foreign epoch evidence refuses; protocol-1 readers reject the
96:    fresh payload; default initialization and old anchors are unchanged.
97: 7. Both interruption boundaries recover the same signed epoch and exact anchor
98:    without credentials, including refusal of self-consistent tampered markers.
99: 8. Rerun the real loops copy through reads, writes, exact export and recovery.
100: 
101: Sol owns engine/lang implementation; Terra owns SDK/state/rehearsal integration;
102: Luna provides adversarial review; root owns integration acceptance and evidence.

=== docs/scratch/arrival-break/consistency-c6-boundary-design-2026-09-06.md ===
1: # C6 — boundary continuity design
2: 
3: Status: accepted by root after two Fable 5.1 **high** design reviews and
4: source/test-backed triage. Implementation is now authorized within this design.
5: The follow-up raw verdict remains REVISE; its sole new blocker was disproved
6: by the existing params-pin gate. See the retained review triage.
7: Baseline `ef8b21b2` on `arrival/finish` includes
8: the accepted C3 continuation checkpoint. This document is the proposed decision,
9: not a claim that current runtime already enforces it. Sol audits engine history
10: and replay, Terra SDK operations, Luna independent failure cases, and root owns
11: the policy and review triage.
12: 
13: ## Decision and scope
14: 
15: A continuing boundary keeps its recorded consumption history. An ordinary
16: declaration edit changes the current interpretation of facts; it does not
17: restart that boundary. The proposed identity for this supported subset remains
18: the exact local vertex name, boundary role, and boundary name. No declaration
19: hash, file path, projection generation, or new wire identifier becomes identity.
20: 
21: The recommended policy is **inherit for in-place edits**. A trigger/count,
22: condition, fold, parse, route, or dispatch edit keeps the existing tick edge.
23: This is an explicit interpretation policy, not a claim that the old tick would
24: have fired under the new rules. A pending fact already consumed by that edge
25: does not become eligible again just because a declaration changed.
26: 
27: Whole-loop retirement followed by same-name recreation needs separate evidence
28: when an old local tick exists. A tick whose loop/vertex role was ambiguous when
29: received also cannot become unambiguous through a later configuration edit.
30: Those cases refuse runtime when the target consumes that ambiguous stream.
31: Removing the consumer is allowed; reintroducing it re-exposes the same conflict.
32: Facts, ticks, and declarations
33: remain available as evidence; no prior row is changed or relabeled.
34: 
35: The user has been offered a choice between inherited in-place trigger/count
36: edits and a stricter interim refusal of those edits. No answer has arrived as
37: this draft is prepared for review; root proceeds with the recommended inherit
38: policy as a stated assumption. Any later answer and the adversarial design
39: review must be reconciled before implementation. Credential requests and persisted bindings (D0/D2), explicit
40: same-name restart/carry ceremonies, and durable vertex IDs are separate work.
41: 
42: ## What the implementation actually does today
43: 
44: `Vertex.hydrate_snapshot` re-folds captured facts under the current declaration
45: in receipt order. It does **not** deserialize an old tick payload as current
46: fold state. A local loop tick invokes `Loop.replay_boundary`: reset to the
47: current initial state when reset is enabled, clear repeating-count bookkeeping,
48: or mark a one-shot boundary exhausted. A local vertex tick restores the vertex
49: period timestamp and does not reset every loop.
50: 
51: `plan_pending_boundaries` selects the greatest event-time/receipt edge per local
52: tick name. Facts at an equal timestamp precede or follow that edge by receipt
53: coordinate. This remains distinct from the tick's fact cursor and from
54: declaration receipt ordering. Count boundaries remain ingress-driven.
55: 
56: The grammar currently exposes `when`, `after`, and `every`; its compiler always
57: sets loop-boundary `reset=True`. The lower-level `Loop` supports carry, but
58: there is no public declaration reset/carry edit to implement in C6. Fold
59: overrides replace initial state and fold code, not declared boundary reset.
60: 
61: Consequently an in-place count edit retains the recorded boundary and replays
62: facts after it. The exact existing count-recovery behavior is:
63: 
64: | Target mode and retained evidence | Hydrated state and next behavior |
65: | --- | --- |
66: | `every M`, with an owned tick and K subsequently routed facts | Count is K, including when K >= M. Hydration does not fire. If K >= M, the next accepted routed ingress fires; otherwise M-K more routed facts are needed. |
67: | `every M`, with no owned tick and K replayed facts | Existing recovery sets count to K modulo M. It creates no missing historical ticks. |
68: | `after M`, with any owned loop tick | Inherits an exhausted one-shot boundary. New ingress does not restart it. |
69: | `after M`, with no owned tick and K replayed facts | Exhausted when K >= M; otherwise count is K. A fresh name can therefore already be exhausted by older facts. |
70: | `after` changed in place to `every M`, with an old owned tick | Current repeating mode resumes from that retained tick and subsequent routed facts, not from the declaration edit. |
71: | Kind-trigger edit with an owned tick | Pending evaluation retains the old event-time/receipt edge; only unconsumed facts are checked against the new trigger/conditions. |
72: 
73: A user wanting a fresh count or first firing is requesting a restart; C6 does
74: not silently provide one. Historical payloads keep their original meaning and
75: bytes even when current replay differs. Count-return values ignored during
76: hydration must not turn into retrospective dispatch or appended ticks.
77: 
78: Sources: `libs/engine/src/engine/vertex.py:784`, `:1260`;
79: `libs/engine/src/engine/loop.py:157`;
80: `libs/engine/src/engine/compiler.py:541`, `:890`;
81: `libs/lang/src/lang/document.py:463`, `:1100`.
82: 
83: ## Contract matrix
84: 
85: | Situation at the bounded head | Supported result |
86: | --- | --- |
87: | Same continuously present loop, unchanged declaration | Inherit its recorded reset/count/period and pending consumption evidence. |
88: | Same continuously present loop, edited fold/parse/routes/trigger/count/conditions/run or presentation | Inherit the same edge and replay under the new interpretation; no implicit restart. |
89: | No local ticks for a loop; edit, remove/recreate, or introduce a boundary | Allowed, subject to existing checks. Older facts may replay and pending triggers may become eligible; this is not a fresh-facts cutoff. |
90: | Remove a loop that has old ticks | Allowed when it is absent from the proposed runtime. Preserve old ticks as evidence. |
91: | Reintroduce that retired runtime name after it had a local tick | Refuse ordinary declaration preparation/preview and runtime capture. A final-document comparison alone cannot detect this. |
92: | Add a genuinely unused loop name | Allowed. It has a distinct future tick identity, but may still consume older facts selected by current routing. This is not state carry or an explicit restart. |
93: | Vertex boundary list edited in place | Inherit the vertex-name edge. Declaration order remains meaningful; no new vertex identity. |
94: | Historical tick had `origin == name == vertex` while that loop also existed | Refuse when the target has a vertex boundary. A corrected target without that consumer may run, but adding a vertex boundary later refuses. The old row remains ambiguous. |
95: | Historical collision existed but produced no ambiguous local tick | Permit a collision-free append-forward correction. Preserve C5's existing accepted case. |
96: | Foreign or originless tick | Keep as evidence; it does not establish a local edge or a local incarnation conflict. Equal labels in another lineage prove no identity. |
97: | Owned tick predates the own declaration genesis | Refuse if the target consumes its loop name or vertex period: no recorded declaration establishes its role. Removing that consumer can avoid the conflict; a new name is not a historical alias. |
98: | Tick could belong to a generated name whose historical expansion is not recorded | Refuse the affected runtime interpretation as unprovable; current files/environment cannot provide historical evidence. |
99: | Explicit restart, state carry, alias, or same-name incarnation cutover | Deferred new protocol behavior; not inferred from an ordinary edit, projection rebuild, or locator move. |
100: 
101: Removing an explicit `cite` declaration still leaves the implicit runtime
102: `cite` loop. That is an in-place interpretation change, not retirement of the
103: runtime name. Likewise, disabling a loop's boundary leaves the loop present;
104: old ticks still reset it under current hydration. The declaration representation
105: and the effective runtime namespace must not be conflated.
106: 
107: ## History and evidence algorithm
108: 
109: The shared validator is pure over one captured declaration anchor, complete
110: self-lineage declaration fact history, bounded ticks, and the target document
111: set (effective current state for runtime, proposed successor for editing).
112: It does not open a store, sign, read keys, consult external source files or the
113: environment, repair projections, or execute any source/dispatch command.
114: 
115: 1. Validate the declaration anchor against the captured full H through the
116:    existing custody/projection contract. Select only the own genesis and
117:    self-lineage declaration overlays. Foreign and unscoped declarations remain
118:    inert, matching the existing resolver. Sort by receipt ordinal and sequence,
119:    never authored time or fact ID.
120: 2. Reconstruct effective runtime names at the genesis and each committed
121:    declaration revision. Preserve retirement evidence across intermediate
122:    revisions; do not compare only genesis/current or before/proposed documents.
123:    Multiple declaration documents in one Arrival batch form one revision:
124:    evaluate the resulting effective set, not transient partial document states
125:    with no observable runtime between them. This grouping is for namespace
126:    continuity; document overlay order remains receipt-sequence order. Wire
127:    batches contain fact rows only; a CAS containing fact and tick drafts gives
128:    those drafts distinct record ordinals. A query reporting an owned tick and
129:    declaration fact at the same ordinal contradicts this shape and refuses
130:    with both actual coordinates. Do not invent an ordering for that adapter
131:    contradiction. This is not a newly legal mixed-row record format.
132: 3. At each owned tick's receipt position, classify its role using that revision.
133:    A vertex-name tick with a simultaneously present loop of that name is
134:    ambiguous. A currently relevant loop-name tick with no provable historical
135:    loop membership is unproven. Tick payload shape, signature, cursor, or
136:    current name validity cannot recover the missing role evidence.
137: 4. For each target runtime name with historical local ticks, require continuous
138:    membership since the relevant tick. A disappearance and later return
139:    conflicts even if its final declaration equals the earlier one. Internal
140:    tracking of membership intervals is evidence analysis, not a newly minted
141:    persistent incarnation ID. Ignore retired names that the target does not
142:    interpret. An ambiguous vertex-name tick matters when the target declares
143:    a vertex boundary; without that consumer the saved period field has no
144:    supported Arrival effect. Later re-enabling that boundary restores the
145:    refusal, not the missing role evidence.
146: 5. Analyze the proposed successor as one additional revision with no fabricated
147:    fact ID, timestamp, ordinal, or Commit. This allows retirement and safe
148:    configuration correction even when the old runtime itself refuses. Run
149:    the check for no-op proposals too; no-op does not certify unsafe execution.
150: 6. Return normally or a deterministic diagnostic naming the reason, boundary,
151:    and actual conflicting tick/declaration receipt where available. Do not
152:    manufacture an epoch/cutoff or report guessed identity as proven.
153: 
154: The custody-bounded query is still an adapter contract: completing a watermark
155: does not independently establish row agreement or prove a projected declaration
156: was authored by the claimed observer. C6 adds continuity analysis, not a second
157: custody audit or new tick-authentication rule.
158: 
159: The evidence read is through captured H even when event timestamps are negative
160: or far in the future. `TickRequest` defaults to `since=0`; the validator must
161: explicitly request the full timestamp range. Existing hydration/pending
162: timestamp selection is a separate policy and must not be widened accidentally.
163: 
164: Use documents as the common target input for all three entrypoints. The result
165: includes the target's provable runtime names and unresolved-generator flag.
166: Apply C5 reservation to provable names, including literal generated loops,
167: during declaration preview and preparation as well as runtime. Runtime also
168: checks names in both directions: every provable target name must be materialized
169: (including implicit `cite`), and every actual compiled name must belong to the
170: proved set or be covered by an explicitly unknown generator. An unexplained
171: extra or missing name refuses before hydration. Thus current parameter-file
172: changes between verification and compilation cannot silently remove a proved
173: consumer. This checks names, not arbitrary fold-code equivalence.
174: 
175: Unchanged wire declaration decoding remains authoritative. Prefer sharing the
176: existing overlay step/ordering code rather than introducing a second subtly
177: different definition of self-lineage history. Unknown declaration kinds retain
178: the resolver's forward-compatible inert treatment; malformed supported
179: namespace evidence refuses rather than yielding a fabricated safe history.
180: 
181: ## Generated loop names
182: 
183: Only template sources with a declared `loop` generate runtime loop specs in
184: the current compiler. Bare paths, inline source commands, and templates without
185: such a loop do not create additional loop identities. They must not trigger a
186: blanket source-history refusal.
187: 
188: For a template loop, literal inline parameter rows and the stored loop document
189: can establish generated names without opening the template file. Match the
190: compiler's actual ordering and override semantics: sources sorted by recorded
191: order/subject, parameter rows in order, generated specs overriding explicit
192: specs at equal names. Variables used only by collection commands do not make a
193: literal loop name unprovable.
194: 
195: A `from` parameter file's hash pin commits to historical bytes. If bytes
196: available now verify against the pin recorded for a revision, those bytes can
197: establish that revision's parameter rows. An absent, mismatched, or unpinned
198: file supplies no such evidence. Environment-indirected `kind` remains unknown
199: even in verified rows because the resolved environment value was not recorded.
200: Unknown generators can produce/override any name, including the vertex name.
201: 
202: Keep the classifier pure with explicit `verified_params: hash -> ordered rows`
203: evidence. A shared caller-side collector used by runtime, preparation, and
204: semantic preview obtains candidate bytes from captured historical parameter
205: paths relative to the locator, hashes those exact bytes, and accepts them only
206: for matching recorded pins. Parse the same byte snapshot that was hashed;
207: never verify a path and reopen it to parse potentially changed bytes. Reuse an
208: extracted form of the compiler's parameter-text parser, preserving encoding,
209: header, comments, row ordering, and last-column behavior. Do not implement a
210: second grammar. Cache by verified content hash within this capture only.
211: Unknown/unavailable evidence remains unknown and only blocks a relevant proof;
212: an irrelevant unreadable historical source must not poison a direct loop.
213: No network retrieval or environment resolution supplies historical evidence.
214: 
215: The classifier uses the same whole-value `$NAME` indirection recognition and
216: `$$` leading-dollar escape as the compiler. Partial strings remain literal,
217: matching current behavior. Parameter indirection used only by source commands
218: does not make a literal `kind` unknown. This evidence collector does not replace
219: current runtime pin verification and compilation, which retain their own checks.
220: 
221: That runtime pin gate already exists: `_build_effective_arrival_candidate`
222: calls `effective_declaration_from_documents` with default `verify_pins=True`;
223: the latter calls `verify_source_pins_from_documents`, which checks both source
224: content and `from.params_sha256` before `compile_sources`. Do not add a duplicate
225: gate based on the follow-up review's mistaken claim that it is absent.
226: Continuity here describes the recorded declaration and its pinned expansion,
227: not forensic proof that every past external program obeyed that declaration.
228: Unknown legacy behavior or an origin label is not upgraded into authentication.
229: 
230: Use three-valued membership per name and revision. Direct, implicit, or literal
231: generated membership proves **present** even if another generator has unknown
232: names: an override changes its interpretation but does not remove that name.
233: If the name is not in the provable set and an unresolved generator could emit
234: it, membership is **unknown**. Otherwise it is **absent**.
235: 
236: For every old local loop tick that the target would interpret, membership must
237: be provably present at its receipt and throughout all later revisions through
238: the target. Unknown membership anywhere in that interval refuses: an unknown
239: intervening revision could conceal retirement/recreation without containing a
240: tick itself. Analyze every relevant tick, not just the newest pending edge;
241: hydration also consumes historical reset markers. A tick whose name is absent
242: from the target is not attached to a current loop, so that retired stream alone
243: does not block execution. Unknown target membership for an old tick refuses.
244: 
245: For a vertex-name tick consumed by a target vertex boundary, loop membership
246: at its receipt must be provably absent.
247: Present means a role collision; unknown means its role cannot be established.
248: The vertex identity itself continues while its boundary list is edited or
249: disabled, so only loop-name ambiguity at that tick changes this role proof.
250: Unresolved revisions before all relevant ticks do not, by themselves, create
251: consumption obligations. This is a conservative evidence rule, not proof that
252: unknown expansions actually collided. Literal generated sources and provably
253: continuous direct loops must remain usable. Do not compile old declarations
254: against current external inputs or claim that no document edit proves stability.
255: 
256: ## Integration and effects
257: 
258: - Runtime: invoke the validator in the shared effective-candidate builder
259:   before `hydrate_snapshot`, pending-boundary planning, signer invocation, and source
260:   collection. Ordinary, batch, preview, and source paths inherit that one check.
261:   The lower-level caller-responsible planners remain internal; C6 does not
262:   pretend to validate an arbitrary caller-built `Vertex` against history.
263:   SDK credential providers may already have loaded signer capabilities before
264:   capture; C6 does not claim that loading never occurred or redesign providers.
265:   Raise `BoundaryContinuityRefused(RuntimeWriteRefused)` retaining the actual
266:   `basis`, `captured_head`, effective declaration, and a small immutable issue
267:   DTO. Expose actual `tick_id`, receipt `ordinal`, relevant declaration `fact_id`
268:   and `vertex` through existing C2 scalar evidence fields when known. The local
269:   planning attempt has phase `prepare` and custody append not entered; it does
270:   not erase prior successful source tiers or imply an external witness did not
271:   advance. The diagnostic contains no full source/record payloads.
272: - Declaration preparation: validate the proposed successor at the same CURRENT
273:   basis after history/custody checks and before key-history work that invokes
274:   signers or creates drafts/intents. Use `DeclarationPreparationRefused` with
275:   established prepare/custody-not-entered evidence and captured H. An accepted
276:   registry open may still advance an external witness; custody-not-entered
277:   refers to append, not an assertion of zero effects anywhere. Preserve the
278:   structured conflict as an explicit exception cause (`raise ... from ...`);
279:   C2 already serializes `__cause__`. A general cause parameter on every
280:   preparation refusal factory is unnecessary. Raise that explicit preparation
281:   refusal ahead of the generic basis-error wrapper, preserving a continuity
282:   diagnostic instead of mislabeling it as failure to capture the basis.
283: - SDK semantic preview: use the same bounded history/target validator, with its
284:   existing normalized refusal family and no invented signing/Commit evidence.
285:   A preview must not say applicable for a proposal that the history gate refuses.
286: - Reads/verify/export: do not add this execution gate to evidence reconstruction
287:   or ordinary read APIs. Read-state interpretation remains available and is not
288:   a certification of safe runtime continuity.
289: - Legacy attached `Vertex.replay`/`evaluate_boundaries` and `load_vertex_program`
290:   are outside this supported Arrival capture contract. Their separate origin
291:   and variable-substitution behavior remains legacy-retirement work; C6 must
292:   not claim to have made every historical CLI/runtime path conformant.
293: - Initialization has no old tick history. C5's pre-genesis name check remains;
294:   no pointless history pass or key migration is added.
295: - Existing declaration apply/recovery uses its frozen plan/durable intent.
296:   Runtime capture independently rejects any unsafe history imported or appended
297:   through other mechanisms. No recovery rewrite, automatic retry, or implicit
298:   transition is introduced.
299: 
300: ## Acceptance and staged work
301: 
302: Engine tests must reproduce the old acceptance of a ticked remove/recreate and
303: of a corrected historical loop/vertex collision. Assert the refusal happens
304: before hydration, signing, append, pending planning, or collection as appropriate.
305: Use full bounded receipt histories, including intermediate retirement, batched
306: changes, equal/out-of-order event times, foreign declarations/ticks, a relevant
307: undeclared historical tick, implicit `cite`, and stale local-file disagreement.
308: 
309: Positive engine and real SDK scenarios must demonstrate in-place fold and
310: boundary-count edits retaining edges, `after` inheriting exhaustion, tick-free
311: changes reinterpreting older facts, retirement followed by a fresh-name
312: replacement, unchanged/literal template sources, and tick-free C5 repair.
313: Keep evidence reads/export working for refused histories and verify exact
314: custody prefix preservation through an accepted appended correction.
315: 
316: Negative source scenarios cover missing/mismatched historical parameter pins
317: and env-derived generated names with old ticks even when source documents are
318: unchanged. Positive scenarios prove historical pin-matching rows work in all
319: three entrypoints, direct names stay provably present despite unrelated unknown
320: generators, and a file replacement between read/hash/parse cannot substitute
321: unverified rows. A command-only source edit with provable names remains usable.
322: Test ambiguous-history repair without a vertex consumer, followed by refusal
323: when one is proposed again. Exercise every row of the count-recovery table,
324: including a fresh-name `after` already exhausted by old facts.
325: 
326: Stages: root reconciles this design and agent audits; freeze exact design and
327: supporting source packet; Fable 5.1 high reviews it; root triages all findings
328: and revises/re-reviews material contract changes. Only then assign Sol engine
329: implementation, Terra SDK acceptance, and Luna independent validation. Run
330: focused regression/baseline demonstrations followed by engine, SDK, architecture
331: and scoped lint checks. Finish with the established Fable implementation review
332: (low effort unless the user asks otherwise). No implementation starts merely
333: because a reviewer process exited successfully; its findings must be resolved.
334: 
335: An explicit boundary transition remains future design: it would append intent
336: and a receipt-grounded cutover, identify the relevant role/name and predecessor
337: evidence, define restart versus carry, and preserve all historical rows. C6
338: does not smuggle that new replay protocol into a routine declaration edit.

=== docs/libs/sdk/ADOPTION.md ===
1: # Adopt a migrated Arrival declaration
2: 
3: `sdk.adopt_arrival` appends the declaration anchor that makes a migrated
4: Arrival history usable by ordinary SDK reads and writes. It preserves the
5: migration prefix and uses the existing physical lineage. Fresh stores use
6: `init_vertex`; stores with an adopted declaration use `edit_declaration`.
7: 
8: The caller supplies two distinct snapshots:
9: 
10: - `reviewed_text` and its `reviewed_sha256`: exact declaration bytes selected
11:   for adoption, such as the copied legacy vertex used for migration.
12: - `declaration_text`: the current published vertex, naming an explicit backend,
13:   physical lineage, and authority role.
14: 
15: Their declaration documents must agree apart from residence. This first
16: operation cannot introduce or replace observer keys, or adopt a changed
17: declaration as an incidental part of migration. It checks the selected head,
18: registry-forming signatures, declaration identities and captured observer keys
19: before signing the new anchor.
20: It independently verifies the resulting FACT and ARRIVAL signatures against
21: the selected mapped binding's public key; a provider-local verifier cannot
22: replace that check.
23: It also checks that the selected backend provides projection catch-up before
24: resolving signing credentials; the preflight does not advance the projection.
25: 
26: ```python
27: from sdk import adopt_arrival
28: 
29: # Keep these snapshots and the report verification receipt from the offline
30: # migration workflow. Verify its report at selected_head BEFORE adoption.
31: result = adopt_arrival(
32:     published_vertex,
33:     selected_head=migration.head,
34:     reviewed_text=reviewed_text,
35:     reviewed_sha256=reviewed_sha256,
36:     declaration_text=published_vertex.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
37:     observer="alice",
38:     credentials=mapped_provider,
39: )
40: receipt = result.as_dict()
41: ```
42: 
43: The mapped binding must already exist and match the observer's captured key
44: history. Adoption resolves distinct FACT and ARRIVAL authorship requests;
45: neither lookup creates keys nor falls back to legacy credentials. The result
46: retains the adoption commit, projection outcome and public binding evidence.
47: Migration report verification remains the offline caller's responsibility;
48: the report's live-head comparison no longer applies after adoption advances
49: the history.
50: 
51: Before appending, the operation durably reserves the exact signed draft in
52: `<vertex>.arrival-adopt.intent`. If interrupted, retain the intent and the
53: typed error's commit/head evidence, then reconcile explicitly:
54: 
55: ```python
56: from sdk import recover_arrival_adoption
57: 
58: recovered = recover_arrival_adoption(intent_path)
59: ```
60: 
61: A stale apply may leave this intent reserved; use its `intent_path` for explicit
62: recovery before attempting a fresh adoption. Maintenance capability is checked
63: again before apply or recovery appends, using the registry supplied to that call.
64: 
65: Recovery requires no signing credentials. It either appends the reserved draft
66: at its original predecessor or recognizes that exact draft at its expected
67: ordinal, synchronizes the projection and checks the published cache. It does
68: not re-sign or append a duplicate. If later records exist, `head` still names
69: the adoption head; `observed_head` records the later tip. A reconstructed commit
70: labels its durability evidence as recovery evidence rather than claiming the
71: original append receipt was retained.
72: 
73: If recovery Full-verifies that another record has taken the reserved next
74: ordinal, it retires only that provably superseded intent and returns a stale
75: refusal. A caller can then prepare a fresh adoption at the new selected head.
76: Malformed intents also return a typed SDK refusal and remain in place for
77: operator inspection. Reviewed source, template and parameter pins must remain
78: intact during recovery, as they must for normal runtime declaration resolution.
79: 
80: The operation reconciles the already-published cache without rewriting it.
81: A changed cache or a post-append projection failure leaves a recovery boundary;
82: a durable append is not rolled back. Process-exit tests cover reservation and
83: append boundaries, not arbitrary power loss. Live writer coordination and a
84: representative user-store rehearsal remain separate from this SDK operation.
85: 
86: Adoption alone does not prove continuity for older boundary ticks. If preserved
87: legacy ticks would be consumed as current loop resets or vertex periods but
88: predate the adopted declaration, ordinary writes can refuse with
89: `BoundaryContinuityRefused`. Migration, adoption, reads and export can succeed
90: while writes remain unavailable. The loops real-store rehearsal demonstrated
91: this case; do not bypass the continuity check or silently discard those ticks.
92: To explicitly begin fresh execution state, select the signed adoption policy:
93: 
94: ```python
95: result = adopt_arrival(
96:     target,
97:     selected_head=migration.head,
98:     reviewed_text=reviewed_text,
99:     reviewed_sha256=reviewed_sha256,
100:     declaration_text=published_text,
101:     observer="project",
102:     credentials=mapped_provider,
103:     runtime_epoch="fresh",
104: )
105: ```
106: 
107: The default `runtime_epoch="strict"` preserves the existing continuity checks.
108: Fresh mode records declaration protocol 2 and the exact signed marker
109: `fresh-after-anchor-v1`; older protocol-1 readers refuse it. It starts execution
110: folds at their declared initial values, counters at zero, and period context
111: without any old tick. Only facts and ticks received after the adoption anchor
112: participate in runtime replay and source cadence, regardless of their event
113: timestamps. Post-adoption continuity checks remain in force.
114: 
115: `read_state` reflects this execution epoch and includes mode/anchor evidence in
116: its generation metadata; aggregate state applies each member's own floor.
117: `read_summary`, fact/tick queries and export retain all historical rows. Global
118: duplicate-ID checks and physical tick predecessor/window hashes also retain
119: all history: starting fresh execution does not reset the custody chain.
120: 
121: Recovery derives the policy from the authenticated reserved draft and exposes
122: the recovered `runtime_epoch`; it takes no policy override. An existing adopted
123: store cannot be reset by editing its locator or passing a new recovery option.
124: Select fresh mode when preparing the explicit adoption of an unadopted copy.

=== libs/engine/src/engine/arrival.py ===
1: """arrival — the append-only log that holds canonical custody for a store.
2: 
3: Slice 0 of the arrival substrate (design fact
4: ``decision:design/arrival-slice0-record-grammar``; the wire format is written
5: out in ``docs/dev/arrival-slice0-record-grammar-2026-08-17.md``). One file per
6: store, ``<name>.arrival``, one JSON object per line. A record's position in
7: that file — its **ordinal** — is its identity coordinate, paired with the
8: **lineage** the genesis record opens. Everything derived from the log is a
9: projection and is never authoritative.
10: 
11: What slice 0 delivered: the record grammar, genesis minting, append under an
12: interprocess lock, read by ordinal, the walk with density and chain
13: verification, torn-tail truncation, corrupt-interior refusal, and the resume
14: mark. Cut A (decision:design/arrival-sliceA-authority) added the authority
15: half: the genesis carries the founding public key, self-signed at ordinal 0,
16: and :func:`verify_authorship` resolves every verifying key from a
17: ``(lineage, ordinal)`` coordinate in the log — never from any artifact
18: outside it. Projection re-derivation, declared projection orders, and audit
19: re-basing are later slices and are not here.
20: 
21: Two postures carry over from the existing store and are load-bearing:
22: 
23: * **Truncate only what was never complete, and only at the tail.** A final
24:   line with no ``\\n`` is an interrupted append; anything else that fails to
25:   decode, fails its ``rh``, breaks the ordinal succession, or breaks the
26:   ``prev`` link is corruption, and the answer is a human look rather than a
27:   silent delete — the posture ``ceremony.IntentCorrupt`` already takes. On a
28:   file that is the only copy, silent recovery is data loss with extra steps.
29: * **The writer truncates, the reader never does.** Reads take no lock, so a
30:   reader cannot distinguish "torn" from "an append is in flight right now";
31:   it sees a complete newline-terminated record or it sees nothing yet. Only
32:   the appender, holding the lock and knowing no append is in progress, may
33:   conclude a tail is torn and cut it.
34: 
35: Known limitation, stated rather than discovered: ``fcntl.flock`` is advisory
36: and its behaviour over NFS and some network filesystems is unreliable. The
37: concurrency contract below holds on a local POSIX filesystem. A store on a
38: network mount is out of contract.
39: """
40: 
41: from __future__ import annotations
42: 
43: import base64
44: import binascii
45: import contextlib
46: import fcntl
47: import hashlib
48: import json
49: import math
50: import os
51: import time
52: from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Iterator, Mapping, Sequence
53: from dataclasses import dataclass
54: from pathlib import Path
55: from typing import NoReturn, TypeGuard
56: 
57: import rfc8785
58: from ulid import ULID
59: 
60: from .arrival_contract import Head
61:

63:     "ARRIVAL_SUFFIX",
64:     "LOCK_SUFFIX",
65:     "TMP_SUFFIX",
66:     "GRAMMAR_VERSION",
67:     "GENESIS_KIND",
68:     "KEY_INTRODUCTION_KIND",
69:     "RECORD_FIELDS",
70:     "ArrivalError",
71:     "ArrivalGrammarError",
72:     "ArrivalCorrupt",
73:     "ArrivalTornTail",
74:     "GenesisRefused",
75:     "AppendRejected",
76:     "StaleHead",
77:     "ForkedHeight",
78:     "AuthorshipUnverified",
79:     "ArrivalLog",
80:     "Entry",
81:     "KeyRegistry",
82:     "KeyResolution",
83:     "ResumeMark",
84:     "Verify",
85:     "build_record",
86:     "key_registry",
87:     "verify_authorship",

89:     "verify_authorship_records",

99: 
100: ARRIVAL_SUFFIX = ".arrival"
101: LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"
102: TMP_SUFFIX = ".tmp"
103: 
104: GRAMMAR_VERSION = 1
105: GENESIS_KIND = "genesis"
106: 
107: # The kind that introduces a key into the log's own registry. Its body names
108: # the observer the key speaks for and the key itself; the record must be
109: # signed by a key that is ALREADY valid at its ordinal, which is what makes
110: # the registry a chain of custody rather than a mutable table.
111: KEY_INTRODUCTION_KIND = "key"
112: 
113: # Emitted key order. Transport encoding, not canonicalization — the same
114: # posture ``jsonl_codec._dump`` documents; canonicalization for hashing is JCS
115: # and is independent of the order bytes come out in. ``rh`` is last purely as
116: # a reading convenience: it cannot cover itself, so it is computed over the
117: # object with ``rh`` removed.
118: RECORD_FIELDS = ("v", "lin", "ord", "prev", "at", "k", "observer", "origin", "body")
119: _SIG = "sig"
120: _RH = "rh"
121: _ALLOWED = frozenset((*RECORD_FIELDS, _SIG, _RH))
122: 
123: # JCS (RFC 8785) numeric domain — mirrors the guard ``jsonl_codec`` puts at
124: # its own gate. An integer outside it is not canonicalizable, so a record
125: # carrying one cannot be hashed: refuse at the codec rather than detonate
126: # inside the hasher.
127: _JCS_INT_MAX = 2**53 - 1
128: _JCS_INT_MIN = -(2**53) + 1
129: 
130: # Reverse scan granularity for finding a line boundary. Chunked so the scan
131: # never loads the whole log and never gives up as a function of line length.
132: _CHUNK = 64 * 1024
133: 
134: _HEX = frozenset("0123456789abcdef")
135: 
136: # A signer is injected, never imported: engine does not depend on ``sign``.
137: # Shape matches the store's ``fact_signer`` — (observer, commitment digest
138: # hex) -> signature, or None when that observer has no key.
139: Signer = Callable[[str, str], "str | None"]
140: 
141: # Verification is injected under the same posture. Shape: (public key in the
142: # ratified wire format, signature, commitment digest hex) -> bool. The
143: # composing layer supplies the algorithm and the domain-separation prefix;
144: # this module supplies WHICH key may speak at WHICH position, and nothing
145: # about how a signature is checked.
146: Verify = Callable[[str, str, str], bool]
147: 
148: # The ratified key wire format: an Ed25519 public key as raw-32-byte base64,
149: # copy-identical to the composing layer's on-disk public-key file. The
150: # grammar pins the shape (so a malformed key is refused at the append site);
151: # the algorithm stays the injected verifier's business.
152: _KEY_RAW_LEN = 32
153: 
154: 
155: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
156: # Errors
157: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
158: 
159: 
160: class ArrivalError(Exception):
161:     """Base for every refusal the arrival log raises."""
162: 
163: 
164: class ArrivalGrammarError(ArrivalError, ValueError):
165:     """A record object does not match the grammar.
166: 
167:     Raised in BOTH directions from one validator: an encode is held to the
168:     same domain a decode enforces, so a wrongly typed field fails at the
169:     append site, where it is attributable, rather than becoming a durable
170:     line that bricks every later open.
171:     """
172: 
173: 
174: class ArrivalCorrupt(ArrivalError):
175:     """A complete record in the log is not intact, and the log refuses.
176: 
177:     Corruption is anything a complete line can be wrong about: it fails to
178:     decode, its ``rh`` does not recompute, its ordinal breaks the dense
179:     succession, or its ``prev`` does not name its predecessor. None of it is
180:     a state an appender can produce, so it is evidence of a torn write that
181:     somehow survived, of an out-of-band edit, or of tampering — and the safe
182:     answer is a human look, not a silent skip or a truncation.
183: 
184:     ``ordinal`` names where the walk stopped: the ordinal the record was
185:     expected to carry, so the human has a place to start reading.
186:     """
187: 
188:     def __init__(self, message: str, ordinal: int) -> None:
189:         super().__init__(f"arrival log corrupt at ordinal {ordinal}: {message}")
190:         self.ordinal = ordinal
191: 
192: 
193: class ArrivalTornTail(ArrivalError):
194:     """The arrival log ends mid-record before a terminating newline.
195: 
196:     The trailing bytes of the log do not end with a newline delimiter,
197:     indicating that the final record was only partially written.
198:     """
199: 
200: 
201: class GenesisRefused(ArrivalError):
202:     """A lineage cannot be opened, or a file cannot be read as an arrival log.
203: 
204:     Three shapes, all refusals rather than repairs: the arrival file already
205:     exists (a lineage is minted exactly once, and overwriting one destroys a
206:     store); the genesis carries no signature (genesis is the lineage's
207:     attestation root — the existing unsignable-genesis rule, carried across);
208:     or the file's first record is not a valid genesis, in which case the file
209:     is not an arrival log and there is nothing to infer. Identity is never
210:     read out of content: position 0 is structural and cannot be forged into
211:     existence by appending.
212:     """
213: 
214: 
215: class AuthorshipUnverified(ArrivalError):
216:     """A signed record's authorship cannot be established from the log.
217: 
218:     Raised by :func:`verify_authorship` when a signature fails to verify
219:     under every key that is valid for its observer at its position — the
220:     ruled rule: a key is valid at position N iff it was introduced at a
221:     position < N, or N is the genesis position and the record is
222:     self-certifying. A failure is evidence of a forged signature, a key
223:     introduction that never happened, or a self-certification attempted
224:     above ordinal 0 — never a state this module's own writers can produce.
225: 
226:     ``ordinal`` names the record whose authorship failed.
227:     """
228: 
229:     def __init__(self, message: str, ordinal: int) -> None:
230:         super().__init__(f"authorship unverified at ordinal {ordinal}: {message}")
231:         self.ordinal = ordinal
232: 
233: 
234: class AppendRejected(ArrivalError):
235:     """A candidate record does not follow the log's head.
236: 
237:     Append validates, it does not assign: the coordinate is written into the
238:     record, so a candidate whose ``ord`` is not the head's plus one, whose
239:     ``lin`` is not the log's lineage, or whose ``prev`` does not name the
240:     head's ``rh`` is refused before a byte is written. A rejected append
241:     leaves the log exactly as it was.
242:     """
243: 
244: 
245: class StaleHead(AppendRejected):
246:     """The compare-and-swap pin no longer describes this log's head.
247: 
248:     A SUBCLASS rather than a bare :class:`AppendRejected` because the parent
249:     is raised for two different things: this, and the placement faults
250:     :meth:`ArrivalLog._check_follows` finds in a candidate carried in from
251:     elsewhere. An adapter that has to answer "was this a head mismatch?"
252:     would otherwise be left sniffing messages, and a message is not a type.
253:     Every existing ``except AppendRejected`` and ``raises(AppendRejected)``
254:     keeps working, because this is one.
255:     """
256: 
257: 
258: class ForkedHeight(ArrivalError):
259:     """A candidate would fill a height this log already holds differently.
260: 
261:     Deliberately NOT an :class:`AppendRejected`. That family means "the head
262:     moved, re-read it and try again", and ``store.merge_store`` retries on it
263:     — but a fork is the one refusal retrying cannot clear. The two histories
264:     disagree about what happened at a coordinate, and no amount of re-reading
265:     makes them agree; a retry loop would spin instead of surfacing.
266: 
267:     Replication stops here rather than choosing between the two records,
268:     because choosing is admission into another lineage, and admission is a
269:     different operation with different evidence behind it.
270:     """
271: 
272: 
273: def _refuse_stale_head(actual: dict, expected: Head | None) -> None:
274:     """Refuse unless ``actual`` is the head the caller pinned.
275: 
276:     ALL THREE coordinate fields, which is what makes this a compare-and-swap
277:     over the log's identity rather than over its length. The ordinal alone
278:     cannot tell "nothing arrived" from "the record at this ordinal was
279:     replaced": a log truncated back and rewritten to the same height passes an
280:     ordinal compare and fails this one, and that case is precisely the
281:     rollback the backend contract asks a store to detect (§11).
282: 
283:     Called from inside the fence at both append sites, never from outside it —
284:     a compare that ran before the lock would be answering about a head some
285:     other writer is free to move before the write lands. The two call sites
286:     stay separate calls on purpose: each is independently the thing that makes
287:     its own method a compare-and-swap, and each has its own test.
288:     """
289:     if expected is None:
290:         return
291:     if (
292:         actual["lin"] == expected.lineage
293:         and actual["ord"] == expected.ordinal
294:         and actual[_RH] == expected.record_hash
295:     ):
296:         return
297:     raise StaleHead(
298:         f"the log's head is ({actual['lin']}, {actual['ord']}, {actual[_RH]}), "
299:         f"not the expected ({expected.lineage}, {expected.ordinal}, "
300:         f"{expected.record_hash}) — records arrived since the caller "
301:         "reconciled, or this coordinate now holds a different record"
302:     )
303: 
304: 
305: def _checked_pin(following: object) -> Head | None:
306:     """``following`` as a head pin, refusing anything weaker.
307: 
308:     An ordinal is REFUSED rather than widened into a head, because widening
309:     it here would mean this function inventing the two fields the caller did
310:     not supply — and a pin the callee completed is not a pin. Construction
311:     over detection (``decision:practice/construction-vs-detection-ratchets``):
312:     there is no spelling of a weaker compare-and-swap for a caller to reach
313:     for, so none can be reached for by accident.
314: 
315:     :class:`ArrivalError` and deliberately not :class:`AppendRejected`: this
316:     is a caller bug, and ``store.merge_store`` retries on
317:     :class:`AppendRejected` — a type error caught by that loop would spin
318:     instead of surfacing.
319:     """
320:     if following is None or isinstance(following, Head):
321:         return following
322:     if _is_int(following):
323:         raise ArrivalError(
324:             f"following must be a Head, not the bare ordinal {following!r} — "
325:             "an ordinal-only pin cannot tell an untouched log from one "
326:             "truncated and rewritten to the same height. Pass the full head "
327:             "(engine.arrival_contract.Head), or None for an unpinned append"
328:         )
329:     raise ArrivalError(
330:         f"following must be a Head or None, got {type(following).__name__}"
331:     )
332:

339: def arrival_path_for(base: Path | str) -> Path:
340:     """The arrival log for a store base path: ``<name>.arrival``.
341: 
342:     Suffix appended to the full name, never ``with_suffix`` — the residence
343:     and ceremony sidecar helpers do the same, so ``alcove.db`` and ``alcove``
344:     do not collapse onto one arrival path.
345:     """
346:     base = Path(base)
347:     return base.parent / (base.name + ARRIVAL_SUFFIX)
348: 
349: 
350: def lock_path_for(arrival_path: Path | str) -> Path:
351:     """The append-exclusion lock beside a log: ``<name>.arrival.lock``.
352: 
353:     Distinct from the index quarantine lock in ``jsonl_store``: different
354:     resource, different holder, and the two must not be confused.
355:     """
356:     arrival_path = Path(arrival_path)
357:     return arrival_path.parent / (arrival_path.name + LOCK_SUFFIX)
358: 
359: 
360: def tmp_path_for(arrival_path: Path | str) -> Path:
361:     """The genesis staging path: ``<name>.arrival.tmp``.
362: 
363:     Genesis only. It is the mutex for minting — the process that wins
364:     ``O_EXCL`` on this path is the one allowed to publish — so it is a fixed
365:     name rather than a per-process temp file.
366:     """
367:     arrival_path = Path(arrival_path)
368:     return arrival_path.parent / (arrival_path.name + TMP_SUFFIX)

371: def mint_lineage() -> str:
372:     """A fresh lineage id. ULID, the repo's id species."""
373:     return str(ULID())
