134: # The one wire codec this backend exports and imports. Named after the grammar
135: # it is, and versioned separately from `GRAMMAR_VERSION` on purpose: the codec
136: # is what an export FILE claims about its own framing, and a future codec that
137: # packed the same records differently would leave the record grammar alone.
138: EXPORT_CODEC = "arrival-jsonl-v1"
139: 
140: 
141: def file_projection_path(location: Path | str) -> Path:
142:     """Choose a derived pathname without interpreting the ledger's format.
143: 
144:     Retain the established sibling for conventional log names. Other explicit
145:     file locators get a distinct sidecar; a .db spelling is still an Arrival
146:     ledger and must never be opened as its own SQLite projection.
147:     """
148:     path = Path(location)
149:     if path.suffix.lower() in (".arrival", ".jsonl"):
150:         return path.with_suffix(".db")
151:     return path.with_name(path.name + ".projection.db")
152: 
153: # How the codec frames one record. A manifest field rather than a convention,
154: # because "each element is one record's line INCLUDING its newline" is what
155: # makes ``b"".join(prefix.records)`` byte-identical to the log's own prefix —
156: # a property a reader can only rely on if the export states it.
157: _FRAMING = "newline-terminated"
158: 
159: 
160: # What an append has established before it reports success. The mechanism is
161: # named because the profile alone does not tell an operator what to check:
162: # §05's callout is explicit that this contract is LOCAL POSIX storage, and
163: # that moving the same bytes onto NFS does not inherit it.
164: _DURABILITY = DurabilityReceipt(
165:     profile=DurabilityProfile.HOST,
166:     mechanism="advisory flock, one write, one fsync, on local POSIX storage",
167: )
168: 
169: 
170: def _decoded(prefix: ExportedPrefix) -> list[dict]:
171:     """The export's records, decoded and held to the grammar.
172: 
173:     :func:`engine.arrival.decode_record` is the gate, so a record whose ``rh``
174:     does not recompute never reaches the import — the bytes travelled, and
175:     anything that travelled has to be re-established rather than assumed.
176: 
177:     Framing is read from the manifest and ENFORCED: a codec that says its
178:     elements are newline-terminated and hands over one that is not has
179:     contradicted itself, and quietly accepting either shape would make
180:     ``b"".join(records)`` mean two different things.
181:     """
182:     framing = prefix.manifest.get("framing")
183:     if framing != _FRAMING:
184:         raise ValueError(
185:             f"this backend reads {_FRAMING!r} framing and nothing else, but "
186:             f"this export's manifest claims {framing!r}"
187:         )
188:     records: list[dict] = []
189:     for index, line in enumerate(prefix.records):
190:         if not line.endswith(b"\n"):
191:             raise ArrivalCorrupt(
192:                 f"element {index} carries no newline, but the manifest claims "
193:                 f"{_FRAMING!r} framing",
194:                 index,
195:             )
196:         records.append(decode_record(line[:-1]))
197:     return records
198: 
199: 
200: def _refuse_disagreeing_manifest(
201:     prefix: ExportedPrefix, imported: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]
202: ) -> None:
203:     """Re-derive every manifest claim from the records and compare.
204: 
205:     A manifest travels with the bytes it describes, so it is exactly as
206:     trustworthy as they are: checking it is the only thing that makes carrying
207:     one worth doing. Each claim is re-derived rather than sampled — a count
208:     that matched while the head did not would still be a corrupt export.
209: 
210:     Density is what makes this cheap: the prefix runs from ordinal 0 to the
211:     captured head with nothing missing, so ``count`` is arithmetic and the
212:     starting ordinal is a constant.
213:     """
214:     if not imported:
215:         raise ArrivalCorrupt(
216:             "this export holds no records — a prefix runs from genesis, so "
217:             "the smallest honest export is one record",
218:             0,
219:         )
220:     if prefix.manifest.get("protocol") != GRAMMAR_VERSION:
221:         raise ArrivalCorrupt(
222:             f"this export claims protocol {prefix.manifest.get('protocol')!r}, "
223:             f"but this backend reads grammar {GRAMMAR_VERSION}",
224:             0,
225:         )
226:     if imported[0]["ord"] != 0:
227:         raise ArrivalCorrupt(
228:             f"this export starts at ordinal {imported[0]['ord']}, not 0 — a "
229:             "prefix that does not start at genesis is a suffix, and importing "
230:             "one is replication, not import",
231:             imported[0]["ord"],
232:         )
233:     last = imported[-1]
234:     derived = Head(
235:         lineage=last["lin"], ordinal=last["ord"], record_hash=last["rh"]
236:     )
237:     if derived != prefix.head:
238:         raise ArrivalCorrupt(
239:             f"this export's records end at {derived}, but it claims to capture "
240:             f"{prefix.head}",
241:             last["ord"],
242:         )
243:     claimed = (
244:         prefix.manifest.get("lineage"),
245:         prefix.manifest.get("through_ordinal"),
246:         prefix.manifest.get("through_record_hash"),
247:         prefix.manifest.get("count"),
248:     )
249:     if claimed != (derived.lineage, derived.ordinal, derived.record_hash, len(imported)):
250:         raise ArrivalCorrupt(
251:             f"this export's manifest claims {claimed}, but its records give "
252:             f"{(derived.lineage, derived.ordinal, derived.record_hash, len(imported))}",
253:             last["ord"],
254:         )
255: 
256: 
257: def _head_of(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Head:
258:     """A record's coordinate as a contract :class:`Head`.
259: 
260:     The one place the wire field names meet the neutral type. Keeping it to
261:     one function is what lets the rest of this module talk in ``Head`` and
262:     the log keep talking in records.
263:     """
264:     return Head(
265:         lineage=record["lin"], ordinal=record["ord"], record_hash=record["rh"]
266:     )
267: 
268: 
269: class FileLedger:
270:     """Custody over one ``.arrival`` log, in the contract's vocabulary.
271: 
272:     Satisfies :class:`engine.arrival_contract.ArrivalLedger` in full, and
273:     offers one op beyond it — ``import_prefix``, which the Protocol
274:     deliberately does not declare (see the module docstring).
275: 
276:     **Which verification level each operation invokes** (§06 requires a
277:     backend to say): :meth:`read`, :meth:`scan` and :meth:`head` all reach
278:     their answer through :meth:`engine.arrival.ArrivalLog.walk`, so they
279:     invoke FULL — the log's read path establishes that everything before a
280:     coordinate is intact before it will name what is at it. Only
281:     :meth:`verify` with an :class:`~engine.arrival_contract.Open` scope is
282:     cheap. That is a property of this backend, not of the contract; a backend
283:     with stored head metadata would answer :meth:`head` at OPEN.
284:     """
285: 
286:     def __init__(
287:         self, log: ArrivalLog, *, max_atomic_records: int | None = None
288:     ) -> None:
289:         """``max_atomic_records`` is None for "no configured limit".
290: 
291:         Different from a limit of one: §04 requires every backend to support
292:         one record and lets it advertise more. The file append holds the
293:         whole group under one lock and one fsync with no limit of its own, so
294:         an unset limit is the honest default — but a deployment that wants
295:         one gets a refusal that fires BEFORE any mutation, which is what §04
296:         asks for and what §12's configured-limit gate exercises.
297:         """
298:         self._log = log
299:         self._max_atomic_records = max_atomic_records
300: 
301:     # -- custody -----------------------------------------------------------
302: 
303:     def mint(self, options: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Head:
304:         """Exclusively create one signed genesis and return head 0.
305: 
306:         ``options`` are adapter-interpreted, the same way §02's ``location``
307:         is: this backend forwards them to
308:         :meth:`engine.arrival.ArrivalLog.mint`, which needs an observer, a
309:         signer and the founding public key.
310: 
311:         A second mint raises ``GenesisRefused`` — a backend exception, not a
312:         contract refusal, because the ratified refusal set has no member for
313:         "already minted". Passing it through is the honest option; the
314:         alternative is choosing one of the five and claiming something the
315:         evidence does not support.
316:         """
317:         log = ArrivalLog.mint(self._log.path, **dict(options))
318:         self._log = log
319:         return _head_of(log.genesis())
320: 
321:     def append(
322:         self, expected: Head | None, drafts: Sequence[RecordDraft]
323:     ) -> Commit:
324:         """Compare the full head, then assign and commit — indivisibly (§04).
325: 
326:         The whole transition is :meth:`ArrivalLog.append_marked_many`: the
327:         fence, the full-head compare (F1), coordinate assignment, one write
328:         and one fsync. Nothing is re-implemented here, which is the point —
329:         the append fence is ``flock``-based and per-open-file-description,
330:         and a second appender beside it would be a second way to be wrong.
331: 
332:         ``before`` is derived rather than re-read: the first record's
333:         ``prev`` IS the predecessor's record hash and its ordinal minus one
334:         IS the predecessor's ordinal, so the head the append actually landed
335:         on is known exactly, without a second trip past a log another writer
336:         is free to extend.
337:         """
338:         if not drafts:
339:             raise ValueError(
340:                 "append was handed no drafts — an empty append is a caller "
341:                 "bug, not a no-op to absorb"
342:             )
343:         if (
344:             self._max_atomic_records is not None
345:             and len(drafts) > self._max_atomic_records
346:         ):
347:             raise AtomicLimitExceeded(
348:                 f"{len(drafts)} records exceeds this backend's configured "
349:                 f"atomic limit of {self._max_atomic_records} — refused before "
350:                 "any mutation, because splitting the request across "
351:                 "transactions would turn one logical group into several"
352:             )
353:         entries = [
354:             Entry(
355:                 k=draft.kind,
356:                 body=dict(draft.body),
357:                 observer=draft.observer,
358:                 origin=draft.origin,
359:                 at=draft.authored_at,
360:                 signature=draft.signature,
361:             )
362:             for draft in drafts
363:         ]
364:         try:
365:             records, _mark = self._log.append_marked_many(
366:                 entries, following=expected
367:             )
368:         except StaleHead as exc:
369:             # 1:1, and only from the CAS subclass. The parent AppendRejected
370:             # is also raised for placement faults in a carried-in candidate,
371:             # and mapping those to HeadMismatch would assert something about
372:             # the head that the fault does not say.
373:             raise HeadMismatch(str(exc)) from exc
374: 
375:         first, last = records[0], records[-1]
376:         return Commit(
377:             before=Head(
378:                 lineage=first["lin"],
379:                 ordinal=first["ord"] - 1,
380:                 record_hash=first["prev"],
381:             ),
382:             records=tuple(records),
383:             after=_head_of(last),
384:             durability=_DURABILITY,
385:         )
386: 
387:     def replicate(
388:         self, expected: Head | None, records: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]
389:     ) -> Commit:
390:         """Insert an exact suffix of pre-coordinated records (§08).
391: 
392:         Composition, not a second appender: the whole transition is
393:         :meth:`engine.arrival.ArrivalLog.append_records`, which is the batched
394:         form of the primitive that has had the right posture all along —
395:         append VALIDATES, it never assigns. Nothing here rehashes, re-signs,
396:         or renumbers, so the records that land are byte-for-byte the records
397:         that were offered, which is the one property replication exists to
398:         keep. The same lock, the same full-head compare-and-swap and the same
399:         single fsync as :meth:`append`, because they are literally the same
400:         code path under a different build.
401: 
402:         Two refusals, and they are different claims:
403: 
404:         * :class:`~engine.arrival_contract.SameHeightFork` — the log already
405:           holds a DIFFERENT record at a height this batch would fill. The two
406:           histories disagree, retrying cannot make them agree, and choosing
407:           between them would be admission into another lineage.
408:         * :class:`~engine.arrival_contract.HeadMismatch` — the head is not
409:           where this batch assumed, either because ``expected`` no longer
410:           describes it or because the batch is not the suffix that follows it.
411:           Re-read and recompute which records are missing.
412: 
413:         A batch whose ordinals disagree with each other, or whose supplied
414:         ``rh`` does not recompute, refuses as this backend's own
415:         ``AppendRejected``/``ArrivalGrammarError``: the ratified refusal set
416:         has no member for "this candidate is malformed", and picking one would
417:         be a verdict the evidence does not support
418:         (``finding:slice2-wp1-refusal-set-gaps``).
419:         """
420:         if not records:
421:             raise ValueError(
422:                 "replicate was handed no records — an empty replication is a "
423:                 "caller bug, not a no-op to absorb"
424:             )
425:         if (
426:             self._max_atomic_records is not None
427:             and len(records) > self._max_atomic_records
428:         ):
429:             raise AtomicLimitExceeded(
430:                 f"{len(records)} records exceeds this backend's configured "
431:                 f"atomic limit of {self._max_atomic_records} — refused before "
432:                 "any mutation, because a partially applied suffix is the one "
433:                 "artifact a replica must never hold"
434:             )
435:         try:
436:             landed, _mark = self._log.append_records(
437:                 [dict(record) for record in records], following=expected
438:             )
439:         except ForkedHeight as exc:
440:             raise SameHeightFork(str(exc)) from exc
441:         except StaleHead as exc:
442:             # 1:1 from the CAS subclass only, for the reason `append` gives:
443:             # the parent AppendRejected also covers placement faults, and
444:             # mapping those to HeadMismatch would assert something about the
445:             # head that the fault does not say.
446:             raise HeadMismatch(str(exc)) from exc
447: 
448:         first, last = landed[0], landed[-1]
449:         return Commit(
450:             before=Head(
451:                 lineage=first["lin"],
452:                 ordinal=first["ord"] - 1,
453:                 record_hash=first["prev"],
454:             ),
455:             records=tuple(landed),
456:             after=_head_of(last),
457:             durability=_DURABILITY,
458:         )
459: 
460:     def export(self, *, through: Head, codec: str) -> ExportedPrefix:
461:         """Re-encode the complete prefix behind a captured head (§08).
462: 
463:         Net-new over :meth:`scan` and
464:         :func:`engine.arrival.encode_record`, and it is deliberately thin:
465:         ``scan`` already refuses a head this log does not hold and already
466:         stops at the captured ordinal, so the export inherits both without
467:         restating either.
468: 
469:         **Streaming.** ``records`` is a generator, so nothing is materialised
470:         and nothing is read until it is drained — the same caveat
471:         :meth:`scan` carries, and the reason an export of a large lineage is
472:         runnable at all. Each element is one record's line INCLUDING its
473:         newline, so ``b"".join(...)`` reproduces the log's own prefix bytes
474:         exactly. The manifest says so rather than leaving it to be discovered.
475: 
476:         **The manifest carries no clock and no host.** Everything in it is
477:         derived from the captured head and the grammar, which is what makes
478:         export → import → export byte-identical rather than
479:         byte-identical-except-for-a-timestamp. ``count`` is
480:         ``through.ordinal + 1`` by density and needs no drain to compute — and
481:         the drain proves it, because a walk that found a gap would have
482:         refused before reaching the head.
483: 
484:         A codec this backend does not have is a caller bug against
485:         :meth:`capabilities`, not a contract refusal — the ratified set has no
486:         member for it, and inventing one would be the over-claim §12 exists to
487:         catch.
488:         """
489:         if codec != EXPORT_CODEC:
490:             raise ValueError(
491:                 f"this backend exports {EXPORT_CODEC!r} and nothing else, but "
492:                 f"{codec!r} was asked for — capabilities().export_codecs is "
493:                 "the list to check against"
494:             )
495: 
496:         def lines() -> Iterator[bytes]:
497:             for record in self.scan(through=through):
498:                 yield (encode_record(dict(record)) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
499: 
500:         return ExportedPrefix(
501:             head=through,
502:             codec=codec,
503:             records=lines(),
504:             manifest={
505:                 "protocol": GRAMMAR_VERSION,
506:                 "codec": codec,
507:                 "framing": _FRAMING,
508:                 "lineage": through.lineage,
509:                 "through_ordinal": through.ordinal,
510:                 "through_record_hash": through.record_hash,
511:                 "count": through.ordinal + 1,
512:             },
513:         )
514: 
515:     def import_prefix(self, prefix: ExportedPrefix) -> Head:
516:         """The §08-default portable import, and nothing beyond it.
517: 
518:         Two targets and no third: a log that does not exist yet, or one whose
519:         every record agrees exactly with the import through its own head. Any
520:         other target REFUSES. There is no merge arm here — content that has to
521:         be re-coordinated to fit is being admitted into another lineage, and
522:         admission is a different operation.
523: 
524:         Returns the target's :class:`~engine.arrival_contract.Head` after the
525:         import, and not a ``Commit``: an import into an empty replica has no
526:         ``before`` to name, and manufacturing one would be the first lie a
527:         replica told about where it came from.
528: 
529:         **The manifest is checked, never trusted.** It travels with the bytes,
530:         so it is exactly as trustworthy as they are; every field is
531:         re-derived from the decoded records and compared. A manifest that
532:         disagrees with its own records is a corrupt export, and reporting the
533:         disagreement is the whole reason to carry one.
534: 
535:         **Replica is not authority** (§08's callout). This method copies
536:         records; it grants nothing. A store that then accepts independent
537:         writes has forked, byte-identical start or not, and no flag here
538:         prevents that — custody does.
539: 
540:         The verified remainder is materialised, because it is handed to one
541:         atomic :meth:`replicate`. That is the honest limit of a MINIMAL
542:         importer: an import too large to hold is a resumable-transfer design,
543:         and this is not one.
544:         """
545:         if prefix.codec != EXPORT_CODEC:
546:             raise ValueError(
547:                 f"this backend imports {EXPORT_CODEC!r} and nothing else, but "
548:                 f"this export claims codec {prefix.codec!r}"
549:             )
550:         imported = _decoded(prefix)
551:         _refuse_disagreeing_manifest(prefix, imported)
552: 
553:         if not self._log.exists():
554:             # A new empty replica. Genesis cannot be appended onto a head that
555:             # is not there, and it must not be re-minted either: a replica
556:             # whose ordinal 0 differed by one byte would be a different
557:             # lineage wearing the same id.
558:             log = ArrivalLog.adopt_genesis(self._log.path, imported[0])
559:             self._log = log
560:             head = _head_of(log.genesis())
561:             if len(imported) == 1:
562:                 return head
563:             return self.replicate(head, imported[1:]).after
564: 
565:         head = self.head()
566:         self._refuse_disagreeing_prefix(imported, head)
567:         remainder = [
568:             record for record in imported if record["ord"] > head.ordinal
569:         ]
570:         if not remainder:
571:             # The import reaches exactly this target's head and agrees with it
572:             # the whole way. Nothing was missing — not a failure, and not a
573:             # no-op to hide. An import that stopped SHORT of the head never
574:             # gets here; it refuses above.
575:             return head
576:         return self.replicate(head, remainder).after
577: 
578:     def _refuse_disagreeing_prefix(
579:         self, imported: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]], head: Head
580:     ) -> None:
581:         """§08's exact-prefix-agreement gate for a non-empty target.
582: 
583:         Over :meth:`scan`, which is the read op that already establishes the
584:         target's prefix is intact — so this adds one comparison and no second
585:         traversal of its own. Position by position against the import, so the
586:         refusal names the ordinal the two disagree at rather than reporting
587:         that they differ somewhere.
588: 
589:         Distinct from the same-height fork :meth:`replicate` refuses: that one
590:         fires on an overlap it was HANDED, this one on the overlap it is about
591:         to SKIP. Both say the histories disagree at a height; skipping an
592:         overlap without checking it is how a replica silently acquires a
593:         prefix it never verified.
594: 
595:         **An import that ends BEFORE the target's head refuses.** §08 asks for
596:         agreement THROUGH the head, and a prefix that stops short structurally
597:         cannot establish that — there is nothing to compare the records above
598:         it against. Reporting success would be a verdict this operation has no
599:         evidence for: it would say "this target agrees with the import through
600:         its head" while never having looked at the heights in between. The
601:         length is therefore checked FIRST and explicitly, rather than left to a
602:         zip that would silently stop at the shorter side.
603:         """
604:         # Dense from 0 (the manifest check establishes both), so the target's
605:         # prefix is exactly this many records and the import must cover it.
606:         overlap = head.ordinal + 1
607:         if len(imported) < overlap:
608:             captured = imported[-1]
609:             raise HeadMismatch(
610:                 f"this import captures head ({captured['lin']}, "
611:                 f"{captured['ord']}, {captured['rh']}), which is behind "
612:                 f"{self._log.path}'s head ({head.lineage}, {head.ordinal}, "
613:                 f"{head.record_hash}) — §08 requires exact prefix agreement "
614:                 "THROUGH the target's head, and an import that stops short "
615:                 "cannot establish it. Export again at or past the target's head"
616:             )
617: 
618:         for mine, theirs in zip(
619:             self.scan(through=head), imported[:overlap], strict=True
620:         ):
621:             if mine["rh"] != theirs["rh"]:
622:                 raise SameHeightFork(
623:                     f"ordinal {mine['ord']} of {self._log.path} holds rh "
624:                     f"{mine['rh']}, but the import holds rh {theirs['rh']} at "
625:                     f"ordinal {theirs['ord']} — this import is not a continuation "
626:                     "of this log's history. Importing into a non-empty target "
627:                     "requires exact prefix agreement through its head"
628:                 )
629: 
630:     # -- reads through the ledger ------------------------------------------
631: 
632:     def head(self, lineage: str | None = None) -> Head:
633:         """The currently complete head.
634: 
635:         Absence and corruption surface as this backend's own
636:         ``GenesisRefused`` / ``ArrivalCorrupt`` — see :meth:`mint` for why
637:         they are not translated. A ``lineage`` that is not this log's IS one
638:         of the ratified refusals: asking a ledger about a lineage it does not
639:         hold is an operation it may not perform.
640:         """
641:         record = self._log.head()
642:         if lineage is not None and record["lin"] != lineage:
643:             raise NotAuthority(
644:                 f"{self._log.path} holds lineage {record['lin']}, not the "
645:                 f"requested {lineage} — this ledger is not that lineage's "
646:                 "authority, and opening a path never makes it one"
647:             )
648:         return _head_of(record)
649: 
650:     def head_at(self, watermark: Watermark) -> Head:
651:         """The full head a projection's watermark names.
652: 
653:         The resolution §07 needs and the query half cannot perform: a
654:         watermark is a coordinate, and only the ledger holds the record whose
655:         hash completes it. It answers or it refuses — a watermark the log
656:         will not vouch for is a disagreement between projection and ledger,
657:         and answering it with a manufactured head would hide exactly that.
658:         """
659:         record = self._log.read(watermark.ordinal)
660:         if record["lin"] != watermark.lineage:
661:             raise NotAuthority(
662:                 f"the projection reports lineage {watermark.lineage}, but "
663:                 f"{self._log.path} holds {record['lin']} — the projection is "
664:                 "not a projection of this log"
665:             )
666:         return _head_of(record)
667: 
668:     def read(self, coordinate: int) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
669:         """The exact record, after establishing its membership in the lineage.
670: 
671:         Membership is not a lookup: the walk that reaches the coordinate has
672:         verified that everything before it chains, because a record whose
673:         predecessors do not chain is not at the coordinate it claims.
674:         """
675:         return self._log.read(coordinate)
676: 
677:     def scan(
678:         self, *, after: int | None = None, through: Head | None = None
679:     ) -> Iterator[Mapping[str, Any]]:
680:         """An ordered, consistent prefix range and no later record (§06).
681: 
682:         ``through`` is a CAPTURED head, and capturing is what makes the range
683:         a snapshot: the record found at that ordinal must be the one the
684:         caller captured, or the prefix it is asking for is not the prefix
685:         this log has. Absence before the captured head is corruption and not
686:         end of stream, so a walk that ends early refuses rather than
687:         returning short.
688: 
689:         **This is a generator, so calling it checks nothing** — the same
690:         caveat :meth:`engine.arrival.ArrivalLog.walk` carries, and for the
691:         same reason. Every check below runs as records are pulled.
692:         """
693:         floor = -1 if after is None else after
694:         reached = through is None
695:         for record in self._log.walk():
696:             if through is not None and record["ord"] == through.ordinal:
697:                 if (
698:                     record["lin"] != through.lineage
699:                     or record["rh"] != through.record_hash
700:                 ):
701:                     raise HeadMismatch(
702:                         f"ordinal {through.ordinal} of {self._log.path} holds "
703:                         f"{record['lin']}/{record['rh']}, not the captured "
704:                         f"{through.lineage}/{through.record_hash} — the "
705:                         "snapshot this scan was asked for is not this log's"
706:                     )
707:                 reached = True
708:             if record["ord"] > floor:
709:                 yield record
710:             if through is not None and record["ord"] >= through.ordinal:
711:                 break
712:         if not reached:
713:             assert through is not None
714:             raise HeadMismatch(
715:                 f"{self._log.path} ends before ordinal {through.ordinal} — "
716:                 "absence before a captured head is corruption, not end of "
717:                 "stream"
718:             )
719: 
720:     def verify(self, scope: VerifyScope) -> Head:
721:         """Verify through a named head; return the head the claim covers.
722: 
723:         **Verification reports; it never repairs.** Nothing here takes the
724:         append lock, and the lock is the only thing that licenses truncating
725:         a torn tail — so no path through this method can rewrite the log it
726:         was asked to judge. (§06 states that as a contract MUST as of
727:         ``decision:design/arrival-slice2-contract-text`` ruling 1; this
728:         adapter held it before the ruling, because the alternative is
729:         reporting an agreement it just manufactured.)
730: 
731:         ``Incremental`` is NOT offered, and :meth:`capabilities` says so. A
732:         verified suffix walk has to start somewhere, and this backend starts
733:         one from a resume mark's byte offset — which a :class:`Head` does not
734:         carry. Finding the checkpoint's position would mean walking to it,
735:         making "incremental" the same work as ``Full`` under a name that
736:         promises less. An honest absent level beats a level that lies about
737:         its cost.
738:         """
739:         if isinstance(scope, Open):
740:             # Genesis and the adopted head record — §06's Open level exactly.
741:             # `_tail_record` and not the public `head()`: `head()` reaches its
742:             # answer through a full walk, which would make this level a Full
743:             # verification wearing an Open label. Reading the tail validates
744:             # the genesis and the head record it adopts, and truncates
745:             # nothing (that lives behind the lock, which this never takes).
746:             self._log.genesis()
747:             return _head_of(self._log._tail_record())
748: 
749:         if isinstance(scope, Incremental):
750:             raise NotSupported(
751:                 "the file adapter offers OPEN and FULL verification only — a "
752:                 "verified suffix walk starts from a resume mark's byte "
753:                 "offset, and a Head does not carry one. capabilities() "
754:                 "reports the two levels it actually has"
755:             )
756: 
757:         if not isinstance(scope, Full):
758:             raise TypeError(f"not a verification scope: {scope!r}")
759: 
760:         # Grammar, density, lineage and the hash chain for the complete named
761:         # prefix. `walk` is consumed through that head, then stopped: Full(H)
762:         # makes no claim about a later concurrently appended or corrupted tail.
763:         found: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None
764:         for record in self._log.walk():
765:             if record["ord"] == scope.through.ordinal:
766:                 found = record
767:                 break
768:         if found is None:
769:             raise HeadMismatch(
770:                 f"{self._log.path} holds no record at ordinal "
771:                 f"{scope.through.ordinal} — the head this verification was "
772:                 "asked about is not in this log"
773:             )
774:         head = _head_of(found)
775:         if head != scope.through:
776:             raise HeadMismatch(
777:                 f"ordinal {scope.through.ordinal} verifies as {head}, not the "
778:                 f"claimed {scope.through}"
779:             )
780:         return head
781: 
782:     def capabilities(self) -> Capabilities:
783:         """What this backend actually offers — no more (§12).
784: 
785:         Deployment tooling refuses an assignment whose required guarantees are
786:         absent, so an over-claim here is worse than a missing feature: it turns
787:         a refusal into a runtime failure.
788: 
789:         ``REPLICA`` joins ``AUTHORITY`` because :meth:`replicate` now exists —
790:         the profile names what a store may be ASKED to do, and an adapter that
791:         can consume pre-coordinated records without assigning any is what makes
792:         the replica role performable. ``ARCHIVE`` stays absent: nothing here
793:         offers a read-only sealed mode, and claiming one would be exactly the
794:         lie this report exists to make catchable.
795: 
796:         The codec tuple grows to what :meth:`export` will actually produce, and
797:         to nothing else. A test cross-checks both claims against the object.
798:         """
799:         return Capabilities(
800:             protocol_version=GRAMMAR_VERSION,
801:             profiles=frozenset({Profile.AUTHORITY, Profile.REPLICA}),
802:             durability=DurabilityProfile.HOST,
803:             verification_levels=frozenset(
804:                 {VerificationLevel.OPEN, VerificationLevel.FULL}
805:             ),
806:             writer_concurrency=(
807:                 "multi-process on one host, advisory flock; LOCAL POSIX "
808:                 "storage only — a store on NFS or another network filesystem "
809:                 "is out of contract"
810:             ),
811:             snapshot=(
812:                 "captured-head prefix; readers take no lock and see only "
813:                 "newline-terminated records, so an append in flight is "
814:                 "invisible rather than partial"
815:             ),
816:             watermark=(
817:                 "the projection reports a (lineage, ordinal) coordinate; the "
818:                 "ledger attests the head at it"
819:             ),
820:             max_atomic_records=self._max_atomic_records,
821:             idempotency_keys=False,
822:             export_codecs=(EXPORT_CODEC,),
823:             limits=(),
824:         )
825: 
826: 
827: def _meta(index_path: Path, key: str) -> str | None:
828:     """One ``store_meta`` value, through a connection that cannot write.
829: 
830:     Opened per call rather than held: the watermark advances as the
831:     projection consumes, so a cached answer would be a stale claim about
832:     freshness, which is the one thing a watermark must never be. Read-only by
833:     URI, so this path cannot repair what it is reporting on even by accident.
834:     """
835:     if not index_path.exists():
836:         return None
837:     conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{index_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
838:     try:
839:         row = conn.execute(
840:             "SELECT value FROM store_meta WHERE key = ?", (key,)
841:         ).fetchone()
842:     except sqlite3.OperationalError:
843:         return None  # no store_meta table: an index that has never consumed
844:     finally:
845:         conn.close()
846:     return None if row is None else row[0]
847: 
848: 
849: def _snapshot_meta(conn: sqlite3.Connection, key: str) -> str | None:
850:     """Read projection metadata on the same transaction as its rows."""
851:     try:
852:         row = conn.execute(
853:             "SELECT value FROM store_meta WHERE key = ?", (key,)
854:         ).fetchone()
855:     except sqlite3.OperationalError:
856:         return None
857:     return None if row is None else row[0]
858:

885: 
886: class _FileQuerySnapshot:
887:     """One SQLite read transaction, bounded to a captured Arrival prefix.
888: 
889:     The snapshot deliberately works below ``StoreReader``: that class's public
890:     page API has no captured-head bound.  The legacy reader remains available
891:     on :class:`FileQuery`; this private implementation is the new portable
892:     surface and never exposes its connection.
893:     """
894: 
895:     def __init__(
896:         self,
897:         path: Path,
898:         *,
899:         captured_head: Head,
900:         requirement: ProjectionRequirement,
901:         continuation: Continuation | None,
902:     ) -> None:
903:         self._path = path
904:         self._captured_head = captured_head
905:         self._conn = sqlite3.connect(
906:             f"{path.absolute().as_uri()}?mode=ro", uri=True
907:         )
908:         self._conn.execute("PRAGMA query_only=ON")
909:         self._conn.execute("BEGIN DEFERRED")
910:         self._closed = False
911:         try:
912:             self._fact_signature_column = self._has_column("facts", "signature")
913:             self._tick_chain_columns = {
914:                 row[1] for row in self._conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(ticks)")
915:             }
916:             lineage = _snapshot_meta(self._conn, ARRIVAL_LINEAGE_KEY)
917:             ordinal = _snapshot_meta(self._conn, ARRIVAL_ORDINAL_KEY)
918:             if lineage is None or ordinal is None:
919:                 raise ProjectionAbsent(f"{path} has no complete projection watermark")
920:             watermark = Watermark(lineage=lineage, ordinal=int(ordinal))
921:             if watermark.lineage != captured_head.lineage:
922:                 raise NotAuthority(
923:                     f"projection at {path} represents {watermark.lineage}, not "
924:                     f"captured lineage {captured_head.lineage}"
925:                 )
926:             if continuation is not None:
927:                 if continuation.captured_head != captured_head:
928:                     raise InvalidContinuation(
929:                         "continuation captured head differs from this read"
930:                     )
931:                 if continuation.projected_through.lineage != captured_head.lineage:
932:                     raise InvalidContinuation(
933:                         "continuation represented another lineage"
934:                     )
935:                 if watermark.ordinal < continuation.projected_through.ordinal:
936:                     raise InvalidContinuation(
937:                         "projection no longer reaches the continuation prefix"
938:                     )
939:                 if (
940:                     requirement is ProjectionRequirement.CURRENT
941:                     and continuation.projected_through.ordinal < captured_head.ordinal
942:                 ):
943:                     raise ProjectionBehind(
944:                         f"continuation prefix ends at "
945:                         f"{continuation.projected_through.ordinal}, but the "
946:                         f"captured head is {captured_head.ordinal}"
947:                     )
948:                 bound = continuation.projected_through.ordinal
949:             elif watermark.ordinal < captured_head.ordinal:
950:                 if requirement is ProjectionRequirement.CURRENT:
951:                     raise ProjectionBehind(
952:                         f"projection at {path} ends at {watermark.ordinal}, but "
953:                         f"the captured head is {captured_head.ordinal}"
954:                     )
955:                 bound = watermark.ordinal
956:             else:
957:                 # A watermark beyond H may be a normal append/catch-up after H
958:                 # was captured. The consumer validates its membership and
959:                 # clamps the externally reported basis to H.
960:                 bound = captured_head.ordinal
961:             self._bound = Watermark(lineage=captured_head.lineage, ordinal=bound)
962:             self._observed_watermark = watermark
963:             self._declaration_anchor = self._read_declaration_anchor()
964:             self._continuation = continuation
965:             self._view_generation = self._generation(bound)
966:             if (
967:                 continuation is not None
968:                 and continuation.view_generation != self._view_generation
969:             ):
970:                 raise InvalidContinuation(
971:                     "projection view changed since this continuation was issued"
972:                 )
973:         except BaseException:
974:             self.close()
975:             raise
976: 
977:     @property
978:     def represented(self) -> Watermark:
979:         """The actual watermark read in this transaction, before any clamp."""
980:         return self._observed_watermark
981: 
982:     @property
983:     def view_generation(self) -> str:
984:         return self._view_generation
985: 
986:     @property
987:     def observed_watermark(self) -> Watermark:
988:         """The actual projection mark, retained for coordinator validation."""
989:         return self._observed_watermark
990: 
991:     @property
992:     def declaration_anchor(self) -> DeclarationAnchor:
993:         return self._declaration_anchor
994: 
995:     def _read_declaration_anchor(self) -> DeclarationAnchor:
996:         """Read the marker and its exact genesis without inferring identity."""
997:         own_lineage = _snapshot_meta(self._conn, "own_lineage")
998:         if own_lineage is None:
999:             return DeclarationAnchor(own_lineage=None, genesis=None)
1000:         try:
1001:             row = self._conn.execute(
1002:                 "SELECT " + self._fact_select() + " FROM facts "
1003:                 "WHERE id = ? AND kind = '_decl.genesis'",
1004:                 (own_lineage,),
1005:             ).fetchone()
1006:         except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
1007:             raise ProjectionAbsent(
1008:                 f"{self._path} cannot read declaration identity: {exc}"
1009:             ) from exc
1010:         return DeclarationAnchor(
1011:             own_lineage=own_lineage,
1012:             genesis=None if row is None else self._fact(row),
1013:         )
1014: 
1015:     def _has_column(self, table: str, column: str) -> bool:
1016:         columns = {row[1] for row in self._conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})")}
1017:         return column in columns
1018: 
1019:     def _fact_select(self) -> str:
1020:         columns = "id, kind, ts, observer, origin, payload, arrival_ordinal, arrival_seq"
1021:         return columns + (", signature" if self._fact_signature_column else "")
1022: 
1023:     def _tick_select(self) -> str:
1024:         columns = [
1025:             "id", "name", "ts", "since", "origin", "payload",
1026:             "arrival_ordinal", "arrival_seq",
1027:         ]
1028:         for column in ("prev_hash", "window_start", "fact_cursor", "window_hash", "signature"):
1029:             columns.append(column if column in self._tick_chain_columns else f"NULL AS {column}")
1030:         return ", ".join(columns)
1031: 
1032:     def _generation(self, bound: int) -> str:
1033:         """Opaque identity for this file projection through ``bound``.
1034: 
1035:         SQLite offers no durable projection-generation token. A digest of the
1036:         snapshot's schema, declaration identity, and complete bounded row
1037:         content makes a conservative token: maintenance or row changes
1038:         invalidate a resume even when its ledger prefix remains available.
1039:         """
1040:         digest = hashlib.sha256()
1041:         schema_version = self._conn.execute("PRAGMA schema_version").fetchone()[0]
1042:         genesis = self._declaration_anchor.genesis
1043:         anchor = {
1044:             "own_lineage": self._declaration_anchor.own_lineage,
1045:             "genesis": None
1046:             if genesis is None
1047:             else {
1048:                 "id": genesis.id,
1049:                 "kind": genesis.kind,
1050:                 "ts": genesis.ts,
1051:                 "observer": genesis.observer,
1052:                 "origin": genesis.origin,
1053:                 "payload": genesis.payload,
1054:                 "arrival_ordinal": genesis.arrival_ordinal,
1055:                 "arrival_seq": genesis.arrival_seq,
1056:             },
1057:         }
1058:         digest.update(
1059:             f"schema:{schema_version}:bound:{bound}:".encode()
1060:         )
1061:         digest.update(json.dumps(anchor, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode())
1062:         for table, columns in (
1063:             (
1064:                 "facts",
1065:                 self._fact_select(),
1066:             ),
1067:             (
1068:                 "ticks",
1069:                 self._tick_select(),
1070:             ),
1071:         ):
1072:             try:
1073:                 rows = self._conn.execute(
1074:                     f"SELECT {columns} FROM {table} WHERE arrival_ordinal <= ? "
1075:                     "ORDER BY arrival_ordinal, arrival_seq",
1076:                     (bound,),
1077:                 )
1078:             except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
1079:                 raise ProjectionAbsent(
1080:                     f"{self._path} cannot answer projected {table}: {exc}"
1081:                 ) from exc
1082:             digest.update(table.encode())
1083:             for row in rows:
1084:                 digest.update(
1085:                     json.dumps(row, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode()
1086:                 )
1087:                 digest.update(b"\0")
1088:         return f"file-projection-v1:{digest.hexdigest()}"
1089: 
1090:     @staticmethod
1091:     def _fact(row: tuple[Any, ...]) -> Fact:
1092:         return Fact(
1093:             id=row[0], kind=row[1], ts=float(row[2]), observer=row[3], origin=row[4],
1094:             payload=json.loads(row[5]), arrival_ordinal=int(row[6]), arrival_seq=int(row[7]),
1095:             payload_text=row[5], signature=row[8] if len(row) > 8 else None,
1096:         )
1097: 
1098:     @staticmethod
1099:     def _tick(row: tuple[Any, ...]) -> Tick:
1100:         return Tick(
1101:             id=row[0],
1102:             name=row[1],
1103:             ts=float(row[2]),
1104:             since=None if row[3] is None else float(row[3]),
1105:             origin=row[4],
1106:             payload=json.loads(row[5]),
1107:             arrival_ordinal=int(row[6]),
1108:             arrival_seq=int(row[7]),
1109:             payload_text=row[5],
1110:             prev_hash=row[8],
1111:             window_start=row[9],
1112:             fact_cursor=row[10],
1113:             window_hash=row[11],
1114:             signature=row[12],
1115:         )
1116: 
1117:     def facts(self, request: FactRequest) -> FactPage:
1118:         if request.order not in ("newest", "oldest"):
1119:             raise ValueError(f"facts order must be 'newest' or 'oldest', got {request.order!r}")
1120:         if request.limit is not None and request.limit < 1:
1121:             raise ValueError("facts limit must be >= 1 or None")
1122:         if self._continuation is not None and request != self._continuation.request:
1123:             raise InvalidContinuation("continuation request does not match this facts request")
1124: 
1125:         clauses = ["arrival_ordinal <= ?"]
1126:         params: list[Any] = [self._bound.ordinal]
1127:         if request.kind is not None:
1128:             from .sql_util import kind_subtree_predicate
1129: 
1130:             kind_sql, kind_params = kind_subtree_predicate(request.kind)
1131:             clauses.append(kind_sql)
1132:             params.extend(kind_params)
1133:         if request.observer is not None:
1134:             if "/" in request.observer:
1135:                 clauses.append("(observer = ? OR observer = ?)")
1136:                 params.extend((request.observer, request.observer.rsplit("/", 1)[1]))
1137:             else:
1138:                 tail = "/" + request.observer
1139:                 clauses.append("(observer = ? OR substr(observer, -?, ?) = ?)")
1140:                 params.extend((request.observer, len(tail), len(tail), tail))
1141:         if not request.include_internal:
1142:             clauses.append("kind NOT GLOB '_decl.*'")
1143:         if self._continuation is not None:
1144:             cursor = self._continuation.cursor
1145:             # A page is a hard row bound, so resume at the complete receipt
1146:             # coordinate.  One packed Arrival record can contribute rows to
1147:             # several pages; custody remains atomic at the ledger layer.
1148:             if request.order == "newest":
1149:                 clauses.append(
1150:                     "(arrival_ordinal < ? OR "
1151:                     "(arrival_ordinal = ? AND (arrival_seq < ? OR "
1152:                     "(arrival_seq = ? AND id < ?))))"
1153:                 )
1154:             else:
1155:                 clauses.append(
1156:                     "(arrival_ordinal > ? OR "
1157:                     "(arrival_ordinal = ? AND (arrival_seq > ? OR "
1158:                     "(arrival_seq = ? AND id > ?))))"
1159:                 )
1160:             params.extend(
1161:                 (
1162:                     cursor.arrival_ordinal,
1163:                     cursor.arrival_ordinal,
1164:                     cursor.arrival_seq,
1165:                     cursor.arrival_seq,
1166:                     cursor.fact_id,
1167:                 )
1168:             )
1169:         if request.fact_id is not None:
1170:             # Preserve the established lookup rule: an exact visible ID wins
1171:             # even when other IDs extend it. Only when no exact row survives
1172:             # this request's bound, filters, and cursor is the value a prefix.
1173:             exact_sql = (
1174:                 "SELECT "
1175:                 + self._fact_select()
1176:                 + " FROM facts WHERE "
1177:                 + " AND ".join((*clauses, "id = ?"))
1178:                 + " LIMIT 1"
1179:             )
1180:             exact = self._conn.execute(
1181:                 exact_sql, (*params, request.fact_id)
1182:             ).fetchone()
1183:             if exact is not None:
1184:                 return FactPage(
1185:                     items=(self._fact(exact),),
1186:                     cursor=None,
1187:                     truncated=False,
1188:                     order=request.order,
1189:                 )
1190:             # IDs are arbitrary strings. Compare their UTF-8 bytes literally
1191:             # so Unicode, NUL, and LIKE/GLOB metacharacters remain ordinary ID
1192:             # content rather than depending on a sentinel alphabet or pattern
1193:             # escaping convention.
1194:             clauses.append(
1195:                 "substr(CAST(id AS BLOB), 1, length(CAST(? AS BLOB))) "
1196:                 "= CAST(? AS BLOB)"
1197:             )
1198:             params.extend((request.fact_id, request.fact_id))
1199: 
1200:         direction = "DESC" if request.order == "newest" else "ASC"
1201:         sql = (
1202:             "SELECT " + self._fact_select() + " FROM facts WHERE " + " AND ".join(clauses) +
1203:             f" ORDER BY arrival_ordinal {direction}, arrival_seq {direction}, id {direction}"
1204:         )
1205:         if request.limit is None:
1206:             rows = self._conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
1207:             return FactPage(
1208:                 items=tuple(self._fact(row) for row in rows), cursor=None,
1209:                 truncated=False, order=request.order,
1210:             )
1211: 
1212:         # Fetch one look-ahead row.  Unlike ledger/export operations, a query
1213:         # page does not preserve a whole Arrival record: ``limit`` is a strict
1214:         # maximum number of projected fact rows.
1215:         rows = self._conn.execute(sql + " LIMIT ?", (*params, request.limit + 1)).fetchall()
1216:         more = len(rows) > request.limit
1217:         page_rows = rows[:request.limit]
1218:         cursor = None
1219:         if more:
1220:             last = page_rows[-1]
1221:             cursor = FactCursor(int(last[6]), int(last[7]), last[0])
1222:         return FactPage(
1223:             items=tuple(self._fact(row) for row in page_rows), cursor=cursor,
1224:             truncated=more, order=request.order,
1225:         )
1226: 
1227:     def ticks(self, request: TickRequest) -> tuple[Tick, ...]:
1228:         clauses = ["arrival_ordinal <= ?", "ts >= ?", "ts <= ?"]
1229:         params: list[Any] = [self._bound.ordinal, request.since, request.until]
1230:         if request.name is not None:
1231:             clauses.append("name = ?")
1232:             params.append(request.name)
1233:         rows = self._conn.execute(
1234:             "SELECT " + self._tick_select() + " FROM ticks WHERE "
1235:             + " AND ".join(clauses)
1236:             + " ORDER BY ts, arrival_ordinal, arrival_seq",
1237:             params,
1238:         ).fetchall()
1239:         return tuple(self._tick(row) for row in rows)
1240: 
1241:     def summary(self, request: SummaryRequest) -> Summary:
1242:         internal = "" if request.include_internal else " AND kind NOT GLOB '_decl.*'"
1243:         fact_total = self._conn.execute(
1244:             "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM facts WHERE arrival_ordinal <= ?" + internal,
1245:             (self._bound.ordinal,),
1246:         ).fetchone()[0]
1247:         tick_total = self._conn.execute(
1248:             "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ticks WHERE arrival_ordinal <= ?",
1249:             (self._bound.ordinal,),
1250:         ).fetchone()[0]
1251:         fact_rows = self._conn.execute(
1252:             "SELECT kind, COUNT(*), MIN(ts), MAX(ts) FROM facts "
1253:             "WHERE arrival_ordinal <= ?" + internal + " GROUP BY kind",
1254:             (self._bound.ordinal,),
1255:         ).fetchall()
1256:         tick_rows = self._conn.execute(
1257:             "SELECT name, COUNT(*), MIN(ts), MAX(ts) FROM ticks "
1258:             "WHERE arrival_ordinal <= ? GROUP BY name",
1259:             (self._bound.ordinal,),
1260:         ).fetchall()
1261:         signed_count = 0
1262:         columns = {row[1] for row in self._conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(facts)")}
1263:         if "signature" in columns:
1264:             signed_count = int(self._conn.execute(
1265:                 "SELECT COUNT(signature) FROM facts WHERE arrival_ordinal <= ?" + internal,
1266:                 (self._bound.ordinal,),
1267:             ).fetchone()[0])
1268:         return Summary(
1269:             fact_total=int(fact_total), tick_total=int(tick_total),
1270:             signed_count=signed_count, unsigned_count=int(fact_total) - signed_count,
1271:             fact_kinds={
1272:                 row[0]: {"count": row[1], "earliest": row[2], "latest": row[3]}
1273:                 for row in fact_rows
1274:             },
1275:             tick_names={
1276:                 row[0]: {"count": row[1], "earliest": row[2], "latest": row[3]}
1277:                 for row in tick_rows
1278:             },
1279:         )
1280: 
1281:     def _search_coverage(self) -> tuple[Head, str, str] | None:
1282:         try:
1283:             rows = self._conn.execute(
1284:                 "SELECT key, value FROM arrival_fts_state"
1285:             ).fetchall()
1286:         except sqlite3.OperationalError:
1287:             return None
1288:         state = {str(key): str(value) for key, value in rows}
1289:         try:
1290:             head = Head(
1291:                 state["lineage"], int(state["ordinal"]), state["record_hash"]
1292:             )
1293:             fields_hash = state["fields_hash"]
1294:             schema_token = state["schema_version"]
1295:         except (KeyError, ValueError):
1296:             return None
1297:         actual_schema = str(self._conn.execute("PRAGMA schema_version").fetchone()[0])
1298:         if schema_token != actual_schema:
1299:             return None
1300:         return head, fields_hash, schema_token
1301: 
1302:     def search(self, request: SearchRequest) -> SearchPage:
1303:         """Run FTS5 only when its exact corpus is this snapshot's head."""
1304:         if request.limit < 1:
1305:             raise ValueError("search limit must be >= 1")
1306:         coverage = self._search_coverage()
1307:         if coverage is None:
1308:             raise SearchStale("file search coverage is absent or schema-invalid")
1309:         ranking_through, fields_hash, _schema_token = coverage
1310:         if ranking_through != self._captured_head:
1311:             raise SearchStale(
1312:                 "file search corpus does not exactly match this captured head"
1313:             )
1314:         if fields_hash != request.expected_fields_hash:
1315:             raise SearchStale(
1316:                 "file search coverage was built for different declared fields"
1317:             )
1318: 
1319:         clauses = [
1320:             "arrival_facts_fts MATCH ?",
1321:             "f.arrival_ordinal <= ?",
1322:         ]
1323:         params: list[Any] = [request.expression, self._bound.ordinal]
1324:         if request.kind is not None:
1325:             from .sql_util import kind_subtree_predicate
1326: 
1327:             kind_sql, kind_params = kind_subtree_predicate(request.kind, "f.kind")
1328:             clauses.append(kind_sql)
1329:             params.extend(kind_params)
1330:         if request.observer is not None:
1331:             clauses.append("f.observer = ?")
1332:             params.append(request.observer)
1333:         if request.since is not None:
1334:             clauses.append("f.ts >= ?")
1335:             params.append(request.since)
1336:         if request.until is not None:
1337:             clauses.append("f.ts <= ?")
1338:             params.append(request.until)
1339:         if not request.include_internal:
1340:             clauses.append("f.kind NOT GLOB '_decl.*'")
1341:         where = " AND ".join(clauses)
1342:         joined = (
1343:             " FROM arrival_facts_fts JOIN facts f "
1344:             "ON f.id = arrival_facts_fts.fact_id WHERE " + where
1345:         )
1346:         total = int(self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*)" + joined, params).fetchone()[0])
1347:         rows = self._conn.execute(
1348:             "SELECT " + self._fact_select() + ", "
1349:             "bm25(arrival_facts_fts), "
1350:             "snippet(arrival_facts_fts, 0, '[', ']', '…', 16)"
1351:             + joined
1352:             + " ORDER BY bm25(arrival_facts_fts), f.arrival_ordinal DESC, "
1353:             "f.arrival_seq DESC, f.id DESC LIMIT ?",
1354:             (*params, request.limit + 1),
1355:         ).fetchall()
1356:         truncated = len(rows) > request.limit
1357:         matches = tuple(
1358:             SearchMatch(
1359:                 fact=self._fact(row[:-2]), rank=float(row[-2]), snippet=row[-1]
1360:             )
1361:             for row in rows[:request.limit]
1362:         )
1363:         return SearchPage(
1364:             matches=matches,
1365:             total_matches=total,
1366:             truncated=truncated,
1367:             ranking="sqlite-fts5-bm25",
1368:             ranking_through=ranking_through,
1369:             fields_hash=fields_hash,
1370:         )
1371: 
1372:     def close(self) -> None:
1373:         if self._closed:
1374:             return
1375:         self._closed = True
1376:         try:
1377:             self._conn.rollback()
1378:         finally:
1379:             self._conn.close()
1380: 
1381: 
1382: class FileQuery:
1383:     """Reads over the projection, with no route back into custody.
1384: 
1385:     Constructed from an index PATH, and it builds its own read handle. That
1386:     is the separation stated as construction rather than as discipline:
1387:     there is no parameter through which an :class:`ArrivalLog` or an
1388:     ``ArrivalStore`` could be passed in, so there is no instance from which
1389:     an append could be reached — including by a future edit that adds a
1390:     convenience the author did not think through. The reader it builds is
1391:     :class:`engine.store_reader.StoreReader`, whose connection is opened
1392:     ``PRAGMA query_only=ON``.
1393: 
1394:     :attr:`reader` is the row-shaped read surface, deliberately left as this
1395:     backend's own rather than declared on
1396:     :class:`engine.arrival_contract.ArrivalQuery`. One adapter is not a
1397:     pattern, and a neutral spelling of "give me the facts" invented against a
1398:     single implementation would be an invention, not a contract.
1399: 
1400:     **The reader is built on first use, not at construction** (slice 3 §0.4).
1401:     It used to be built eagerly, and ``StoreReader`` refuses a path that does
1402:     not exist — so a store whose projection had never been materialised could
1403:     not be opened through the registry AT ALL, even though its ledger half was
1404:     perfectly openable. That blocked ``mint`` through the registry, which is
1405:     the path slice 4's sidecar takes to get its bootstrap receipt, and it sat
1406:     against the ratified F2 carve-out, which explicitly anticipates an absent
1407:     projection ("materialising a projection that does not yet exist is not
1408:     repair"). Deferring the construction is the whole fix: **opening** stops
1409:     requiring a projection, while **asking for rows** still refuses honestly
1410:     with the same ``FileNotFoundError`` from the same place. Nothing here
1411:     creates an index — permitted is not required, and creating one on the way
1412:     to a read would be the adapter deciding a materialisation policy that
1413:     belongs to whoever asked.
1414:     """
1415: 
1416:     def __init__(self, index_path: Path | str) -> None:
1417:         self._path = Path(index_path)
1418:         self._reader: StoreReader | None = None
1419: 
1420:     @property
1421:     def reader(self) -> StoreReader:
1422:         """The row-shaped read surface, built on first access and then held.
1423: 
1424:         Held rather than rebuilt per call, unlike :func:`_meta`'s connection:
1425:         that one is re-opened every time because a cached watermark would be a
1426:         stale claim about freshness, which is the one thing a watermark must
1427:         never be. A row reader has no such obligation — it answers about rows,
1428:         not about how far it has consumed — so one handle per query object is
1429:         the same lifetime it had when this was an attribute.
1430:         """
1431:         if self._reader is None:
1432:             self._reader = StoreReader(self._path)
1433:         return self._reader
1434: 
1435:     def lineage(self) -> str | None:
1436:         """The lineage this projection represents, or None when it holds none.
1437: 
1438:         §07: query results report the lineage they actually represent. A
1439:         fresh index that has consumed nothing represents no lineage, and
1440:         saying so is different from guessing at the log's.
1441:         """
1442:         return _meta(self._path, ARRIVAL_LINEAGE_KEY)
1443: 
1444:     def projected_through(self) -> Watermark | None:
1445:         """How much of the lineage this projection accounts for (§07).
1446: 
1447:         A :class:`~engine.arrival_contract.Watermark` and not a ``Head``:
1448:         this projection stores a coordinate, not a record hash — see the
1449:         Watermark docstring, and ``finding:slice2-wp1-projection-has-no-head
1450:         -hash`` for why closing that gap is not WP1's to invent. Resolving it
1451:         to a verified head is :meth:`FileLedger.head_at`.
1452: 
1453:         Both fields or nothing. A partial mark is not a position.
1454:         """
1455:         lineage = _meta(self._path, ARRIVAL_LINEAGE_KEY)
1456:         ordinal = _meta(self._path, ARRIVAL_ORDINAL_KEY)
1457:         if lineage is None or ordinal is None:
1458:             return None
1459:         return Watermark(lineage=lineage, ordinal=int(ordinal))
1460: 
1461:     def open_snapshot(
1462:         self,
1463:         *,
1464:         captured_head: Head,
1465:         requirement: ProjectionRequirement,
1466:         continuation: Continuation | None = None,
1467:     ) -> QuerySnapshot:
1468:         """Open a read-only SQLite snapshot bounded by ``captured_head``.
1469: 
1470:         No projection is created or repaired here. A missing index is an
1471:         explicit current-read refusal, or an empty allow-behind snapshot that
1472:         carries no represented watermark for diagnostics.
1473:         """
1474:         if not self._path.exists():
1475:             if requirement is ProjectionRequirement.CURRENT:
1476:                 raise ProjectionAbsent(f"{self._path} does not exist")
1477:             return _AbsentFileQuerySnapshot()
1478:         return _FileQuerySnapshot(
1479:             self._path,
1480:             captured_head=captured_head,
1481:             requirement=requirement,
1482:             continuation=continuation,
1483:         )
1484: 
1485:     def close(self) -> None:
1486:         """Close the read handle this query built, if it ever built one.
1487: 
1488:         Closing must not be the thing that CONSTRUCTS a reader — a query opened
1489:         over an absent projection and closed without being read would then
1490:         raise from ``close()``, turning the lazy fix into a refusal moved to a
1491:         stranger place. So this consults the field rather than the property.
1492:         """
1493:         if self._reader is not None:
1494:             self._reader.close()
1495:             self._reader = None
1496: 
1497: 
1498: class FileProjectionMaintenance:
1499:     """Explicit, bounded catch-up for the file adapter's SQLite projection.
1500: 
1501:     Construction performs no I/O. ``catch_up`` validates the requested full
1502:     head against the log before opening a write transaction, then re-reads the
1503:     projection mark under ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` so concurrent maintainers
1504:     serialize on the projection itself. Existing rows and identity markers are
1505:     never discarded or replaced.
1506:     """
1507: 
1508:     def __init__(self, log_path: Path | str, index_path: Path | str) -> None:
1509:         self._log = ArrivalLog(log_path)
1510:         self._path = Path(index_path)
1511:         self._closed = False
1512: 
1513:     def capabilities(self) -> MaintenanceCapabilities:
1514:         return MaintenanceCapabilities(catch_up=True, rebuild=False)
1515: 
1516:     @staticmethod
1517:     def _tables(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> set[str]:
1518:         return {
1519:             str(row[0])
1520:             for row in conn.execute(
1521:                 "SELECT name FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table'"
1522:             )
1523:         }
1524: 
1525:     @staticmethod
1526:     def _read_mark(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> ResumeMark | None:
1527:         values = (
1528:             _meta_get(conn, ARRIVAL_LINEAGE_KEY),
1529:             _meta_get(conn, ARRIVAL_OFFSET_KEY),
1530:             _meta_get(conn, ARRIVAL_ORDINAL_KEY),
1531:         )
1532:         if values == (None, None, None):
1533:             return None
1534:         if any(value is None for value in values):
1535:             raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1536:                 "projection carries a partial Arrival resume mark"
1537:             )
1538:         lineage, raw_offset, raw_ordinal = values
1539:         assert raw_offset is not None and raw_ordinal is not None
1540:         try:
1541:             offset = int(raw_offset)
1542:             ordinal = int(raw_ordinal)
1543:         except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
1544:             raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1545:                 "projection carries a non-integer Arrival resume mark"
1546:             ) from exc
1547:         if not isinstance(lineage, str) or not lineage or offset <= 0 or ordinal < 0:
1548:             raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1549:                 "projection carries an invalid Arrival resume mark"
1550:             )
1551:         return ResumeMark(lineage, offset, ordinal)
1552: 
1553:     def _validate_target(self, through: Head) -> None:
1554:         record = self._log.read(through.ordinal)
1555:         if (
1556:             record["lin"] != through.lineage
1557:             or record["ord"] != through.ordinal
1558:             or record["rh"] != through.record_hash
1559:         ):
1560:             raise HeadMismatch(
1561:                 "projection maintenance target is not the full head at its coordinate"
1562:             )
1563: 
1564:     def _validate_existing(
1565:         self, conn: sqlite3.Connection
1566:     ) -> tuple[ResumeMark | None, str | None]:
1567:         required = {"facts", "ticks", "store_meta"}
1568:         tables = self._tables(conn)
1569:         if not tables:
1570:             # sqlite may leave a zero-schema file after a rolled-back first
1571:             # materialization. It contains no projection evidence to recover
1572:             # or overwrite and is equivalent to an absent derived artifact.
1573:             return None, None
1574:         missing = required - tables
1575:         if missing:
1576:             raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1577:                 f"existing projection lacks required tables: {sorted(missing)}"
1578:             )
1579:         mark = self._read_mark(conn)
1580:         rows_present = has_rows(conn)
1581:         if mark is None and rows_present:
1582:             raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1583:                 "projection holds rows without an Arrival resume mark"
1584:             )
1585:         if mark is not None:
1586:             anchor = self._log.anchor(mark)
1587:             if anchor is None:
1588:                 raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1589:                     "projection resume mark is not a verified log boundary"
1590:                 )
1591:             if _meta_get(conn, "coordinate_axis") != "arrival":
1592:                 raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1593:                     "represented projection does not declare the Arrival coordinate axis"
1594:                 )
1595:         return mark, _meta_get(conn, "own_lineage")
1596: 
1597:     def _validate_identity(self, marker: str | None, lineage: str) -> None:
1598:         if marker is not None and marker != lineage:
1599:             raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1600:                 f"projection own_lineage {marker!r} differs from log lineage {lineage!r}"
1601:             )
1602: 
1603:     def _insert_record(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
1604:         for sequence, (kind, row) in enumerate(rows_of_record(record)):
1605:             try:
1606:                 conn.execute(
1607:                     FACT_INSERT_SQL if kind == "fact" else TICK_INSERT_SQL,
1608:                     (*row, record["ord"], sequence),
1609:                 )
1610:             except Exception as exc:
1611:                 raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1612:                     f"projection refuses {kind} {row[0]!r} from ordinal "
1613:                     f"{record['ord']}; existing state is not a consumable prefix"
1614:                 ) from exc
1615: 
1616:     def catch_up(self, through: Head) -> MaintenanceAdvance:
1617:         if self._closed:
1618:             raise RuntimeError("projection maintenance handle is closed")
1619:         self._validate_target(through)
1620: 
1621:         existed = self._path.exists()
1622:         self._path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1623:         # A competing maintainer owns a normal serialization turn, not an
1624:         # immediate failure. Keep the wait finite so operational lock loss is
1625:         # still reported through ProjectionSyncError with observed evidence.
1626:         conn = sqlite3.connect(str(self._path), timeout=30.0)
1627:         conn.isolation_level = None
1628:         try:
1629:             if existed:
1630:                 mark, marker = self._validate_existing(conn)
1631:                 self._validate_identity(marker, through.lineage)
1632:             else:
1633:                 mark, marker = None, None
1634: 
1635:             # The shared schema helper owns its commits, so schema setup must
1636:             # complete before the explicit row/watermark transaction begins.
1637:             # It is idempotent derived structure; projection content and its
1638:             # resume mark remain one atomic transaction below.
1639:             _ensure_index_schema(conn, self._log)
1640:             conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
1641:             try:
1642:                 # Revalidate all evidence after acquiring the adapter's write
1643:                 # lock. Another maintainer may have advanced or exposed a
1644:                 # conflict between the initial observation and this turn.
1645:                 mark, marker = self._validate_existing(conn)
1646:                 self._validate_identity(marker, through.lineage)
1647:                 before = (
1648:                     None
1649:                     if mark is None
1650:                     else Watermark(mark.arrival_lineage, mark.arrival_ordinal)
1651:                 )
1652: 
1653:                 changed = False
1654:                 last_mark = mark
1655:                 if mark is None or mark.arrival_ordinal < through.ordinal:
1656:                     resumed, records = self._log.walk_marked(mark)
1657:                     if mark is not None and resumed == 0:
1658:                         raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1659:                             "projection resume mark was refused during verified traversal"
1660:                         )
1661:                     for record, record_mark in records:
1662:                         if record["ord"] > through.ordinal:
1663:                             break
1664:                         if (
1665:                             record["ord"] == through.ordinal
1666:                             and record["rh"] != through.record_hash
1667:                         ):
1668:                             raise HeadMismatch(
1669:                                 "log changed at the maintenance target after full "
1670:                                 "verification"
1671:                             )
1672:                         self._insert_record(conn, record)
1673:                         last_mark = record_mark
1674:                         changed = True
1675:                     if last_mark is None or last_mark.arrival_ordinal < through.ordinal:
1676:                         raise HeadMismatch(
1677:                             "verified traversal ended before the maintenance target"
1678:                         )
1679: 
1680:                 if marker is None:
1681:                     licensed = licensed_own_lineage(conn, through.lineage)
1682:                     if licensed is not None:
1683:                         _meta_set(conn, "own_lineage", licensed)
1684:                         changed = True
1685:                 if last_mark is None:
1686:                     raise HeadMismatch("maintenance established no projection mark")
1687:                 if changed or mark != last_mark:
1688:                     _stamp_mark(conn, last_mark)
1689:                 conn.commit()
1690:             except BaseException:
1691:                 conn.rollback()
1692:                 raise
1693: 
1694:             after = Watermark(last_mark.arrival_lineage, last_mark.arrival_ordinal)
1695:             return MaintenanceAdvance(before=before, after=after, changed=changed)
1696:         finally:
1697:             conn.close()
1698: 
1699:     def close(self) -> None:
1700:         self._closed = True
1701: 
1702: 
1703: class FileSearchMaintenance:
1704:     """Explicit full-prefix FTS5 builder; never reached from a read snapshot."""
1705: 
1706:     def __init__(self, log_path: Path | str, index_path: Path | str) -> None:
1707:         self._log = ArrivalLog(log_path)
1708:         self._path = Path(index_path)
1709:         self._closed = False
1710: 
1711:     def _coverage(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> SearchCoverage | None:
1712:         try:
1713:             values = dict(conn.execute("SELECT key, value FROM arrival_fts_state"))
1714:             return SearchCoverage(
1715:                 Head(values["lineage"], int(values["ordinal"]), values["record_hash"]),
1716:                 values["fields_hash"],
1717:                 values["schema_version"],
1718:             )
1719:         except (sqlite3.Error, KeyError, ValueError):
1720:             return None
1721: 
1722:     def coverage(self) -> SearchCoverage | None:
1723:         if not self._path.exists():
1724:             return None
1725:         conn = sqlite3.connect(str(self._path))
1726:         try:
1727:             return self._coverage(conn)
1728:         finally:
1729:             conn.close()
1730: 
1731:     def build(self, through: Head, spec: SearchFieldSpec) -> SearchIndexBuild:
1732:         if self._closed:
1733:             raise RuntimeError("search maintenance handle is closed")
1734:         record = self._log.read(through.ordinal)
1735:         if (record["lin"], record["ord"], record["rh"]) != (
1736:             through.lineage, through.ordinal, through.record_hash
1737:         ):
1738:             raise HeadMismatch("search target no longer names this file prefix")
1739:         if not self._path.exists():
1740:             raise ProjectionAbsent("cannot build search before the projection exists")
1741:         conn = sqlite3.connect(str(self._path), timeout=30.0)
1742:         conn.isolation_level = None
1743:         try:
1744:             conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
1745:             try:
1746:                 lineage = _meta_get(conn, ARRIVAL_LINEAGE_KEY)
1747:                 ordinal = _meta_get(conn, ARRIVAL_ORDINAL_KEY)
1748:                 if lineage is None or ordinal is None:
1749:                     raise ProjectionAbsent(
1750:                         "cannot build search before the projection watermark exists"
1751:                     )
1752:                 watermark = Watermark(str(lineage), int(str(ordinal)))
1753:                 if watermark.lineage != through.lineage or watermark.ordinal < through.ordinal:
