1754:                     raise ProjectionBehind("projection does not reach the search target")
1755:                 before = self._coverage(conn)
1756:                 conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS arrival_facts_fts")
1757:                 conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS arrival_fts_state")
1758:                 conn.execute(
1759:                     "CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE arrival_facts_fts USING fts5("
1760:                     "text_content, fact_id UNINDEXED)"
1761:                 )
1762:                 conn.execute(
1763:                     "CREATE TABLE arrival_fts_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)"
1764:                 )
1765:                 rows = conn.execute(
1766:                     "SELECT id, kind, payload FROM facts WHERE arrival_ordinal <= ? "
1767:                     "ORDER BY arrival_ordinal, arrival_seq, id", (through.ordinal,)
1768:                 ).fetchall()
1769:                 from .search_fields import extract_field_text
1770: 
1771:                 for fact_id, kind, payload_text in rows:
1772:                     fields = spec.fields_by_kind.get(kind, ())
1773:                     if not fields:
1774:                         continue
1775:                     try:
1776:                         payload = json.loads(payload_text)
1777:                     except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
1778:                         raise ArrivalCanonicalUnsupported(
1779:                             f"projected fact {fact_id!r} has invalid payload text"
1780:                         ) from exc
1781:                     text = " ".join(extract_field_text(payload, field) for field in fields)
1782:                     if text.strip():
1783:                         conn.execute(
1784:                             "INSERT INTO arrival_facts_fts(text_content, fact_id) VALUES (?, ?)",
1785:                             (text, fact_id),
1786:                         )
1787:                 schema_version = str(conn.execute("PRAGMA schema_version").fetchone()[0])
1788:                 state = {
1789:                     "lineage": through.lineage,
1790:                     "ordinal": str(through.ordinal),
1791:                     "record_hash": through.record_hash,
1792:                     "fields_hash": spec.fields_hash,
1793:                     "normalization_version": spec.normalization_version,
1794:                     "schema_version": schema_version,
1795:                 }
1796:                 conn.executemany(
1797:                     "INSERT INTO arrival_fts_state(key, value) VALUES (?, ?)", state.items()
1798:                 )
1799:                 conn.commit()
1800:                 after = SearchCoverage(through, spec.fields_hash, schema_version)
1801:                 return SearchIndexBuild(
1802:                     before=before,
1803:                     after=after,
1804:                     changed=before != after,
1805:                 )
1806:             except BaseException:
1807:                 conn.rollback()
1808:                 raise
1809:         finally:
1810:             conn.close()
1811: 
1812:     def close(self) -> None:
1813:         self._closed = True

=== libs/engine/src/engine/vertex.py ===
1: """Vertex: where loops meet.
2: 
3: A Vertex manages fold engines, routes facts by kind to the right
4: consumer, holds an optional Store, and produces Ticks when a
5: temporal boundary fires.
6: 
7: Kind-based routing: register a fold for each kind. When a fact
8: arrives, the Vertex dispatches to the matching fold engine.
9: Projection is the internal fold engine detail — callers register
10: folds, not Projections.
11: 
12: Boundary triggering: a fold engine can declare a boundary kind.
13: When a fact with that kind arrives, the engine's state is snapshot
14: into a Tick and optionally reset. The boundary fires after the fold
15: completes (fold-before-boundary).
16: 
17: Decoupled boundary evaluation: evaluate_boundaries() checks boundary
18: triggers for facts that arrived via external emit (between vertex runs).
19: Facts folded during replay don't trigger boundaries — evaluate_boundaries()
20: scans the current period's facts and fires any matching boundaries against
21: the fully-rebuilt fold state. Called by the Executor before source execution.
22: 
23: Grant-aware receive: the Vertex gates facts against an optional Grant's
24: potential. Observer-state kinds (focus.{observer}, scroll.{observer},
25: selection.{observer}) must match the fact's observer.
26: """
27: 
28: from __future__ import annotations
29: 
30: import fnmatch
31: import re
32: from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
33: from contextlib import contextmanager
34: from dataclasses import dataclass
35: from datetime import UTC, datetime, timezone
36: from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, NamedTuple
37: 
38: from lang.document import is_internal_kind
39: 
40: from .loop import Loop
41: from .store import Store
42: from .tick import Tick
43: 
44: if TYPE_CHECKING:
45:     from atoms import Fact
46: 
47:     from .peer import Grant
48: 
49: 
50: # Observer-state kind pattern: kind.{observer_name}
51: _OBSERVER_STATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^(focus|scroll|selection)\.(.+)$")
52: 
53: 
54: @dataclass(frozen=True)
55: class FactAttestation:
56:     """Persisted signature state of the COMMITTED fact row.
57: 
58:     Populated by reading the row the store actually committed (never from
59:     "keys exist locally" inference — a per-observer signer that returns
60:     ``None`` yields ``signed=False`` even when signing is configured;
61:     write-receipt-vs-temporal-query, LIBS_CHANGES P1).
62: 
63:     - ``signed`` — the committed row carries an authorship signature.
64:     - ``observer`` — the observer the row was committed under (the
65:       authorship claim's subject).
66: 
67:     ``signed`` is a presence claim, not a verification claim; a distinct
68:     ``verified`` field arrives when verification-grade read-back exists
69:     (the former ``signature_present`` twin was provably identical and
70:     dissolved).
71:     """
72: 
73:     signed: bool
74:     observer: str
75: 
76: 
77: @dataclass(frozen=True)
78: class TickAttestation:
79:     """Persisted chain/signature state of the COMMITTED tick row.
80: 
81:     Read back from the tick row the store committed when the boundary
82:     fired — never inferred from whether a tick signer was wired.
83: 
84:     - ``signed`` — the committed row carries an Ed25519 signature over
85:       its commitment hash (presence, not verification — same note as
86:       :class:`FactAttestation`).
87:     - ``chained`` — the row carries the chain fields (``window_hash``
88:       et al.); ``False`` marks a pre-chain-era row.
89:     """
90: 
91:     signed: bool
92:     chained: bool
93: 
94: 
95: @dataclass(frozen=True)
96: class Receipt:
97:     """The write receipt — identity of your write, not current state.
98: 
99:     Returned by ``Vertex.receive_receipt`` / ``VertexProgram.receive``:
100: 
101:     - ``fact_id`` — the id the store assigned to this write (equal to
102:       ``id_override`` when one was passed). ``None`` when the attached
103:       store doesn't track ids (EventStore/FileStore) or nothing was
104:       stored.
105:     - ``tick`` — the Tick if this fact fired a boundary, else None.
106:     - ``stored`` — whether the fact was appended to an attached store.
107:       ``False`` on gate rejection (grant potential, observer-state
108:       ownership) and on storeless vertices (which may still have folded
109:       the fact). Distinguishes "stored, no boundary fired" from
110:       "rejected, nothing written" — both were an ambiguous ``None``
111:       under the tick-only return.
112: 
113:     ``fact_id``/``stored`` describe THIS vertex's store only — a fact
114:     forwarded to a nested child with its own store is appended there
115:     under the child's own bookkeeping, not reflected here.
116: 
117:     - ``attestation`` — the committed fact row's persisted signature
118:       state (:class:`FactAttestation`), read back from the store after
119:       the append. **Tri-state**: ``None`` means the store doesn't report
120:       attestation (EventStore/FileStore, storeless vertices, gate
121:       rejection) — NOT "unsigned". ``FactAttestation(signed=False)`` is
122:       a positive claim from a committed row; clients must not print
123:       ``signed: false`` for a ``None`` attestation.
124:     - ``tick_attestation`` — same honesty for the boundary tick, when
125:       one fired AND its committed row is reportable
126:       (:class:`TickAttestation`); ``None`` otherwise.
127: 
128:     Deliberately carries no fold state: a write returns a stable handle
129:     to itself; "current state" is a separate racy read
130:     (write-receipt-vs-temporal-query).
131:     """
132: 
133:     fact_id: str | None
134:     tick: Tick | None
135:     stored: bool
136:     attestation: FactAttestation | None = None
137:     tick_attestation: TickAttestation | None = None
138: 
139: 
140: class ReservedKindError(Exception):
141:     """A fact whose kind is in the reserved declaration namespace (``_decl.*``)
142:     was routed into a persisting vertex from ordinary ingress.
143: 
144:     The ``_decl.*`` prefix is the internal-table protocol's own vocabulary
145:     (SPEC §9.2), written only through the genesis/absorb ceremony — never
146:     ordinary ingress (emit, sources, the tasks harness). Guarding at the
147:     engine ingest tier makes the reservation structural rather than a
148:     per-caller courtesy. Replay re-ingest (storeless) and the ceremony's own
149:     direct write (which bypasses ``receive``) are unaffected.
150:     """
151: 
152: 
153: def _json_default(obj: object) -> object:
154:     """Handle MappingProxyType in JSON serialization."""
155:     from types import MappingProxyType
156: 
157:     if isinstance(obj, MappingProxyType):
158:         return dict(obj)
159:     raise TypeError(f"Object of type {type(obj).__name__} is not JSON serializable")
160: 
161: 
162: def _eval_condition(state: Any, condition: Any) -> bool:
163:     """Evaluate a single BoundaryCondition against fold state.
164: 
165:     State can be a dict (named targets) or MappingProxyType. The condition's
166:     target is looked up in state, then compared using the operator.
167:     """
168:     from types import MappingProxyType
169: 
170:     if isinstance(state, MappingProxyType):
171:         state = dict(state)
172:     if not isinstance(state, dict):
173:         return False
174:     value = state.get(condition.target)
175:     if value is None:
176:         return False
177:     try:
178:         fval = float(value)
179:         fcomp = float(condition.value)
180:     except (ValueError, TypeError):
181:         # Fall back to string comparison for == and !=
182:         if condition.op == "==":
183:             return str(value) == str(condition.value)
184:         if condition.op == "!=":
185:             return str(value) != str(condition.value)
186:         return False
187:     if condition.op == ">=":
188:         return fval >= fcomp
189:     if condition.op == "<=":
190:         return fval <= fcomp
191:     if condition.op == ">":
192:         return fval > fcomp
193:     if condition.op == "<":
194:         return fval < fcomp
195:     if condition.op == "==":
196:         return fval == fcomp
197:     if condition.op == "!=":
198:         return fval != fcomp
199:     return False
200: 
201: 
202: def _eval_conditions(state: Any, conditions: tuple) -> bool:
203:     """Evaluate all BoundaryConditions — AND semantics."""
204:     return all(_eval_condition(state, c) for c in conditions)
205: 
206: 
207: class _VertexBoundarySpec(NamedTuple):
208:     """One vertex-level boundary declaration.
209: 
210:     A vertex may declare several (e.g. `session closed` and `seal`); each fires
211:     the whole vertex independently. Specs are evaluated in declaration order —
212:     the first one a fact satisfies fires the tick, preserving single-boundary
213:     firing semantics per fact (one fact mints one tick, never several). See
214:     friction:vertex-boundary-last-declaration-wins.
215:     """
216: 
217:     kind: str
218:     match: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()
219:     conditions: tuple = ()
220:     run: str | None = None
221: 
222: 
223: class Vertex:
224:     """Where loops meet.
225: 
226:     Register folds by kind. Receive facts routed by kind. Fire a
227:     temporal boundary to produce a Tick snapshot of all fold states.
228: 
229:     Optionally backed by a Store — if provided, every received fact
230:     is appended to the store before routing.
231: 
232:     Grant-aware: receive() takes a Fact (with observer) and optional Grant.
233:     The Vertex gates facts against the grant's potential (if provided) and
234:     enforces observer-state kind ownership based on fact.observer.
235: 
236:     Nesting: a Vertex can contain child vertices. After local routing,
237:     facts are forwarded to children that accept the kind. Child ticks
238:     become facts that re-enter the parent.
239:     """
240: 
241:     def __init__(
242:         self,
243:         name: str = "",
244:         *,
245:         store: Store | None = None,
246:         strict: bool = False,
247:     ) -> None:
248:         self._name = name
249:         # Declared strict admission: when True, receive() refuses undeclared
250:         # kinds with a typed UndeclaredKind BEFORE storage (bypass only via
251:         # the explicit admit_undeclared parameter). See
252:         # decision:design/strict-enforcement-at-engine-receive.
253:         self._strict = strict
254:         self._loops: dict[str, Loop] = {}
255:         self._boundary_map: dict[str, str] = {}  # boundary_kind → fold_kind
256:         self._has_loop_boundaries = False
257:         self._boundary_match: dict[str, tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]] = {}  # boundary_kind → match
258:         self._boundary_conditions: dict[str, tuple] = {}  # boundary_kind → conditions
259:         # Vertex-level boundaries — a vertex may declare several, each firing
260:         # the whole vertex. Evaluated in declaration order (first match fires).
261:         self._vertex_boundaries: list[_VertexBoundarySpec] = []
262:         self._vertex_boundary_kinds: set[str] = set()  # fast accepts() membership
263:         self._vertex_period_start: datetime | None = None
264:         self._store = store
265:         self._replaying = False  # suppress boundaries during replay
266:         self._has_children = False
267:         self._children: list[Vertex] = []
268:         self._routes: dict[str, str] = {}  # pattern → loop_name
269:         self._has_routes = False
270:         self._route_cache: dict[str, str | None] = {}
271:         self._accepts_cache: dict[str, bool] = {}
272:         self._parse_pipelines: dict[str, list] = {}  # kind → compiled ParseOp list
273: 
274:     @property
275:     def name(self) -> str:
276:         """Vertex name — stamped as origin on produced Ticks."""
277:         return self._name
278: 
279:     @property
280:     def _has_vertex_boundary(self) -> bool:
281:         """True when the vertex declares at least one vertex-level boundary."""
282:         return bool(self._vertex_boundaries)
283: 
284:     def _match_vertex_boundary(
285:         self,
286:         kind: str,
287:         payload: Any,
288:     ) -> _VertexBoundarySpec | None:
289:         """First vertex-level boundary spec this fact satisfies, or None.
290: 
291:         Declaration order is authoritative: a fact that satisfies more than one
292:         boundary fires the first-declared match only (one fact → one tick).
293:         Payload match and fold-state conditions are both checked.
294:         """
295:         for spec in self._vertex_boundaries:
296:             if spec.kind != kind:
297:                 continue
298:             if spec.match and not all(payload.get(k) == v for k, v in spec.match):
299:                 continue
300:             if spec.conditions:
301:                 cond_loop = self._loops.get(self._routed_kind(kind))
302:                 if cond_loop is None or not _eval_conditions(cond_loop.state, spec.conditions):
303:                     continue
304:             return spec
305:         return None
306: 
307:     @property
308:     def children(self) -> list[Vertex]:
309:         """Child vertices, in registration order."""
310:         return list(self._children)
311: 
312:     def add_child(self, child: Vertex) -> None:
313:         """Add a child vertex.
314: 
315:         Facts received by this vertex will be forwarded to children that
316:         accept the kind. Ticks produced by children become facts that
317:         re-enter this vertex.
318:         """
319:         self._children.append(child)
320:         self._has_children = True
321:         self._accepts_cache.clear()
322: 
323:     def set_routes(self, routes: dict[str, str]) -> None:
324:         """Set pattern-based routing rules.
325: 
326:         Routes map glob patterns to loop names. When a fact arrives,
327:         patterns are checked in order and the first match determines
328:         which loop receives the fact.
329: 
330:         Pattern syntax (fnmatch):
331:         - * matches any sequence of characters
332:         - ? matches any single character
333:         - [seq] matches any character in seq
334: 
335:         Examples:
336:             {"disk.*": "disk"}      # disk.usage, disk.io → disk loop
337:             {"proc.*": "proc"}      # proc.cpu, proc.mem → proc loop
338:             {"disk": "disk"}        # exact match (no wildcards)
339: 
340:         Args:
341:             routes: Dict mapping glob patterns to loop names
342:         """
343:         self._routes = routes.copy()
344:         self._has_routes = bool(self._routes)
345:         self._route_cache.clear()
346:         self._accepts_cache.clear()
347: 
348:     def set_parse_pipelines(self, pipelines: dict[str, list]) -> None:
349:         """Set per-kind parse pipelines.
350: 
351:         Parse pipelines transform fact payloads before routing to folds.
352:         Derived fields are added alongside originals.
353: 
354:         Args:
355:             pipelines: Dict mapping kind name to list of compiled ParseOps
356:         """
357:         self._parse_pipelines = pipelines.copy()
358: 
359:     def _resolve_route(self, kind: str) -> str | None:
360:         """Resolve a fact kind to a loop name via route patterns.
361: 
362:         Returns the loop name if a route matches, None otherwise.
363:         Patterns are checked in dict order (Python 3.7+ preserves insertion order).
364:         Caches per-kind results because receive() and accepts() often see the
365:         same kinds repeatedly.
366:         """
367:         cached = self._route_cache.get(kind, None)
368:         if kind in self._route_cache:
369:             return cached
370:         for pattern, loop_name in self._routes.items():
371:             if fnmatch.fnmatch(kind, pattern):
372:                 self._route_cache[kind] = loop_name
373:                 return loop_name
374:         self._route_cache[kind] = None
375:         return None
376: 
377:     def accepts(self, kind: str) -> bool:
378:         """Check if this vertex handles a kind.
379: 
380:         Returns True if the kind is registered as a route (fold engine),
381:         loop name, boundary kind, or matches a pattern route — or if any
382:         child accepts it. Used by parent vertices to determine whether
383:         to forward facts to this child.
384:         """
385:         cached = self._accepts_cache.get(kind)
386:         if cached is not None:
387:             return cached
388: 
389:         accepted = (
390:             kind in self._loops
391:             or kind in self._boundary_map
392:             or kind in self._vertex_boundary_kinds
393:             or (self._has_routes and self._resolve_route(kind) is not None)
394:             or (self._has_children and any(child.accepts(kind) for child in self._children))
395:         )
396:         self._accepts_cache[kind] = accepted
397:         return accepted
398: 
399:     def register(
400:         self,
401:         kind: str,
402:         initial: Any,
403:         fold: Callable[[Any, Any], Any],
404:         *,
405:         boundary: str | None = None,
406:         reset: bool = True,
407:     ) -> None:
408:         """Convenience: create a Loop from args and register it.
409: 
410:         Preserves the original API — all existing callers keep working.
411:         Internally everything routes through _loops via register_loop().
412: 
413:         Raises ValueError if the kind is already registered or the boundary
414:         kind is already claimed by another engine.
415:         """
416:         loop = Loop(
417:             name=kind,
418:             initial=initial,
419:             fold=fold,
420:             boundary_kind=boundary,
421:             reset=reset,
422:         )
423:         self.register_loop(loop)
424: 
425:     def register_loop(self, loop: Loop) -> None:
426:         """Register an explicit Loop object.
427: 
428:         The loop's name becomes the routing kind. If the loop has a
429:         boundary_kind, that kind will trigger fire() on boundary receipt.
430: 
431:         Raises ValueError if the loop name is already registered or the
432:         boundary kind is already claimed.
433:         """
434:         kind = loop.name
435:         if kind in self._loops:
436:             raise ValueError(f"Kind already registered: {kind}")
437:         if loop.boundary_kind is not None:
438:             if loop.boundary_kind in self._boundary_map:
439:                 raise ValueError(f"Boundary kind already registered: {loop.boundary_kind}")
440:             self._boundary_map[loop.boundary_kind] = kind
441:             self._has_loop_boundaries = True
442:             if loop.boundary_match:
443:                 self._boundary_match[loop.boundary_kind] = loop.boundary_match
444:             if loop.boundary_conditions:
445:                 self._boundary_conditions[loop.boundary_kind] = loop.boundary_conditions
446:         self._loops[kind] = loop
447:         self._accepts_cache.clear()
448: 
449:     def _routed_kind(self, kind: str) -> str:
450:         """Resolve incoming fact kind to the target loop name, if any."""
451:         if kind in self._loops or not self._has_routes:
452:             return kind
453:         resolved = self._resolve_route(kind)
454:         return resolved if resolved is not None else kind
455: 
456:     def _apply_parse_pipeline(self, routed_kind: str, payload: Any) -> Any:
457:         """Apply per-kind parse pipeline, returning None when the fact is dropped."""
458:         parse_pipeline = self._parse_pipelines.get(routed_kind)
459:         if parse_pipeline is None:
460:             return payload
461: 
462:         from atoms import run_parse
463: 
464:         parse_input = dict(payload) if hasattr(payload, "keys") else payload
465:         return run_parse(parse_input, parse_pipeline)
466: 
467:     def register_vertex_boundary(
468:         self,
469:         kind: str,
470:         match: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (),
471:         conditions: tuple = (),
472:         run: str | None = None,
473:     ) -> None:
474:         """Register a vertex-level boundary.
475: 
476:         When a fact of this kind arrives (and matches payload conditions,
477:         and all fold-state conditions are met), ALL loop states are snapshot
478:         into a single Tick. This is the vertex's cycle boundary — e.g.
479:         session close snapshots everything.
480: 
481:         Vertex-level boundaries take precedence over loop-level boundaries
482:         for the same kind.
483: 
484:         Called once per declared boundary — a vertex may register several,
485:         which ACCUMULATE (each fires the whole vertex independently). They are
486:         evaluated in registration/declaration order; the first a fact satisfies
487:         fires (see _match_vertex_boundary). Previously the loader dropped all
488:         but the last declaration (friction:vertex-boundary-last-declaration-wins).
489: 
490:         Optional run clause: shell command carried on the Tick for app-layer
491:         execution when the boundary fires.
492:         """
493:         if kind in self._boundary_map:
494:             raise ValueError(f"Boundary kind '{kind}' already registered at loop level")
495:         self._vertex_boundaries.append(
496:             _VertexBoundarySpec(
497:                 kind=kind,
498:                 match=match,
499:                 conditions=conditions,
500:                 run=run,
501:             )
502:         )
503:         self._vertex_boundary_kinds.add(kind)
504:         self._accepts_cache.clear()
505: 
506:     def receive(
507:         self,
508:         fact: Fact,
509:         grant: Grant | None = None,
510:         *,
511:         _from_child: str | None = None,
512:         id_override: str | None = None,
513:         admit_undeclared: bool = False,
514:     ) -> Tick | None:
515:         """Tick projection of :meth:`receive_receipt`.
516: 
517:         The routing view: returns the Tick if this fact fired a boundary,
518:         else None. Engine-internal callers (child forwarding, executor,
519:         replay) consume this. Client code that needs write identity —
520:         the stored fact id, or stored-vs-rejected — goes through
521:         ``receive_receipt`` (or ``VertexProgram.receive``, which returns
522:         the full Receipt). One implementation, two views: this delegates,
523:         so the projections cannot drift.
524:         """
525:         return self.receive_receipt(
526:             fact,
527:             grant,
528:             _from_child=_from_child,
529:             id_override=id_override,
530:             admit_undeclared=admit_undeclared,
531:         ).tick
532: 
533:     def receive_receipt(
534:         self,
535:         fact: Fact,
536:         grant: Grant | None = None,
537:         *,
538:         _from_child: str | None = None,
539:         id_override: str | None = None,
540:         admit_undeclared: bool = False,
541:         _plan_only: bool = False,
542:     ) -> Receipt:
543:         """Route a fact to the appropriate fold engine, gated by optional grant.
544: 
545:         Gating rules:
546:         1. If grant.potential is not None and fact.kind not in potential → reject
547:         2. For observer-state kinds (focus.{name}, scroll.{name}, selection.{name}),
548:            the {name} must match fact.observer → reject if mismatch
549: 
550:         If a Store is attached, the fact is appended before routing.
551:         Unregistered kinds are silently ignored — they pass through to the
552:         store but don't fold.
553: 
554:         After local routing, forwards to children that accept the kind.
555:         Child ticks become facts that re-enter this vertex (but not back
556:         to the originating child, to prevent recursion).
557: 
558:         After folding, checks if the incoming kind triggers a boundary.
559:         If so, snapshots the triggered engine's state into a Tick and
560:         carries it on the Receipt.
561: 
562:         Returns a :class:`Receipt` — ``stored=False, fact_id=None,
563:         tick=None`` on gate rejection; otherwise ``fact_id`` is the id
564:         the attached store assigned (None for stores that don't track
565:         ids, and for storeless vertices) and ``tick`` is the boundary
566:         Tick or None.
567: 
568:         Args:
569:             fact: The Fact to receive
570:             grant: Optional Grant for potential gating
571:             _from_child: Internal - name of child that produced this fact (prevents loopback)
572:             id_override: Pre-generated fact id to store under (rare —
573:                 replay/transport-shaped callers; ordinary writers let the
574:                 store mint and read the id off the Receipt)
575:             admit_undeclared: Explicit bypass of declared strict admission.
576:                 On a strict vertex an undeclared kind raises
577:                 :class:`~engine.admission.UndeclaredKind` before storage;
578:                 pass True to store it anyway (the bypass is this named
579:                 parameter, never an omission). No effect on non-strict
580:                 vertices.
581: 
582:         Raises:
583:             UndeclaredKind: strict vertex, undeclared kind, no bypass —
584:                 refused before storage.
585:         """
586:         kind = fact.kind
587:         payload = fact.payload
588:         observer = fact.observer
589: 
590:         # Gate 1: potential check (only if grant provided)
591:         if grant is not None and grant.potential is not None and kind not in grant.potential:
592:             return Receipt(fact_id=None, tick=None, stored=False)
593: 
594:         # Gate 2: observer-state ownership
595:         if kind[:6] in {"focus.", "scroll"} or kind.startswith("selection."):
596:             _, _, owner_name = kind.partition(".")
597:             if owner_name and owner_name != observer:
598:                 return Receipt(fact_id=None, tick=None, stored=False)
599: 
600:         # Reserved-namespace ingest guard (SPEC §9.2 write-time reservation).
601:         # A ``_decl.*`` kind is the declaration protocol's own vocabulary,
602:         # written only by the absorb ceremony (which appends directly, not
603:         # through receive). Refuse ordinary ingress that would PERSIST one —
604:         # gating on an attached store, so replay re-ingest (storeless vertex)
605:         # and the production ``Vertex.replay`` (sets store=None, bypasses
606:         # receive) fold historical declaration rows without tripping this.
607:         # Strict admission (decision:design/strict-enforcement-at-engine-receive):
608:         # when the declaration says strict, an undeclared kind is refused with
609:         # a typed error BEFORE storage. "Declared" is accepts() — loop kinds,
610:         # boundary kinds, routes, and kinds any child accepts. Child-tick
611:         # re-entry (_from_child) is engine-internal, not client ingress, and
612:         # is exempt. Observer-state kinds (focus.*/scroll.*/selection.*) get
613:         # no special case: undeclared is undeclared. Bypass is the explicit
614:         # admit_undeclared parameter only.
615:         if self._strict and not admit_undeclared and _from_child is None and not self.accepts(kind):
616:             from .admission import UndeclaredKind
617: 
618:             raise UndeclaredKind(kind, self._name)
619: 
620:         if (self._store is not None or _plan_only) and is_internal_kind(kind):
621:             raise ReservedKindError(
622:                 f"kind '{kind}' is in the reserved declaration namespace "
623:                 f"('_decl.*') — recorded via the absorb ceremony, not ingest"
624:             )
625: 
626:         # Store the full fact (not just kind/payload) for replay. The
627:         # store's append returns the id it stored under (None for stores
628:         # that don't track ids) — that id IS the write's identity and
629:         # rides out on the Receipt. id_override forces a specific id
630:         # (replay/transport-shaped callers); ordinary writers read the
631:         # minted id off the Receipt instead of pre-generating.
632:         fact_id: str | None = None
633:         stored = False
634:         attestation: FactAttestation | None = None
635:         if self._store is not None:
636:             appender = getattr(self._store, "append_attested", None)
637:             if appender is not None:
638:                 # The returned signature IS the committed column: the store
639:                 # reads it back inside the write transaction, post-INSERT,
640:                 # pre-commit (SOL-R3-02; LIBS_CHANGES P1's "the committed
641:                 # row" clause).
642:                 fact_id, signature = appender(fact, id_override=id_override)
643:                 attestation = FactAttestation(
644:                     signed=signature is not None,
645:                     observer=observer,
646:                 )
647:             else:
648:                 fact_id = self._store.append(fact, id_override=id_override)
649:                 attestation = self._fact_attestation(fact_id, observer)
650:             stored = True
651:         elif _plan_only:
652:             # A detached runtime plan must exercise the exact admission,
653:             # parse, fold and boundary path without creating a second store.
654:             # ``stored`` means accepted for this planning-only invocation;
655:             # its id was selected by the caller and no persistence occurred.
656:             fact_id = id_override
657:             stored = True
658: 
659:         # Convert fact timestamp for Loop routing
660:         fact_ts = datetime.fromtimestamp(fact.ts, tz=timezone.utc)
661: 
662:         # Track vertex-level period start (first fact after reset)
663:         # Suppressed during replay — replay sets period from last tick instead
664:         if self._has_vertex_boundary and self._vertex_period_start is None and not self._replaying:
665:             self._vertex_period_start = fact_ts
666: 
667:         if self._has_routes:
668:             routed_kind = self._routed_kind(kind)
669:         else:
670:             routed_kind = kind
671: 
672:         if self._parse_pipelines:
673:             payload = self._apply_parse_pipeline(routed_kind, payload)
674:             if payload is None:
675:                 # Parse rejected this fact — skip fold and routing,
676:                 # consistent with source-level parse where None means
677:                 # "drop the record." Fact is already stored for audit —
678:                 # the receipt says so honestly (stored, no tick).
679:                 return Receipt(fact_id=fact_id, tick=None, stored=stored, attestation=attestation)
680: 
681:         # Route to Loop — Loop tracks its own period_start internally
682:         # Loop.receive() returns True if a count-based boundary should fire
683:         loop = self._loops.get(routed_kind)
684:         count_boundary_fire = False
685:         if loop is not None:
686:             # Inject the event timestamp the same way the replay/read paths
687:             # do — Latest folds consume _ts; without it the live fold would
688:             # diverge from every re-fold of the same store.
689:             count_boundary_fire = loop.receive({**payload, "_ts": fact.ts}, ts=fact_ts)
690: 
691:         # Forward to children that accept this kind
692:         # Skip the child that produced this fact (prevents loopback)
693:         if self._has_children:
694:             for child in self._children:
695:                 if child.name == _from_child:
696:                     continue
697:                 if child.accepts(kind):
698:                     child_tick = child.receive(fact, grant)
699:                     if child_tick is not None:
700:                         # Child produced a tick — convert to fact and re-enter parent
701:                         child_fact = self._tick_to_fact(child_tick, child.name)
702:                         self.receive(child_fact, grant, _from_child=child.name)
703: 
704:         # Phase: boundary (live only — replay bypasses receive entirely)
705:         if self._replaying:
706:             return Receipt(fact_id=fact_id, tick=None, stored=stored, attestation=attestation)
707: 
708:         tick, tick_attestation = self._fire_live_boundaries(
709:             kind,
710:             routed_kind,
711:             payload,
712:             loop,
713:             count_boundary_fire,
714:             fact_ts,
715:         )
716:         return Receipt(
717:             fact_id=fact_id,
718:             tick=tick,
719:             stored=stored,
720:             attestation=attestation,
721:             tick_attestation=tick_attestation,
722:         )
723: 
724:     def plan_receive_receipt(
725:         self,
726:         fact: Fact,
727:         grant: Grant | None = None,
728:         *,
729:         id_override: str,
730:         admit_undeclared: bool = False,
731:     ) -> Receipt:
732:         """Run ordinary ingress against detached state without persistence.
733: 
734:         This is the runtime writer's planning hook. It deliberately reuses
735:         :meth:`receive_receipt` so gate, parse, fold and boundary behavior
736:         cannot drift from live execution, while the private flag makes the
737:         accepted plan observable without attaching a store.
738:         """
739:         if self._store is not None:
740:             raise RuntimeError("planning requires a detached vertex")
741:         return self.receive_receipt(
742:             fact,
743:             grant,
744:             id_override=id_override,
745:             admit_undeclared=admit_undeclared,
746:             _plan_only=True,
747:         )
748: 
749:     def detached_copy(self) -> Vertex:
750:         """Copy runtime fold state without copying or opening a store handle."""
751:         import copy
752: 
753:         clone = copy.copy(self)
754:         clone._store = None
755:         clone._loops = copy.deepcopy(self._loops)
756:         clone._boundary_map = copy.deepcopy(self._boundary_map)
757:         clone._boundary_match = copy.deepcopy(self._boundary_match)
758:         clone._boundary_conditions = copy.deepcopy(self._boundary_conditions)
759:         clone._vertex_boundaries = copy.deepcopy(self._vertex_boundaries)
760:         clone._vertex_boundary_kinds = copy.deepcopy(self._vertex_boundary_kinds)
761:         clone._children = [child.detached_copy() for child in self._children]
762:         clone._routes = copy.deepcopy(self._routes)
763:         clone._parse_pipelines = copy.deepcopy(self._parse_pipelines)
764:         clone._route_cache = {}
765:         clone._accepts_cache = {}
766:         clone._replaying = False
767:         return clone
768: 
769:     def _owns_tick(self, tick: Any) -> bool:
770:         """Whether a persisted tick belongs to this vertex's local runtime.
771: 
772:         A tick is local only when its explicit origin matches this vertex's
773:         name. Tick names are only local fold names; another vertex may publish
774:         the same name into the same physical ledger. Originless evidence
775:         (``None`` or ``""``) is never local proof, including for an unnamed
776:         runtime candidate.
777:         """
778:         return bool(self._name) and getattr(tick, "origin", None) == self._name
779: 
780:     def hydrate_facts(self, facts: list[Fact] | tuple[Fact, ...]) -> int:
781:         """Backward-compatible facts-only replay for a storeless candidate."""
782:         return self.hydrate_snapshot(facts, ())
783: 
784:     def hydrate_snapshot(self, facts: Sequence[Any], ticks: Sequence[Any]) -> int:
785:         """Rebuild this fresh, storeless vertex from already-captured facts.
786: 
787:         The caller supplies one receipt-ordered snapshot.  Hydration is replay:
788:         it never calls ordinary ingress, persists nothing, and never evaluates
789:         or fires a boundary.  Runtime writing uses it to make a candidate from
790:         its CURRENT projection rather than trusting a live vertex's mutable
791:         fold state.
792:         """
793:         if self._store is not None:
794:             raise RuntimeError("hydration requires a storeless vertex")
795:         if self._has_children:
796:             raise RuntimeError("stage 3A hydration does not support child vertices")
797:         count = 0
798:         ticked_loops: set[str] = set()
799:         last_vertex_tick: datetime | None = None
800:         entries = [
801:             (fact.arrival_ordinal, fact.arrival_seq, "fact", fact) for fact in facts
802:         ] + [
803:             (tick.arrival_ordinal, tick.arrival_seq, "tick", tick) for tick in ticks
804:         ]
805:         with self._replay_guard():
806:             for _, _, entry_kind, entry in sorted(entries, key=lambda row: row[:2]):
807:                 if entry_kind == "tick":
808:                     tick = entry
809:                     if not self._owns_tick(tick):
810:                         continue
811:                     loop = self._loops.get(tick.name)
812:                     if loop is not None:
813:                         loop.replay_boundary()
814:                         ticked_loops.add(tick.name)
815:                     if tick.name == self._name:
816:                         # Match ``replay()``: a vertex tick snapshots all
817:                         # loops but does not reset them; its timestamp is the
818:                         # period context restored after the bounded replay.
819:                         last_vertex_tick = datetime.fromtimestamp(tick.ts, tz=timezone.utc)
820:                     continue
821:                 fact = entry
822:                 routed_kind = self._routed_kind(fact.kind) if self._has_routes else fact.kind
823:                 payload = fact.payload
824:                 if self._parse_pipelines:
825:                     payload = self._apply_parse_pipeline(routed_kind, payload)
826:                     if payload is None:
827:                         continue
828:                 loop = self._loops.get(routed_kind)
829:                 if loop is not None:
830:                     loop.receive(
831:                         {**payload, "_ts": fact.ts},
832:                         ts=datetime.fromtimestamp(fact.ts, tz=timezone.utc),
833:                     )
834:                 count += 1
835:         # A historical loop tick is its own exact count/reset checkpoint. A
836:         # loop with no persisted tick retains legacy replay's modulo recovery.
837:         for name, loop in self._loops.items():
838:             if loop.boundary_count is not None and name not in ticked_loops:
839:                 replayed = loop._projection.events_folded
840:                 if loop.boundary_mode == "after":
841:                     loop._boundary_exhausted = replayed >= loop.boundary_count
842:                     loop._count_since_boundary = 0 if loop._boundary_exhausted else replayed
843:                 elif loop.boundary_mode == "every":
844:                     loop._count_since_boundary = replayed % loop.boundary_count
845:                 else:
846:                     loop._count_since_boundary = replayed
847:         if last_vertex_tick is not None:
848:             self._vertex_period_start = last_vertex_tick
849:         return count
850: 
851:     def _reconcile_replayed_boundaries(self) -> None:
852:         """Restore count-boundary bookkeeping after non-firing replay."""
853:         for loop in self._loops.values():
854:             if loop.boundary_count is not None:
855:                 replayed = loop._projection.events_folded
856:                 if loop.boundary_mode == "after":
857:                     if replayed >= loop.boundary_count:
858:                         loop._boundary_exhausted = True
859:                         loop._count_since_boundary = 0
860:                     else:
861:                         loop._count_since_boundary = replayed
862:                 elif loop.boundary_mode == "every":
863:                     loop._count_since_boundary = replayed % loop.boundary_count
864:                 else:
865:                     loop._count_since_boundary = replayed
866: 
867:     def _fire_live_boundaries(
868:         self,
869:         kind: str,
870:         routed_kind: str,
871:         payload: Any,
872:         loop: Loop | None,
873:         count_boundary_fire: bool,
874:         fact_ts: datetime,
875:     ) -> tuple[Tick | None, TickAttestation | None]:
876:         """Fire boundaries after a live fact fold.
877: 
878:         Returns ``(tick, tick_attestation)`` — the fired Tick (or None) and
879:         the committed tick row's persisted signature state (None when no
880:         tick fired or the store doesn't report attestation).
881: 
882:         Handles count-based, vertex-level, and loop-level boundary triggers.
883:         Only called on the live path — replay reconstructs fold state without
884:         firing boundaries.
885: 
886:         Extracted from receive() — the autoresearch proved empirically that
887:         boundary evaluation is a distinct phase from fold routing. Every
888:         optimization that skipped boundary work on the hot path improved
889:         performance, because the cost is in deciding whether to fire, not
890:         in folding.
891:         """
892:         # Count-based boundary trigger (Loop returned True during fold)
893:         if count_boundary_fire and loop is not None:
894:             tick = loop.fire(fact_ts, origin=self._name)
895:             return tick, self._store_tick(tick)
896: 
897:         if not self._has_vertex_boundary and not self._has_loop_boundaries:
898:             return None, None
899: 
900:         # Vertex-level boundary (fires all loops). A vertex may declare several;
901:         # they are evaluated in declaration order and the first a fact satisfies
902:         # fires. A vertex-boundary kind can never also be a loop-boundary kind
903:         # (register_vertex_boundary rejects the collision), so a non-match here
904:         # falls through to the loop-level check with no effect.
905:         if kind in self._vertex_boundary_kinds:
906:             spec = self._match_vertex_boundary(kind, payload)
907:             if spec is not None:
908:                 tick = self._fire_vertex_boundary(
909:                     fact_ts,
910:                     payload,
911:                     run=spec.run,
912:                 )
913:                 return tick, self._store_tick(tick)
914: 
915:         # Loop-level kind-based boundary trigger
916:         fold_kind = self._boundary_map.get(kind)
917:         if fold_kind is None:
918:             return None, None
919: 
920:         match = self._boundary_match.get(kind, ())
921:         if match and not all(payload.get(k) == v for k, v in match):
922:             return None, None
923: 
924:         conditions = self._boundary_conditions.get(kind, ())
925:         if conditions:
926:             target_loop = self._loops[fold_kind]
927:             if not _eval_conditions(target_loop.state, conditions):
928:                 return None, None
929: 
930:         target_loop = self._loops[fold_kind]
931:         tick = target_loop.fire(fact_ts, origin=self._name, boundary_payload=payload)
932:         return tick, self._store_tick(tick)
933: 
934:     def _fire_vertex_boundary(
935:         self,
936:         ts: datetime,
937:         boundary_payload: dict,
938:         run: str | None = None,
939:     ) -> Tick[dict[str, Any]]:
940:         """Fire a vertex-level boundary — snapshot ALL loop states.
941: 
942:         Unlike loop.fire() which snapshots one loop, this captures the
943:         full vertex state. Used for observer lifecycle boundaries like
944:         session close, where the tick should carry everything.
945: 
946:         ``run`` is the shell command of the firing boundary's run clause
947:         (carried on the Tick for app-layer execution) — passed per-fire since
948:         different declared boundaries may carry different run clauses.
949:         """
950:         import json
951: 
952:         # Snapshot all loop states — JSON round-trip to strip MappingProxy
953:         raw = {kind: loop.state for kind, loop in self._loops.items()}
954:         state = json.loads(json.dumps(raw, default=_json_default))
955:         state["_boundary"] = dict(boundary_payload)
956:         tick = Tick(
957:             name=self._name,
958:             ts=ts,
959:             payload=state,
960:             origin=self._name,
961:             since=self._vertex_period_start,
962:             run=run,
963:         )
964:         self._vertex_period_start = None  # reset for next period
965:         return tick
966: 
967:     def tick(self, name: str, ts: datetime) -> Tick[dict[str, Any]]:
968:         """Fire a temporal boundary.
969: 
970:         Snapshots all Loop states into a dict keyed by kind,
971:         wraps in a Tick with the given name and timestamp.
972:         Origin is stamped from the vertex name.
973:         """
974:         state = {kind: loop.state for kind, loop in self._loops.items()}
975:         return Tick(name=name, ts=ts, payload=state, origin=self._name)
976: 
977:     @property
978:     def kinds(self) -> list[str]:
979:         """Registered kinds, in registration order."""
980:         return list(self._loops.keys())
981: 
982:     def state(self, kind: str) -> Any:
983:         """Current fold state for a registered kind.
984: 
985:         Raises KeyError if kind is not registered.
986:         """
987:         return self._loops[kind].state
988: 
989:     def version(self, kind: str) -> int:
990:         """Current fold version for a registered kind.
991: 
992:         Raises KeyError if kind is not registered.
993:         """
994:         return self._loops[kind].version
995: 
996:     def close(self) -> None:
997:         """Release store resources for this vertex AND every descendant.
998: 
999:         Idempotent (store closes are None-guarded) and a no-op for
1000:         storeless vertices. Recursive on purpose: nested children may
1001:         declare their own stores, and a root-only close would leak
1002:         exactly the handle class this verb exists to release. The
1003:         lifecycle verb consumers previously reached
1004:         ``vertex._store.close()`` for — embedded clients close through
1005:         this (or ``VertexProgram.close()`` one level up), never through
1006:         the private attribute.
1007:         """
1008:         for child in self._children:
1009:             child.close()
1010:         if self._store is not None:
1011:             self._store.close()
1012: 
1013:     @contextmanager
1014:     def _replay_guard(self):
1015:         """Per-TREE replay discipline: detach every descendant's store and
1016:         mark the whole tree replaying; restore both in ``finally``.
1017: 
1018:         Per-vertex swapping was a double-append bug: parent replay
1019:         forwards historical facts to children (fallback path), and a
1020:         child whose store was still attached re-persisted the parent's
1021:         entire history on every load. The ``finally`` also fixes the
1022:         leak/wedge where a raising fold mid-replay left ``_store=None``
1023:         permanently — making ``close()`` a silent no-op and the vertex
1024:         unusable.
1025:         """
1026:         saved: list[tuple[Vertex, Any, bool]] = []
1027:         stack: list[Vertex] = [self]
1028:         while stack:
1029:             v = stack.pop()
1030:             saved.append((v, v._store, v._replaying))
1031:             v._store = None
1032:             v._replaying = True
1033:             stack.extend(v._children)
1034:         try:
1035:             yield
1036:         finally:
1037:             for v, s, r in saved:
1038:                 v._store = s
1039:                 v._replaying = r
1040: 
1041:     def replay(self) -> int:
1042:         """Replay stored facts to rebuild fold state.
1043: 
1044:         Reads all facts from the store and routes them through the folds
1045:         without re-appending or firing boundaries. This makes a one-shot
1046:         CLI invocation indistinguishable from a persistent runtime — fold
1047:         state reflects all historical facts, not just the current invocation.
1048: 
1049:         After replay, initializes the vertex period start from the last
1050:         stored tick. This ensures the next boundary fire produces a tick
1051:         with ``since`` pointing to the previous boundary, not the first
1052:         fact in history.
1053: 
1054:         Returns the number of facts replayed.
1055:         """
1056:         if self._store is None:
1057:             return 0
1058: 
1059:         store = self._store
1060:         has_parse_pipelines = bool(self._parse_pipelines)
1061:         use_raw = (
1062:             not self._has_routes
1063:             and not has_parse_pipelines
1064:             and not self._has_children
1065:             and hasattr(store, "since_raw")
1066:         )
1067: 
1068:         if use_raw:
1069:             loops = self._loops
1070:             # Pre-build mutating fold dispatch: kind → (fns, projection)
1071:             # Uses Projection.fold_one_mut — fold logic stays in Projection.
1072:             mut_dispatch: dict[str, tuple] = {}
1073:             for kind, loop in loops.items():
1074:                 fold_fn = loop._projection._fold
1075:                 if fold_fn is not None and hasattr(fold_fn, "__self__"):
1076:                     spec = fold_fn.__self__
1077:                     if hasattr(spec, "folds") and hasattr(spec, "_cached_fold_fns"):
1078:                         mut_dispatch[kind] = (spec._cached_fold_fns, loop._projection)
1079: 
1080:             # Stream path: store provides data, vertex dispatches to projections
1081:             if mut_dispatch and hasattr(store, "replay_cursor"):
1082:                 get = mut_dispatch.get
1083:                 count = 0
1084:                 with self._replay_guard():
1085:                     for kind, payload in store.replay_cursor(0):
1086:                         entry = get(kind)
1087:                         if entry is not None:
1088:                             fns, proj = entry
1089:                             proj.fold_one_mut(payload, fns)
1090:                         count += 1
1091:                 if count == 0:
1092:                     return 0
1093:             else:
1094:                 raw_facts = store.since_raw(0)
1095:                 if not raw_facts:
1096:                     return 0
1097:                 count = len(raw_facts)
1098:                 with self._replay_guard():
1099:                     if mut_dispatch:
1100:                         for kind, payload in raw_facts:
1101:                             entry = mut_dispatch.get(kind)
1102:                             if entry is not None:
1103:                                 fns, proj = entry
1104:                                 proj.fold_one_mut(payload, fns)
1105:                     else:
1106:                         for kind, payload in raw_facts:
1107:                             loop = loops.get(kind)
1108:                             if loop is not None:
1109:                                 loop._projection.fold_one(payload)
1110:         else:
1111:             # Fallback: full Fact objects needed for routes/parse/children
1112:             facts = store.since(0)
1113:             if not facts:
1114:                 return 0
1115:             count = len(facts)
1116:             with self._replay_guard():
1117:                 for fact in facts:
1118:                     routed_kind = self._routed_kind(fact.kind) if self._has_routes else fact.kind
1119:                     payload = fact.payload
1120:                     if has_parse_pipelines:
1121:                         payload = self._apply_parse_pipeline(routed_kind, payload)
1122:                         if payload is None:
1123:                             continue
1124:                     loop = self._loops.get(routed_kind)
1125:                     if loop is not None:
1126:                         loop.receive(
1127:                             {**payload, "_ts": fact.ts},
1128:                             ts=datetime.fromtimestamp(fact.ts, tz=timezone.utc),
1129:                         )
1130:                     if self._has_children:
1131:                         for child in self._children:
1132:                             if child.accepts(fact.kind):
1133:                                 child.receive(fact)
1134: 
1135:         # Replay paths that bypass ``receive`` still need the boundary
1136:         # bookkeeping a live loop would have accumulated.
1137:         self._reconcile_replayed_boundaries()
1138: 
1139:         # Initialize period start from last vertex-level tick.
1140:         # Vertex-level boundary ticks use self._name as tick name.
1141:         # The last such tick's ts is the end of the previous period —
1142:         # the next boundary's since should start from there.
1143:         if self._has_vertex_boundary:
1144:             if hasattr(store, 'last_tick_ts'):
1145:                 ts = store.last_tick_ts(self._name)
1146:                 if ts is not None:
1147:                     self._vertex_period_start = ts
1148:             elif hasattr(store, 'ticks_since'):
1149:                 for tick in reversed(store.ticks_since(0)):
1150:                     if tick.name == self._name:
1151:                         self._vertex_period_start = tick.ts
1152:                         break
1153: 
1154:         return count
1155: 
1156:     def evaluate_boundaries(self) -> list[Tick]:
1157:         """Evaluate boundaries for facts that arrived since the last boundary fire.
1158: 
1159:         Call after replay() to handle externally-emitted facts. During replay,
1160:         boundary evaluation is suppressed — the fold state is rebuilt but
1161:         boundaries don't fire. This method scans facts in the current period
1162:         and checks them against boundary triggers with the fully-rebuilt fold
1163:         state.
1164: 
1165:         Handles kind-based, payload-match, and predicate (fold-state condition)
1166:         boundaries. Does NOT handle count-based boundaries (inherently
1167:         event-driven — they count facts as they arrive via receive()).
1168: 
1169:         Returns list of Ticks produced by fired boundaries.
1170:         """
1171:         if self._store is None:
1172:             return []
1173: 
1174:         ticks: list[Tick] = []
1175: 
1176:         # Determine scan window: facts since the most recent tick.
1177:         # After a boundary fires (or on second evaluate), _vertex_period_start
1178:         # may be None (reset). Use the latest stored tick's timestamp as the
1179:         # authoritative scan start — avoids re-scanning already-evaluated facts.
1180:         since_ts: float = 0.0
1181:         if hasattr(self._store, "ticks_since"):
1182:             stored_ticks = self._store.ticks_since(0)
1183:             if stored_ticks:
1184:                 since_ts = stored_ticks[-1].ts.timestamp()
1185:         if self._vertex_period_start is not None:
1186:             ps_ts = self._vertex_period_start.timestamp()
1187:             if ps_ts > since_ts:
1188:                 since_ts = ps_ts
1189: 
1190:         import time as _time
1191: 
1192:         period_facts = self._store.between(since_ts, _time.time())
1193:         if not period_facts:
1194:             return ticks
1195: 
1196:         # Exclude facts at exactly the scan start — they were already
1197:         # evaluated in a previous cycle (the tick that set since_ts was
1198:         # produced from one of those facts).
1199:         if since_ts > 0 and not self._has_vertex_boundary:
1200:             period_facts = [f for f in period_facts if f.ts > since_ts]
1201:             if not period_facts:
1202:                 return ticks
1203: 
1204:         if self._has_vertex_boundary and not self._boundary_map:
1205:             return self._evaluate_vertex_only_boundaries(period_facts, since_ts)
1206: 
1207:         # Track which loop-level boundaries have fired this evaluation
1208:         # (one fire per boundary per evaluation cycle)
1209:         fired_boundaries: set[str] = set()
1210: 
1211:         for fact in period_facts:
1212:             kind = fact.kind
1213:             payload = fact.payload
1214:             fact_ts = datetime.fromtimestamp(fact.ts, tz=timezone.utc)
1215: 
1216:             # Track vertex-level period start if not set
1217:             if self._has_vertex_boundary and self._vertex_period_start is None:
1218:                 self._vertex_period_start = fact_ts
1219: 
1220:             # --- Vertex-level boundary (declaration order, first match fires) ---
1221:             if kind in self._vertex_boundary_kinds:
1222:                 spec = self._match_vertex_boundary(kind, payload)
1223:                 if spec is not None:
1224:                     tick = self._fire_vertex_boundary(
1225:                         fact_ts,
1226:                         payload,
1227:                         run=spec.run,
1228:                     )
1229:                     self._store_tick(tick)
1230:                     ticks.append(tick)
1231:                     break  # Vertex-level fire ends the period
1232:                 continue
1233: 
1234:             # --- Loop-level boundary ---
1235:             fold_kind = self._boundary_map.get(kind)
1236:             if fold_kind is None or fold_kind in fired_boundaries:
1237:                 continue
1238: 
1239:             # Check payload match conditions
1240:             match = self._boundary_match.get(kind, ())
1241:             if match and not all(payload.get(k) == v for k, v in match):
1242:                 continue
1243: 
1244:             # Check fold-state conditions
1245:             conditions = self._boundary_conditions.get(kind, ())
1246:             if conditions:
1247:                 target_loop = self._loops[fold_kind]
1248:                 if not _eval_conditions(target_loop.state, conditions):
1249:                     continue
1250: 
1251:             # Fire
1252:             target_loop = self._loops[fold_kind]
1253:             tick = target_loop.fire(fact_ts, origin=self._name, boundary_payload=payload)
1254:             self._store_tick(tick)
1255:             ticks.append(tick)
1256:             fired_boundaries.add(fold_kind)
1257: 
1258:         return ticks
1259: 
1260:     def plan_pending_boundaries(
1261:         self,
1262:         facts: tuple[Any, ...],
1263:         ticks: tuple[Any, ...],
1264:         *,
1265:         evaluated_at: float,
1266:     ) -> tuple[Tick, ...]:
1267:         """Evaluate externally pending boundaries from captured evidence only.
1268: 
1269:         This is the storeless counterpart of :meth:`evaluate_boundaries` for
1270:         Arrival source planning. Each boundary's recorded ticks establish its
1271:         event-time period edge. At equal event time, facts received before the
1272:         closing tick belong to that closed period; later arrivals are eligible
1273:         for a new period. A tick's fact cursor is its evidence horizon, not a
1274:         trigger cursor: future-dated facts can already occur before that cursor.
1275:         The method mutates only this detached candidate and never persists.
1276:         Count boundaries remain ingress-driven and are not invented from replay.
1277:         """
1278:         if self._store is not None:
1279:             raise RuntimeError("pending-boundary planning requires a detached vertex")
1280: 
1281:         def tick_time(ts: float) -> float:
1282:             # Runtime ticks are datetimes (microsecond precision). Compare on
1283:             # that same axis or rounding down repeats a consumed fact, while
1284:             # rounding up hides a later receipt carrying the exact same ts.
1285:             # The original fact timestamps and receipt coordinates stay intact.
1286:             return datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, tz=UTC).timestamp()
1287: 
1288:         edges: dict[str, tuple[float, int, int]] = {}
1289:         for tick in ticks:
1290:             if not self._owns_tick(tick):
1291:                 continue
1292:             edge = (tick_time(tick.ts), tick.arrival_ordinal, tick.arrival_seq)
1293:             if tick.name not in edges or edge > edges[tick.name]:
1294:                 edges[tick.name] = edge
1295: 
1296:         def unconsumed(fact: Any, name: str) -> bool:
1297:             edge = edges.get(name)
1298:             return edge is None or (
1299:                 tick_time(fact.ts), fact.arrival_ordinal, fact.arrival_seq
1300:             ) > edge
1301: 
1302:         period_facts = sorted(
1303:             (fact for fact in facts if 0.0 <= fact.ts <= evaluated_at),
1304:             key=lambda fact: (
1305:                 fact.ts,
1306:                 getattr(fact, "arrival_ordinal", 0),
1307:                 getattr(fact, "arrival_seq", 0),
1308:             ),
1309:         )
1310:         if not period_facts:
1311:             return ()
1312: 
1313:         planned: list[Tick] = []
1314:         fired_boundaries: set[str] = set()
1315:         for fact in period_facts:
1316:             kind = fact.kind
1317:             payload = fact.payload
1318:             fact_ts = datetime.fromtimestamp(fact.ts, tz=timezone.utc)
1319:             if (
1320:                 self._has_vertex_boundary
1321:                 and self._vertex_period_start is None
1322:                 and unconsumed(fact, self._name)
1323:             ):
1324:                 self._vertex_period_start = fact_ts
1325: 
1326:             if kind in self._vertex_boundary_kinds:
1327:                 if not unconsumed(fact, self._name):
1328:                     continue
1329:                 spec = self._match_vertex_boundary(kind, payload)
1330:                 if spec is not None:
1331:                     planned.append(self._fire_vertex_boundary(fact_ts, payload, run=spec.run))
1332:                     break
1333:                 continue
1334: 
1335:             fold_kind = self._boundary_map.get(kind)
1336:             if fold_kind is None or fold_kind in fired_boundaries:
1337:                 continue
1338:             if not unconsumed(fact, fold_kind):
1339:                 continue
1340:             match = self._boundary_match.get(kind, ())
1341:             if match and not all(payload.get(key) == value for key, value in match):
1342:                 continue
1343:             conditions = self._boundary_conditions.get(kind, ())
1344:             target_loop = self._loops[fold_kind]
1345:             if conditions and not _eval_conditions(target_loop.state, conditions):
1346:                 continue
1347:             planned.append(
1348:                 target_loop.fire(
1349:                     fact_ts,
1350:                     origin=self._name,
1351:                     boundary_payload=payload,
1352:                 )
1353:             )
1354:             fired_boundaries.add(fold_kind)
1355:         return tuple(planned)
1356: 
1357:     def _evaluate_vertex_only_boundaries(
1358:         self,
1359:         period_facts: list,
1360:         since_ts: float,
1361:     ) -> list[Tick]:
1362:         """Evaluate boundaries when only vertex-level boundaries exist.
1363: 
1364:         Fast path with no loop-level boundary scanning. A vertex may declare
1365:         several vertex-level boundaries; each candidate fact is checked against
1366:         them in declaration order (``_match_vertex_boundary`` — first match
1367:         fires). The first fact that fires ends the scan: a vertex-level fire
1368:         snapshots the whole vertex and resets the period.
1369:         """
1370:         ticks: list[Tick] = []
1371:         boundary_kinds = self._vertex_boundary_kinds
1372:         # Add 1μs tolerance for float→datetime→float round-trip precision loss
1373:         adjusted_since = since_ts + 1e-6 if since_ts > 0 else 0
1374:         for fact in period_facts:
1375:             if adjusted_since > 0 and fact.ts <= adjusted_since:
1376:                 continue
1377:             kind = fact.kind
1378:             if kind not in boundary_kinds:
1379:                 continue
1380:             fact_ts = datetime.fromtimestamp(fact.ts, tz=timezone.utc)
1381:             if self._vertex_period_start is None:
1382:                 self._vertex_period_start = fact_ts
1383:             spec = self._match_vertex_boundary(kind, fact.payload)
1384:             if spec is None:
1385:                 continue
1386:             tick = self._fire_vertex_boundary(
1387:                 fact_ts,
1388:                 fact.payload,
1389:                 run=spec.run,
1390:             )
1391:             self._store_tick(tick)
1392:             ticks.append(tick)
1393:             return ticks
1394:         return ticks
1395: 
1396:     def to_fact(self, tick: Tick) -> Fact:
1397:         """Convert a Tick to a Fact with this vertex as observer.
1398: 
1399:         Used when forwarding ticks from one vertex to another.
1400:         The tick becomes a fact with kind="tick.{tick.name}" and
1401:         the vertex name as observer. Origin is preserved from the tick.
1402:         """
1403:         from atoms import Fact
1404: 
1405:         return Fact(
1406:             kind=f"tick.{tick.name}",
1407:             ts=tick.ts.timestamp(),
1408:             payload=tick.payload,
1409:             observer=self._name,
1410:             origin=tick.origin,
1411:         )
1412: 
1413:     def _store_tick(self, tick: Tick) -> TickAttestation | None:
1414:         """Persist tick to store if it supports tick persistence.
1415: 
1416:         A live boundary mint — every tick from a fired boundary (seal, count,
1417:         predicate) lands here. The tick-signing floor (decision design/tick
1418:         -signing-era-is-a-floor) is enforced BY DEFAULT on append_tick, so a
1419:         keyless mint in the signed era is refused without this path opting in;
1420:         only re-mint paths (rebirth/slice) opt out explicitly.
1421: 
1422:         Returns the committed tick row's attestation for the write receipt —
1423:         from ``append_tick_attested`` (which reads the committed signature
1424:         back inside the write transaction; SOL-R3-02) when the store offers
1425:         it, else the ``tick_signature_state`` read-back; None when the store
1426:         doesn't persist ticks or doesn't report attestation.
1427:         """
1428:         if self._store is None or not hasattr(self._store, "append_tick"):
1429:             return None
1430:         appender = getattr(self._store, "append_tick_attested", None)
1431:         if appender is not None:
1432:             _, signature = appender(tick)
1433:             return TickAttestation(signed=signature is not None, chained=True)
1434:         return self._tick_attestation(self._store.append_tick(tick))
1435: 
1436:     def _fact_attestation(self, fact_id: str | None, observer: str) -> FactAttestation | None:
1437:         """Persisted signature state of the just-committed fact row.
1438: 
1439:         Read back from the store (``fact_signature``) — the committed row is
1440:         the authority, never local key configuration. None when the store
1441:         doesn't report attestation (no ``fact_signature`` read-back, or the
1442:         store doesn't track ids) — a tri-state, not "unsigned".
1443:         """
1444:         if fact_id is None:
1445:             return None
1446:         reader = getattr(self._store, "fact_signature", None)
1447:         if reader is None:
1448:             return None
1449:         return FactAttestation(
1450:             signed=reader(fact_id) is not None,
1451:             observer=observer,
1452:         )
1453: 
1454:     def _tick_attestation(self, tick_row_id: str | None) -> TickAttestation | None:
1455:         """Persisted chain/signature state of the just-committed tick row.
1456: 
1457:         Same committed-row authority as :meth:`_fact_attestation`, for the
1458:         boundary tick a receive fired. None when no tick row was committed
1459:         or the store has no ``tick_signature_state`` read-back.
1460:         """
1461:         if tick_row_id is None:
1462:             return None
1463:         reader = getattr(self._store, "tick_signature_state", None)
1464:         if reader is None:
1465:             return None
1466:         state = reader(tick_row_id)
1467:         if state is None:
1468:             return None
1469:         signature, chained = state
1470:         return TickAttestation(signed=signature is not None, chained=chained)
1471: 
1472:     def _tick_to_fact(self, tick: Tick, child_name: str) -> Fact:
1473:         """Convert a child's Tick to a Fact for re-entry.
1474: 
1475:         The tick's name becomes the fact kind (emit name → kind).
1476:         The child vertex name becomes the observer.
1477:         Payload is spread into the fact. Origin is preserved from the tick.
1478:         """
1479:         from atoms import Fact
1480: 
1481:         payload = tick.payload if isinstance(tick.payload, dict) else {"value": tick.payload}
1482:         return Fact(
1483:             kind=tick.name,
1484:             ts=tick.ts.timestamp(),
1485:             payload=payload,
1486:             observer=child_name,
1487:             origin=tick.origin,
1488:         )
1489: 
1490:     def ingest(
1491:         self,
1492:         kind: str,
1493:         payload: dict,
1494:         observer: str,
1495:         grant: Grant | None = None,
1496:     ) -> Tick | None:
1497:         """Convenience: create a Fact and receive it in one call.
1498: 
1499:         Useful for sources and bridges that have raw data rather than
1500:         pre-constructed Facts.
1501: 
1502:         Args:
1503:             kind: Fact kind
1504:             payload: Dict payload (will be wrapped in Fact.of)
1505:             observer: Who produced this observation
1506:             grant: Optional Grant for potential gating
1507: 
1508:         Returns:
1509:             Tick if a boundary fired, None otherwise.
1510:         """
1511:         from atoms import Fact
1512: 
1513:         fact = Fact.of(kind, observer, **payload)
1514:         return self.receive(fact, grant)

=== libs/engine/src/engine/canonical_audit.py ===
1: """canonical_audit — does the derived index still agree with the canonical log?
2: 
3: An arrival-canonical store has two artifacts: the ``.arrival`` log, which IS
4: the store, and the sibling ``.db``, which is an index derived from it. Every
5: verification surface before this module walked the *index* only, so an
6: out-of-band sqlite row — a row the log never carried — still rendered
7: ``✓ chain intact`` at rc=0. That is a false attestation of exactly the lie-class
8: the chain exists to prevent (design/store/verify-canonical-agreement).
9: 
10: This module is the reader that judges the two artifacts against each other.
11: 
12: **Pure reader, by contract.** Nothing here constructs an :class:`~engine.
13: arrival_store.ArrivalStore` or :class:`~engine.jsonl_store.JsonlStore`. Those
14: constructors *repair* — catch-up, torn-line truncation, rebuild-on-divergence
15: — and repair destroys the evidence verification exists to inspect. Open-time
16: recovery and verification are opposite contracts, so they never share a code
17: path: the log is read with pure readers, the index with a read-only sqlite
18: connection, and no mark or metadata is ever written.
19: 
20: Two depths:
21: 
22: ``audit_agreement``  (L1, the default gate)
23:     Five checks per §D3 for arrival stores:
24:     - ``index``: derived index exists and is readable.
25:     - ``consumed``: stamped ResumeMark vs log head ordinal (suffix count via
26:       ``walk_marked`` — O(records behind)).
27:     - ``rewound``: any index row with arrival_ordinal > consumed_ordinal.
28:     - ``counts``: stamped counters vs COUNT(*), plus NULL-coordinate backstop.
29:     - ``consumed_edge``: read record at consumed ordinal via
30:       :meth:`engine.arrival.ArrivalLog.anchor`, expand ``rows_of_record``,
31:       and ``row_matches`` every row.
32:     L1 MUST NOT call ``ArrivalLog.read`` or ``ArrivalLog.walk`` (both walk from zero).
33: 
34: ``audit_deep``  (``--deep``)
35:     L1 (verifying 1 anchor record) then full :meth:`engine.arrival.ArrivalLog.walk`
36:     (density, hashes, ordinals, chain, verifying all N records), row-by-row index
37:     comparison over ``rows_of_record``, multiset derived log audit
38:     (:func:`engine.arrival_projection.audit_derived_log`), and tick hash chain
39:     re-derived from log content. Exactly 1 + N records verified in total.
40: """
41:

93: @dataclass(frozen=True)
94: class Check:
95:     """One named agreement check and its verdict.
96: 
97:     ``name`` is the handle a caller reports ("index", "consumed", "rewound",
98:     "counts", "consumed_edge", "content", "chain", "derived_log", …) so
99:     the output can say WHICH check failed rather than "verification failed".
100:     """
101: 
102:     name: str
103:     ok: bool
104:     detail: str = ""
105:     behind_by: int = 0
106:     at_ordinal: int = -1
107: 
108:     def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
109:         return {
110:             "check": self.name,
111:             "ok": self.ok,
112:             "detail": self.detail,
113:             "behind_by": self.behind_by,
114:             "at_ordinal": self.at_ordinal,
115:         }
116: 
117: 
118: @dataclass(frozen=True)
119: class AgreementReport:
120:     """The verdict of an audit: every check that ran, in the order it ran."""
121: 
122:     checks: tuple[Check, ...] = ()
123:     deep: bool = False
124:     counts: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
125: 
126:     @property
127:     def ok(self) -> bool:
128:         return all(c.ok for c in self.checks)
129: 
130:     @property
131:     def divergences(self) -> tuple[Check, ...]:
132:         return tuple(c for c in self.checks if not c.ok)
133: 
134:     @property
135:     def index_behind(self) -> bool:
136:         """Diverged, but only because the index is behind the log.
137: 
138:         A location claim, never an innocence claim. True when there is at
139:         least one divergence and every divergence has ``behind_by > 0`` (the
140:         index has not consumed through the arrival log head). Any other
141:         divergence — rewound marker, count mismatch, content mismatch, chain
142:         break — keeps this False.
143:         """
144:         d = self.divergences
145:         return bool(d) and all(c.behind_by > 0 for c in d)
146: 
147:     def summary(self) -> str:
148:         """One line naming the failures — '' when everything agreed."""
149:         return "; ".join(f"{c.name}: {c.detail}" for c in self.divergences)
150: 
151:     def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
152:         return {
153:             "ok": self.ok,
154:             "deep": self.deep,
155:             "index_behind": self.index_behind,
156:             "checks": [c.as_dict() for c in self.checks],
157:             **({"counts": dict(self.counts)} if self.counts else {}),
158:         }
