410: 
411: def canonical_location(location: str) -> str:
412:     """The one string form of a location, for the binding. DELETE IN SLICE 5.
413: 
414:     ``Path.resolve()``: relative paths become absolute against the process cwd,
415:     ``..`` segments collapse, and symlinks resolve to their target — so two
416:     vertices reaching one log by different routes present one binding key
417:     rather than two, which is exactly the first contact the binding exists to
418:     prevent. Non-strict by default, so a location that does not exist yet
419:     still canonicalizes; the mint path depends on that.
420: 
421:     **Scope the claim.** This assumes a location is a filesystem path. §02 is
422:     explicit that a ``location`` may be a DSN or a service URL, and resolving
423:     one of those against the cwd would mangle it. That is bounded and it dies
424:     with this function: the value is used ONLY as the binding key and as the
425:     diagnostic ``location`` field, never as a journal key — journals are keyed
426:     by lineage — so a mangled location degrades to "no binding found", which
427:     is first contact, the state the binding improves on rather than
428:     guarantees. The file adapter is the only registered backend, and slice 5
429:     removes the binding before a second one can arrive.
430: 
431:     **This is a SPELLING, not an identity**, and the difference is the whole of
432:     ``finding:s3wp3-canonical-location-alias-first-contact``. ``resolve()``
433:     normalizes a path; it does not establish which filesystem object a path
434:     names. A case-variant spelling on a case-insensitive filesystem — the macOS
435:     default — or a second mount of the same volume reaches the very same store
436:     through a string this function returns unchanged and different. Bound under
437:     one spelling and presented under the other, the store has no binding, reads
438:     as first contact, and a replacement with a fresh lineage walks past
439:     :class:`~engine.arrival_head_attestation.LineageReplaced`. That hole is
440:     closed by :func:`aliased_lineage`, which asks the filesystem rather than
441:     the string.
442: 
443:     Residuals, both stated rather than papered over: a store reached through a
444:     symlink whose target later changes presents a different canonical form and
445:     is first contact again; and two aliases that genuinely report DIFFERENT
446:     ``(st_dev, st_ino)`` — two network mounts of one export are the ordinary
447:     case — are beyond anything a client can detect from here. Path-keying is
448:     transitional for exactly these reasons, and the lineage-keyed journal is
449:     the memory that does not have them.
450:     """
451:     return str(Path(location).resolve())
452: 
453: 
454: #: A filesystem object's identity on this host: the device and inode a path
455: #: currently resolves to. Never RECORDED — inodes go stale when a file is
456: #: recreated and get recycled onto unrelated files, so a stored one is a claim
457: #: that rots into a false match. Only ever compared live, at the moment both
458: #: sides are stat'd.
459: Identity = tuple[int, int]
460: 
461: 
462: def _identity_of(location: str) -> Identity | None:
463:     """What filesystem object this path names right now, or None if it is absent.
464: 
465:     The split is between an ANSWER and an unanswered question, and the two used
466:     to be one branch. A path that does not exist genuinely names no object —
467:     that is None, and it is correct, and the mint path depends on it. A path
468:     that DOES exist and will not stat (a permission wall, a transient I/O
469:     error, a partially mounted volume) leaves the question open, and answering
470:     None there means a store replaced under an aliased spelling opens as first
471:     contact.
472:     """
473:     try:
474:         stat = Path(location).stat()
475:     except FileNotFoundError:
476:         return None
477:     except OSError as exc:
478:         raise BindingProbeUnanswered(
479:             f"{location} exists and storage would not stat it ({exc}), so "
480:             "this open cannot tell whether it names the same store as a "
481:             "recorded binding. Nothing has been accepted or written — "
482:             f"{storage_advice(exc)}"
483:         ) from exc
484:     return (stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino)
485: 
486: 
487: def match_identity(
488:     presenting: Identity | None,
489:     recorded: Sequence[tuple[str, str, Identity | None]],
490: ) -> str | None:
491:     """The lineage bound to another spelling of the SAME filesystem object.
492: 
493:     Pure, and separated from the stat calls on purpose: the alias this closes
494:     can only be CONSTRUCTED on a case-insensitive filesystem, so a test that
495:     builds one is skipped on a case-sensitive CI runner. The judgment is the
496:     part worth pinning everywhere, so it takes identities as arguments and is
497:     testable on any filesystem, while the construction test carries an honest
498:     skip.
499: 
500:     ``recorded`` is (location, lineage, identity) in file order, so the newest
501:     binding for an aliased object wins — the same rule
502:     :func:`~engine.arrival_head_attestation.bound_lineage` applies to an exact
503:     location. An unstattable recorded path contributes nothing.
504:     """
505:     if presenting is None:
506:         return None
507:     found: str | None = None
508:     for _location, lineage, identity in recorded:
509:         if identity is not None and identity == presenting:
510:             found = lineage
511:     return found
512: 
513: 
514: _IDENTITY_UNSET = object()
515: 
516: 
517: def aliased_lineage(
518:     location: str, *, identity: Identity | None | object = _IDENTITY_UNSET
519: ) -> str | None:
520:     """The lineage bound to this store under a DIFFERENT spelling.
521: 
522:     Consulted only when the presenting location has no binding of its own —
523:     which is the one moment the hole is open, and which keeps every subsequent
524:     open free of the sweep. It live-stats each recorded binding; a store bound
525:     under one spelling and opened under another is then NOT first contact, and
526:     a replacement at that location refuses.
527: 
528:     The filesystem namespace is ambient authority: two names for one object is
529:     a property of the namespace rather than of the store, so asking the
530:     filesystem which object a name currently denotes is a location claim about
531:     this host and not a verdict about the store. DELETE IN SLICE 5 with the
532:     rest of the binding.
533:     """
534:     # An explicit None means a file path is absent: still read and validate
535:     # the historical bindings before returning no alias. Opaque registry keys
536:     # never call this function; AttestedLedger gates that branch on the
537:     # adapter's ``filesystem`` policy.
538:     try:
539:         text = bindings_path().read_text(encoding="utf-8")
540:     except FileNotFoundError:
541:         # ABSENT is an answer: nothing has ever been bound here.
542:         return None
543:     except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
544:         raise BindingsUnreadable(
545:             f"the bindings file at {bindings_path()} is not valid UTF-8 "
546:             f"({exc}), so this open cannot tell whether another spelling of "
547:             "this store is already bound. Nothing has been accepted or "
548:             "written — repair or remove the file"
549:         ) from exc
550:     except OSError as exc:
551:         raise BindingProbeUnanswered(
552:             f"the bindings file at {bindings_path()} exists and storage "
553:             f"would not yield it ({exc}), so this open cannot tell whether "
554:             "this location already presented a different lineage. Nothing has "
555:             f"been accepted or written — {storage_advice(exc)}"
556:         ) from exc
557:     recorded: list[tuple[str, str, Identity | None]] = []
558:     for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
559:         stripped = line.strip()
560:         if not stripped:
561:             continue
562:         try:
563:             decoded = json.loads(stripped)
564:         except ValueError as exc:
565:             raise BindingsUnreadable(
566:                 f"line {number} of {bindings_path()} does not parse ({exc}), "
567:                 "and a line that cannot be read may be the binding that names "
568:                 "this location. Nothing has been accepted or written — repair "
569:                 "or remove the line"
570:             ) from exc
571:         where = decoded.get("location") if isinstance(decoded, dict) else None
572:         lineage = decoded.get("lineage") if isinstance(decoded, dict) else None
573:         if not (isinstance(where, str) and isinstance(lineage, str)):
574:             # READ, and not interpretable as a binding — a CONTENT failure.
575:             raise BindingsUnreadable(
576:                 f"line {number} of {bindings_path()} is valid JSON but "
577:                 "carries no location and lineage, so it cannot be read as a "
578:                 "binding and cannot be ruled out as naming this store. "
579:                 "Nothing has been accepted or written — repair or remove the "
580:                 "line"
581:             )
582:         # Historical bindings are canonical file paths. Future opaque keys
583:         # are namespaced and must never be handed to Path.stat by this seam.
584:         if where.startswith("backend:"):
585:             continue
586:         recorded.append((where, lineage, _identity_of(where)))
587:     presenting = (
588:         _identity_of(location)
589:         if identity is _IDENTITY_UNSET
590:         else cast(Identity | None, identity)
591:     )
592:     return match_identity(presenting, recorded)
593: 
594: 
595: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
596: # Producers — the entries something other than an ordinary open writes
597: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
598: 
599: 
600: def bootstrap(
601:     head: Head,
602:     *,
603:     level: Level,
604:     location: str,
605:     observed_at: float,
606:     binding: BindingIdentity | None = None,
607: ) -> Path:
608:     """The first entry for a lineage, plus its binding. Returns the journal.
609: 
610:     ``Level.MINT`` when this process minted the genesis, ``Level.FIRST_CONTACT``
611:     when an already-existing store was opened for the first time. **Slice 6's
612:     verification depends on the distinction**: a journal beginning at ``mint``
613:     was witnessed from genesis forward and every head in it is accounted for;
614:     one beginning at ``first-contact`` was trusted on sight, and that label is
615:     permanent. Slice 4's sidecar must produce the former for every migrated
616:     store by minting through :class:`AttestedLedger`, and slice 6 checks it.
617: 
618:     No other level is admitted. ``COMMIT``, ``DESCENDANT`` and ``FULL`` each
619:     name evidence a first entry cannot have — there was nothing to descend
620:     from — so accepting one would let a journal open with a claim stronger than
621:     anything that happened.
622: 
623:     The binding is recorded here rather than by the caller so that the
624:     canonical form is applied in exactly one place (see
625:     :func:`canonical_location`); a caller that wrote its own binding is how the
626:     two spellings diverge.
627:     """
628:     if level not in (Level.MINT, Level.FIRST_CONTACT):
629:         raise ValueError(
630:             f"a bootstrap entry may be {Level.MINT.value!r} or "
631:             f"{Level.FIRST_CONTACT.value!r}, not {level.value!r} — every other "
632:             "level names evidence a first entry cannot have, because there was "
633:             "nothing before it to descend from or verify against"
634:         )
635:     canonical = binding.key if binding is not None else canonical_location(location)
636:     path = append_entry(
637:         HeadAttestation(
638:             head=head,
639:             kind=Kind.BOOTSTRAP,
640:             level=level,
641:             observed_at=observed_at,
642:             location=canonical,
643:         )
644:     )
645:     record_binding(canonical, head.lineage, observed_at)
646:     return path
647: 
648: 
649: def trust_reset(
650:     *,
651:     accepted: Head,
652:     abandoned: Head | None,
653:     refused: Head | None,
654:     reason: str,
655:     location: str,
656:     observed_at: float,
657:     level: Level = Level.FIRST_CONTACT,
658: ) -> Path:
659:     """The operator ceremony's entry, opening a new trust epoch.
660: 
661:     §11's last row asks for exactly this — *"perform explicit trust reset from
662:     archives or operator ceremony and record the gap"* — against the unsafe
663:     shortcut of treating the first presented database as historically proven.
664:     Refusals are terminal for the open and no automatic path may abandon one;
665:     this is the licensed way down, and it is a function an operator's ceremony
666:     calls rather than anything the seam can reach.
667: 
668:     The gap goes in ``note`` and it is the point of the entry: the head being
669:     abandoned, the head that was refused, and why. Entries before the reset
670:     stay in the journal as **evidence, not as claims** — the read scope moves,
671:     the history does not.
672: 
673:     ``level`` defaults to the WEAKEST claim available. An operator ceremony may
674:     have verified the accepted head from genesis, and one that did should pass
675:     ``Level.FULL``; one that took a head from an archive on an operator's word
676:     has proven nothing, which is what ``first-contact`` says. Defaulting down
677:     is deliberate — a default can then only under-claim, and an entry that
678:     under-claims costs a later audit some work while one that over-claims is a
679:     lie the journal keeps forever.
680: 
681:     **The reset is bound to the entry it is appended after**, which is what
682:     makes a replayed copy inexpressible as valid — see
683:     :attr:`~engine.arrival_head_attestation.HeadAttestation.follows`. Binding
684:     it here is the FOOTGUN GUARD, not the protection: an operator constructing
685:     an entry by hand still produces one, and the protection is the read-time
686:     validation in ``_epoch_of``, which is what every reader performs. A writer
687:     that raced another appender between this read and its own write produces a
688:     binding that no longer matches, and that reset is then not honored — the
689:     refusal-side failure, and the reason the read-time half is the load-bearing
690:     one.
691: 
692:     **What a reset fences out.** A reset decrees trust in *N*, and verified
693:     descendants of *N* that pass through history the decree abandoned are
694:     REFUSED (:class:`AbandonedHistoryFenced`) until a new decree reaches them.
695:     Genuine recovery of that history therefore costs exactly one ceremony:
696:     decree the recovered head, and the fence lifts.
697: 
698:     This corrects what this docstring said before amendment #6, which was that
699:     such descendants were accepted. They were, and that was the silent loop —
700:     an accepted re-presentation journaled itself back into the current epoch and
701:     every later open read UNCHANGED (``finding:s3-reset-descendant-silent-loop``).
702: 
703:     The CLI surface for the ceremony is slice 5's cut. This is the producer, so
704:     slices 4 and 6 have something to call.
705:     """
706:     previous = last_entry(accepted.lineage)
707:     follows = (
708:         (0, "") if previous is None else (previous[0], entry_identity(previous[1]))
709:     )
710:     if not reason.strip():
711:         raise ValueError(
712:             "a trust reset records the gap it opens — an empty reason would "
713:             "leave the journal holding the abandonment without the evidence "
714:             "for it, which is the whole thing the ceremony exists to write down"
715:         )
716:     note = (
717:         f"trust reset: abandoning {_head_text(abandoned)}, "
718:         f"refused {_head_text(refused)}, accepting "
719:         f"{accepted.lineage}/{accepted.ordinal}/{accepted.record_hash}. "
720:         f"{reason.strip()}"
721:     )
722:     entry = HeadAttestation(
723:         head=accepted,
724:         kind=Kind.TRUST_RESET,
725:         level=level,
726:         observed_at=observed_at,
727:         location=canonical_location(location),
728:         note=note,
729:         follows=follows,
730:     )
731:     path = append_entry(entry)
732:     _confirm_reset_took_effect(entry)
733:     return path
734: 
735: 
736: def _confirm_reset_took_effect(entry: HeadAttestation) -> None:
737:     """Read the ceremony back, and say so loudly if it did not take.
738: 
739:     The position claim buys its protection with an obligation. Binding a reset
740:     to the line it follows means reading the tail and then appending, and there
741:     is NO lock to hold across the two — the journal is append-only precisely so
742:     that writers need none. So an automated append (an ordinary open, an audit)
743:     landing in that window leaves a legitimate, freshly written reset carrying a
744:     position that is already stale, and a later reader will decline to honor it.
745: 
746:     The direction is safe — an unhonored reset leaves *K* at the higher
747:     abandoned head, which refuses rather than accepts. What is NOT safe is
748:     silence: an operator who ran the ceremony, saw it return, and believes their
749:     store will now open is holding a false belief that the next open will
750:     contradict. So the entry is read back and checked against the same judgment
751:     every reader applies, and a ceremony that did not take effect raises.
752: 
753:     Emit-then-read-back rather than trust-the-write, which is the store's own
754:     ethos: the append landing is not the same claim as the append counting.
755:     """
756:     try:
757:         epoch = read_journal(entry.head.lineage).epoch
758:     except AttestationRefusal as exc:
759:         raise TrustResetNotHonored(
760:             "the trust reset was APPENDED, and the journal could not then be "
761:             f"read back to confirm it took effect: {exc}. The entry is in the "
762:             "file as evidence; whether it opens an epoch is unconfirmed",
763:             entry=entry,
764:         ) from exc
765:     if not epoch or epoch[0] != entry:
766:         raise TrustResetNotHonored(
767:             "the trust reset was APPENDED and is NOT honored as an epoch "
768:             "boundary — another entry landed between reading the tail and "
769:             "writing, so the position this reset records is already stale. "
770:             "Nothing was lost and nothing was wrongly accepted: the previous "
771:             "head still stands, so opens keep refusing. Run the ceremony again "
772:             "against the journal as it now is",
773:             entry=entry,
774:         )
775: 
776: 
777: def audit(
778:     ledger: ArrivalLedger,
779:     *,
780:     presented: Head,
781:     epoch: Sequence[HeadAttestation],
782:     projection: str,
783:     location: str,
784:     observed_at: float,
785: ) -> Path:
786:     """The full chain-plus-projection audit (§D.5). Returns the journal.
787: 
788:     Three things, and the third is what makes the cheap per-open check safe:
789: 
790:     1. ``verify(Full(through=presented))`` — grammar, density, lineage and the
791:        hash chain for the complete prefix.
792:     2. Every head journaled **in the current trust epoch** is still present at
793:        its own ordinal with its own hash. An advance accepted on partial
794:        evidence is re-examined against the complete record of everything
795:        accepted since the last reset — which a single-value cache could not
796:        offer at any price, because it would have forgotten those heads.
797:     3. Only then, an ``audit``/``full`` entry carrying the head the audit
798:        covered and, in ``note``, the projection-agreement result.
799: 
800:     **The all-journaled-heads lookup is built here and cannot be passed in.**
801:     :func:`~engine.arrival_head_attestation.unaccounted_heads` takes an injected
802:     ``at_ordinal`` so the neutral module never reaches for a backend, and an
803:     injection point is a place a fabricated head can lie: a lookup that
804:     answered from the journal, from a cache, or from the projection would
805:     "confirm" every entry without the store having been asked. So this
806:     function accepts no lookup parameter. It builds one from ``ledger.head_at``,
807:     which resolves through a verified walk from ordinal 0 — the same evidence
808:     ``verify`` gathers, obtained through custody rather than around it.
809: 
810:     ``projection`` is the agreement result as a STRING, taken as an input so
811:     this module never imports the projection auditor — §D.5's own discipline,
812:     and the reason the audit stays callable from a CLI that has already
813:     computed it.
814: 
815:     **Writing an entry from a verification path is not what F2 forbids.** F2
816:     forbids repairing the store under judgment. Recording evidence outside it
817:     is the entire purpose of a witness.
818: 
819:     Cost: the full walk, plus one verified walk per journaled head in the
820:     epoch. "Periodic" is operator cadence and this is the operator-cadence
821:     path, so the honest lookup is worth more than a cheaper one — but the cost
822:     is real, and a store whose epoch holds many entries is where a
823:     single-walk-with-a-table form would earn its keep. Named rather than
824:     pre-paid; its forcing consumer is a store large enough to notice.
825:     """
826:     ledger.verify(Full(through=presented))
827:     unaccounted = unaccounted_heads(epoch, _vouched_at(ledger, presented.lineage))
828:     if unaccounted:
829:         raise AuditFoundUnaccountedHeads(
830:             "the store can no longer account for "
831:             f"{len(unaccounted)} head(s) journaled in the current trust epoch: "
832:             + "; ".join(
833:                 f"ordinal {entry.head.ordinal} ({entry.head.record_hash})"
834:                 for entry in unaccounted
835:             )
836:             + ". No audit entry was written — one would record a verification "
837:             "that did not happen. Locate a replica or backup that holds them, "
838:             "or run the explicit trust-reset ceremony and record the gap",
839:             heads=tuple(unaccounted),
840:         )
841:     return append_entry(
842:         HeadAttestation(
843:             head=presented,
844:             kind=Kind.AUDIT,
845:             level=Level.FULL,
846:             observed_at=observed_at,
847:             location=canonical_location(location),
848:             note=projection,
849:         )
850:     )
851: 
852: 
853: def days_since_audit(read: JournalRead, now: float) -> float | None:
854:     """Days since the last audit entry in the CURRENT epoch, or None.
855: 
856:     Report only. The open path never triggers an audit, because a full walk at
857:     open is exactly what the adapter refused to pay under an ``Open`` label —
858:     an operation that quietly upgraded its own verification level would be
859:     lying about its cost. Wiring a command to append an audit entry is slice
860:     5's CLI cut.
861: 
862:     Epoch-scoped for the same reason *K* is: an audit that ran before a trust
863:     reset covered a history the reset abandoned, so counting it would report
864:     freshness the current epoch has not earned. ``None`` means "no audit has
865:     covered this epoch", which is different from "the last one was long ago"
866:     and is why this does not answer with an age of infinity.
867:     """
868:     stamps = [
869:         entry.observed_at for entry in read.epoch if entry.kind is Kind.AUDIT
870:     ]
871:     if not stamps:
872:         return None
873:     return (now - max(stamps)) / _SECONDS_PER_DAY
874: 
875: 
876: def _head_text(head: Head | None) -> str:
877:     """A head for a human, or an explicit nothing."""
878:     if head is None:
879:         return "(none)"
880:     return f"{head.lineage}/{head.ordinal}/{head.record_hash}"
881: 
882: 
883: def _remembered_floor(read: JournalRead) -> int | None:
884:     """The lowest ordinal the journal already knows the accepted head is at.
885: 
886:     One number for all three states of a read, which is what lets the
887:     across-time re-observation be decided in one place rather than repeated on
888:     each comparison branch. An established head knows its own ordinal; a bound
889:     knows at least its own; an unreadable read and an absent journal know
890:     nothing and answer ``None``, because a store cannot look like it went
891:     backward relative to a memory that holds no position.
892:     """
893:     known = read.known
894:     if isinstance(known, EstablishedHead):
895:         return known.entry.head.ordinal
896:     if isinstance(known, HeadLowerBound):
897:         return known.at_least.head.ordinal
898:     return None
899: 
900: 
901: def _vouched_at(
902:     ledger: ArrivalLedger, lineage: str
903: ) -> Callable[[int], Head | None]:
904:     """A lookup that answers only what the LEDGER vouches for at an ordinal.
905: 
906:     ``head_at`` resolves through a verified walk, so an answer here means the
907:     chain from genesis reaches that coordinate and holds that record. A refusal
908:     means the ledger will not vouch for anything there, and ``None`` is the
909:     honest spelling of that — the caller then treats the head as unaccounted,
910:     which is the refusing direction.
911: 
912:     Broad catch, and it is safe in exactly one direction. The contract's
913:     ``head_at`` says it "answers or it refuses" without naming an exception
914:     family, and the file adapter's "no record at that ordinal" is its own
915:     backend error rather than a ``ContractRefusal``, so a neutral caller cannot
916:     enumerate the refusals without naming a backend
917:     (``finding:s3wp3-head-at-refusal-family-unnamed``). Catching broadly is
918:     sound here because every catch lands on "unaccounted", which REFUSES; the
919:     opposite default — treating an unrecognized failure as agreement — is the
920:     silent-acceptance hazard, and that is the direction this must never fail in.
921:     """
922: 
923:     def at_ordinal(ordinal: int) -> Head | None:
924:         try:
925:             return ledger.head_at(Watermark(lineage=lineage, ordinal=ordinal))
926:         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — see the docstring: fails to REFUSE
927:             return None
928: 
929:     return at_ordinal
930: 
931: 
932: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
933: # The seam
934: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
935: 
936: 
937: class _HeadEvidence(Protocol):
938:     """The read-only evidence needed by witness comparison."""
939: 
940:     def verify(self, scope: VerifyScope) -> Head: ...
941: 
942:     def head_at(self, watermark: Watermark) -> Head: ...
943: 
944: 
945: def complete_projection_custody(
946:     evidence: _HeadEvidence,
947:     *,
948:     captured: Head,
949:     represented: Watermark,
950:     lineage_refusal: Callable[[str], BaseException] = NotAuthority,
951:     conflict_refusal: Callable[[str], BaseException] = HeadMismatch,
952: ) -> Head:
953:     """Complete one projection watermark against independently captured custody.
954: 
955:     The caller owns missing/behind policy and its public refusal family. This
956:     seam owns the evidence rule shared by fresh reads and CURRENT writers: the
957:     represented lineage must be the captured lineage, ``head_at`` must vouch
958:     for the exact reported coordinate, and a report at captured height must
959:     name the captured full head. A projection that advanced after capture is
960:     legitimate once custody vouches for it, but the bounded operation still
961:     receives the captured head.
962: 
963:     Backend ``head_at`` refusals deliberately pass through unchanged. They are
964:     the backend-neutral contract's evidence that the reported prefix does not
965:     exist, and wrapping them here would erase the cause callers already expose.
966:     """
967:     if represented.lineage != captured.lineage:
968:         raise lineage_refusal(
969:             f"projection represents {represented.lineage}, not {captured.lineage}"
970:         )
971:     observed = evidence.head_at(represented)
972:     if (
973:         observed.lineage != represented.lineage
974:         or observed.ordinal != represented.ordinal
975:     ):
976:         raise conflict_refusal(
977:             "custody resolved the projection watermark to a different coordinate"
978:         )
979:     if represented.ordinal == captured.ordinal and observed != captured:
980:         raise conflict_refusal(
981:             "projection head disagrees with captured custody head"
982:         )
983:     return captured if observed.ordinal > captured.ordinal else observed
984: 
985: 
986: class _HeadObservation:
987:     """Pure witness comparison shared by ordinary open and restoration proof.
988: 
989:     This object has no custody mutations and does not write observations.
990:     A restoration can test a bounded proposed prefix without accepting it.
991:     """
992: 
993:     def __init__(
994:         self,
995:         ledger: _HeadEvidence,
996:         *,
997:         location: str,
998:         query: ArrivalQuery | None = None,
999:         clock: Callable[[], float] = time.time,
1000:         binding: BindingIdentity | None = None,
1001:     ) -> None:
1002:         self._evidence = ledger
1003:         self._location = location
1004:         # Direct callers retain the transitional file behavior. Registry
1005:         # callers supply an adapter-owned identity, so an opaque DSN never
1006:         # reaches Path.resolve/stat in this seam.
1007:         self._binding = binding
1008:         self._canonical = (
1009:             canonical_location(location) if binding is None else binding.key
1010:         )
1011:         self._query = query
1012:         self._clock = clock
1013: 
1014:     # -- the comparison ----------------------------------------------------
1015: 
1016:     def _observe(self) -> tuple[OpenReport, _Earned | None]:
1017:         """Everything the open judged, and the entry it earned — written by
1018:         the caller.
1019: 
1020:         Order is load-bearing and every step of it is a refusal that must fire
1021:         before anything is remembered:
1022: 
1023:         1. Ask the ledger for a head. No head is §D.4's absent-store split.
1024:         2. The location's binding — a DIFFERENT lineage here is replacement,
1025:            and it must be caught before the presented lineage's journal is
1026:            read, or the seam would consult a journal that has never seen this
1027:            location and answer first contact through the very hole the binding
1028:            closes.
1029:         3. The journal comparison — the custody claim, and the stronger one:
1030:            it is the out-of-band memory, and its refusals name the recovery an
1031:            operator actually performs.
1032:         4. The projection comparison, which §D.2 calls a second and separable
1033:            step. Separable is what keeps the seam working when the projection
1034:            is absent, and second is why an ahead-of-the-ledger index cannot be
1035:            reported as a rollback it is not.
1036: 
1037:         None of these writes. The bootstrap entry a first contact earns is
1038:         RETURNED, so a store that passes the journal comparison and then fails
1039:         the projection one leaves no memory claiming its head was accepted.
1040:         """
1041:         presented, ledger_refusal = self._present()
1042:         if presented is None:
1043:             return self._absent(ledger_refusal), None
1044: 
1045:         remembered_lineage = bound_lineage(self._canonical)
1046:         if remembered_lineage is None:
1047:             # No binding for THIS spelling. Before calling it first contact,
1048:             # ask the filesystem whether another spelling already names this
1049:             # same object — a case variant, or a second mount. Live-stat, and
1050:             # only here: once a binding exists for the spelling in use, the
1051:             # exact match above answers and this sweep never runs.
1052:             if self._binding is None:
1053:                 remembered_lineage = aliased_lineage(self._canonical)
1054:             elif self._binding.filesystem:
1055:                 remembered_lineage = aliased_lineage(
1056:                     self._canonical,
1057:                     identity=self._binding.filesystem_identity,
1058:                 )
1059:         if (
1060:             remembered_lineage is not None
1061:             and remembered_lineage != presented.lineage
1062:         ):
1063:             raise LineageReplaced(
1064:                 f"{self._canonical} previously presented lineage "
1065:                 f"{remembered_lineage} and now presents {presented.lineage} — "
1066:                 "a fresh lineage at a location that already had one is a "
1067:                 "replacement wearing the old name, not a new store. If this "
1068:                 "replacement is intended, the licensed way to accept it is the "
1069:                 "explicit trust-reset ceremony, which records the gap"
1070:             )
1071: 
1072:         read = read_journal(presented.lineage)
1073:         presented = self._not_older_than_the_journal(read, presented)
1074: 
1075:         try:
1076:             known = read.established_head()
1077:         except IndeterminateComparison as exc:
1078:             comparison: Compared | Indeterminate = self._degraded(
1079:                 read, presented, exc
1080:             )
1081:             earned: _Earned | None = None
1082:         else:
1083:             outcome, earned = self._judge(known, presented, read)
1084:             comparison = Compared(
1085:                 outcome=outcome, presented=presented, known=known
1086:             )
1087: 
1088:         return (
1089:             OpenReport(
1090:                 comparison=comparison,
1091:                 projection=self._projection(presented),
1092:                 days_since_audit=days_since_audit(read, self._clock()),
1093:             ),
1094:             earned,
1095:         )
1096: 
1097:     def _not_older_than_the_journal(
1098:         self, read: JournalRead, presented: Head
1099:     ) -> Head:
1100:         """Re-observe the store when it looks like it went backward.
1101: 
1102:         **The comparison is between two files read at two different moments,
1103:         and that gap is a hazard the read rules alone cannot close.** The store
1104:         is observed, then the journal is. A writer that commits and journals
1105:         in between leaves the journal holding a head the store's older
1106:         observation does not have — which is bit-for-bit what a rollback looks
1107:         like. Two processes appending to one lineage while a third opens it is
1108:         not exotic: it is the concurrency this backend advertises, and the
1109:         symptom is an operator told their store was rolled back by an ordinary
1110:         pair of concurrent writes (``finding:s3wp3-open-compares-across-time``).
1111: 
1112:         This is WP1's write-path lesson at the next layer up. There the rule
1113:         was that a read rule closing a hazard can be reopened by a write path;
1114:         here a COMPARISON rule closed at read time is reopened by somebody
1115:         else's write between the two reads.
1116: 
1117:         The fix is to make the refusing observation not older than the journal:
1118:         when the presented head sits below what the journal already knows, the
1119:         store is asked once more, and the fresher answer is what gets
1120:         classified. One extra constant-time tail read, on the descending branch
1121:         only — the dominant unchanged case pays nothing, and the branch that
1122:         does pay is the one about to accuse an operator of losing data.
1123: 
1124:         Terminating, not a retry loop, and the residual window fails SAFE. A
1125:         writer committing after the re-read is invisible to the journal read
1126:         that preceded it, so its effect can only be to make *K* lower than
1127:         reality — which classifies unchanged or advanced and pays a verified
1128:         walk, never a false refusal. A genuine rollback is stable across both
1129:         reads and survives.
1130:         """
1131:         floor = _remembered_floor(read)
1132:         if floor is None or presented.ordinal >= floor:
1133:             return presented
1134:         fresh, _refusal = self._present()
1135:         return presented if fresh is None else fresh
1136: 
1137:     def _present(self) -> tuple[Head | None, BaseException | None]:
1138:         """The head the ledger names, or nothing and why.
1139: 
1140:         ``verify(Open())`` and never ``head()``: the Open level is a
1141:         constant-time reverse tail read that validates the genesis and the
1142:         adopted head record, while ``head()`` reaches its answer through a full
1143:         walk — which would make every open pay a Full verification wearing an
1144:         Open label. That single choice is what makes the dominant unchanged
1145:         case O(1).
1146: 
1147:         **The seam never classifies why the ledger refused**, and that is what
1148:         keeps it neutral. §D.4 needs an absent or empty log to branch rather
1149:         than read as corruption, and the adapter says so with its own
1150:         ``GenesisRefused`` — a backend exception this module would have to
1151:         import to recognize, dragging the codec into the seam and hard-coding
1152:         one adapter into a wrapper that wraps any. It does not need to: WP1's
1153:         :func:`~engine.arrival_head_attestation.compare_absent_store` splits on
1154:         MEMORY, not on the store. "Did the ledger name a head" and "does the
1155:         journal remember one" are two questions, and the four cells they make
1156:         are answerable without ever asking why.
1157: 
1158:         A corrupt log lands on the no-head branch too, and lands correctly:
1159:         with a memory here it is a loss and refuses, and without one it is
1160:         pre-genesis with the refusal carried on the report — where the store's
1161:         own operations go on refusing on their own account. The refusal is
1162:         never swallowed either way.
1163:         """
1164:         try:
1165:             return self._evidence.verify(Open()), None
1166:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — see the docstring
1167:             return None, exc
1168: 
1169:     def _absent(self, ledger_refusal: BaseException | None) -> OpenReport:
1170:         """§D.4's split for a location whose ledger names no head.
1171: 
1172:         Decided on memory alone. The binding says which lineage this location
1173:         last presented; that lineage's journal says whether anything was ever
1174:         accepted for it.
1175: 
1176:         The third state is handled here rather than routed through
1177:         :func:`~engine.arrival_head_attestation.compare_absent_store`, which
1178:         takes an entry or ``None``: a journal holding content none of which is
1179:         readable has no entry to pass, and passing ``None`` would answer
1180:         pre-genesis — a store trusted as never-having-existed precisely because
1181:         its memory became unreadable. That is BLOCKING-2's silent
1182:         trust-on-first-use, reached through the absent-store door instead. It
1183:         refuses, and it needs no bound to do so: the question here is whether
1184:         anything was ever accepted, and unreadable content answers yes.
1185:         """
1186:         remembered_lineage = bound_lineage(self._canonical)
1187:         known = None if remembered_lineage is None else read_journal(
1188:             remembered_lineage
1189:         ).known
1190: 
1191:         if known is None:
1192:             entry: HeadAttestation | None = None
1193:         elif isinstance(known, EstablishedHead):
1194:             entry = known.entry
1195:         elif isinstance(known, HeadLowerBound):
1196:             entry = known.at_least
1197:         else:  # HeadUnreadable — content was claimed and none of it survives
1198:             raise StoreLost(
1199:                 f"{self._canonical} holds no readable head, and the journal "
1200:                 f"for lineage {remembered_lineage} holds content none of which "
1201:                 "this build can read — so heads WERE accepted here and the "
1202:                 "store cannot present one. This is not first contact and it is "
1203:                 "not a fresh location. Recovery is the explicit trust-reset "
1204:                 "ceremony"
1205:             ) from ledger_refusal
1206: 
1207:         outcome = compare_absent_store(entry)
1208:         if outcome is AbsentStoreOutcome.STORE_LOST:
1209:             refusal = refusal_for(outcome)
1210:             assert refusal is not None  # the table's only refusing row
1211:             raise refusal(
1212:                 f"{self._canonical} presents no head, but the journal for "
1213:                 f"lineage {remembered_lineage} remembers "
1214:                 f"{_head_text(entry.head if entry else None)}. The witness "
1215:                 "proves what was lost, not its contents. A fresh genesis here "
1216:                 "would be a replacement wearing the old name, so a re-mint is "
1217:                 "refused too. Locate a replica or backup at or above the "
1218:                 "remembered head, or run the explicit trust-reset ceremony"
1219:             ) from ledger_refusal
1220: 
1221:         return OpenReport(
1222:             comparison=PreGenesis(ledger_refusal=ledger_refusal),
1223:             projection=None,
1224:             days_since_audit=None,
1225:         )
1226: 
1227:     def _judge(
1228:         self,
1229:         known: HeadAttestation | None,
1230:         presented: Head,
1231:         read: JournalRead,
1232:     ) -> tuple[Outcome, _Earned | None]:
1233:         """Classify against a head the journal established in full.
1234: 
1235:         ``at_known`` is gathered ONLY on the ascending branch — same lineage,
1236:         higher ordinal — which is what keeps the dominant unchanged case at the
1237:         single ``verify(Open())`` the head already cost. On every other branch
1238:         there is nothing for it to discriminate.
1239: 
1240:         Descent is established before the classifier is asked, because the
1241:         classifier's ADVANCED row requires it and the classifier takes only
1242:         ``at_known``. Two verified walks: ``verify(Full(through=presented))``
1243:         establishes the chain through the presented head, and
1244:         ``head_at(K)`` answers whether the record at the remembered ordinal is
1245:         still the remembered one. Both are needed and neither substitutes for
1246:         the other — a walk that checks only that it reached the presented head
1247:         has verified the current chain while answering nothing about continuity
1248:         with what was previously accepted, which is precisely the "never accept
1249:         height as proof of continuity" failure.
1250: 
1251:         The advance branch is rare BY CONSTRUCTION, because a writer journals
1252:         its own commit under the full-head fence and the next open then sees
1253:         the presented head equal to the remembered one. An advance observed at
1254:         open means an unjournaled writer touched the lineage — a foreign host,
1255:         a restore, a crashed process, or the legacy store path during slices
1256:         3-4 — and paying a verified walk there is correct rather than a
1257:         regression.
1258:         """
1259:         at_known: Head | None = None
1260:         descent_refusal: BaseException | None = None
1261:         if (
1262:             known is not None
1263:             and presented.lineage == known.head.lineage
1264:             and presented.ordinal > known.head.ordinal
1265:         ):
1266:             at_known, descent_refusal = self._descent(known.head, presented)
1267: 
1268:         outcome = compare(known, presented, at_known)
1269:         refusal = refusal_for(outcome)
1270:         if refusal is not None:
1271:             raise refusal(
1272:                 self._refusal_text(outcome, known, presented, descent_refusal)
1273:             ) from descent_refusal
1274: 
1275:         if outcome is Outcome.FIRST_CONTACT:
1276:             return outcome, _Earned(
1277:                 head=presented, kind=Kind.BOOTSTRAP, level=Level.FIRST_CONTACT
1278:             )
1279:         if outcome is Outcome.ADVANCED:
1280:             # The fence sits HERE: after the outcome, before anything is
1281:             # earned. `compare` stays the pure seven-outcome machine — the
1282:             # question the fence asks needs journal state its signature
1283:             # rightly does not carry.
1284:             self._refuse_abandoned_history(read, presented)
1285:             # RETURNED, never written here. `_projection` still runs after this
1286:             # and can refuse, and an advance written from inside the
1287:             # classification would be a memory recording a head the very same
1288:             # open went on to refuse.
1289:             return outcome, _Earned(
1290:                 head=presented, kind=Kind.ADVANCE, level=Level.DESCENDANT
1291:             )
1292:         # UNCHANGED earns NOTHING. A read that touched the write path would
1293:         # make every open a writer, and the byte-compare that proves it is the
1294:         # rule keeping reads off that path.
1295:         return outcome, None
1296: 
1297:     def _refuse_abandoned_history(
1298:         self, read: JournalRead, presented: Head
1299:     ) -> None:
1300:         """Refuse an advance that descends through decreed-away history.
1301: 
1302:         **Identity-keyed, never ordinal spans.** The anchor set is
1303:         ``(ordinal, record_hash)`` taken from the entries the journal holds in
1304:         abandoned epochs — the same discriminator ``SAME_HEIGHT_FORK`` relies
1305:         on. A span would be either vacuous or catastrophic: an operator who
1306:         resets to 5 and lets the store re-advance mints a NEW 6, 7 and 8 inside
1307:         the abandoned span, and fencing by ordinal would refuse every one of
1308:         them forever. Only the exact records that were abandoned are fenced.
1309: 
1310:         Those entries are still readable in the file — epoch scoping excludes
1311:         them from *K*, never from the read — which is what makes them available
1312:         to be the anchor set at all.
1313: 
1314:         **Reach: every coordinate the descent passes, not just its head.** An
1315:         abandoned branch that grew offline presents *N+3* while the journal's
1316:         abandoned entry sits at *N+1*, and head-only checking waves it through.
1317:         Asking ``head_at`` at each fenced anchor's own coordinate is the
1318:         complete form of that check — an anchor can only be touched at its own
1319:         ordinal — and it is spelled in contract ops, so the fence stays
1320:         backend-neutral like the rest of the seam.
1321: 
1322:         **The lift rule, and the one place it is narrower than its wording.**
1323:         A later decree supersedes an earlier abandonment, so an abandoned entry
1324:         is fenced only while no reset has decreed at or above it — otherwise
1325:         recovering the authentic history would be impossible and the ceremony
1326:         would re-brick the store, which is L-3's shape exactly. The narrowing:
1327:         only the CURRENT boundary decree lifts, not any later reset. Read
1328:         literally, an intermediate decree would lift an entry that a subsequent
1329:         decree then abandoned again — reset to 10, then reset back to 5, and
1330:         the 10 is un-fenced by the decree the second ceremony overrode. The
1331:         boundary is the one decree nothing has superseded, so it is the one
1332:         that speaks. Fences more, never less.
1333: 
1334:         **An unanswered probe refuses.** Every branch of this method lands on
1335:         refusal or on a certified-clean path; there is no arm where a failure
1336:         becomes silence. That is the one-directional rule the rest of this seam
1337:         already states at its broad catches, and this method is where it was
1338:         first broken (:class:`FenceProbeUnanswered`).
1339: 
1340:         Cost: one verified walk per fenced anchor ordinal, on the ADVANCED
1341:         branch only — which is rare by construction, because a writer journals
1342:         its own commit.
1343:         """
1344:         abandoned = read.entries[: len(read.entries) - len(read.epoch)]
1345:         if not abandoned:
1346:             return
1347:         decree = read.epoch[0] if read.epoch else None
1348:         if decree is None or decree.kind is not Kind.TRUST_RESET:
1349:             # No boundary decree means nothing was decreed away, so there is
1350:             # nothing to fence — abandoned entries only exist behind a reset.
1351:             return
1352: 
1353:         fenced: dict[int, set[str]] = {}
1354:         for entry in abandoned:
1355:             head = entry.head
1356:             if head.lineage != presented.lineage:
1357:                 continue
1358:             if head.ordinal <= decree.head.ordinal:
1359:                 continue  # lifted: the standing decree reaches at or above it
1360:             if head.ordinal > presented.ordinal:
1361:                 continue  # cannot be on this history's path at all
1362:             fenced.setdefault(head.ordinal, set()).add(head.record_hash)
1363: 
1364:         for ordinal in sorted(fenced):
1365:             try:
1366:                 vouched = self._evidence.head_at(
1367:                     Watermark(lineage=presented.lineage, ordinal=ordinal)
1368:                 )
1369:             except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — see the refusal's docstring
1370:                 # NO ANSWER IS NOT AN ANSWER. Continuing here would read
1371:                 # evidence-absent as absence-of-touch and land the whole fence
1372:                 # on the acceptance side — which is how sol reproduced the
1373:                 # self-erasing loop straight through a transient error.
1374:                 raise FenceProbeUnanswered(
1375:                     f"{self._canonical} presents {_head_text(presented)}, and "
1376:                     f"the ledger could not be asked what sits at ordinal "
1377:                     f"{ordinal}: {exc}. This machine's operator decreed away "
1378:                     f"history above ordinal {decree.head.ordinal}, and without "
1379:                     "that answer this open cannot certify the presented "
1380:                     "history is clear of it. Nothing is wrong with the store "
1381:                     "as far as this went, and nothing has been accepted or "
1382:                     "written — retry the open, and if it keeps failing the "
1383:                     "ledger is what needs looking at"
1384:                 ) from exc
1385:             if vouched.record_hash in fenced[ordinal]:
1386:                 raise AbandonedHistoryFenced(
1387:                     f"{self._canonical} presents {_head_text(presented)}, whose "
1388:                     f"verified history holds {vouched.record_hash} at ordinal "
1389:                     f"{ordinal} — a record this machine's operator decreed away "
1390:                     f"when they reset trust to ordinal {decree.head.ordinal}. "
1391:                     "The chain is intact; that is not the question. Accepting it "
1392:                     "would silently reverse the decree, and journaling the "
1393:                     "advance would erase the evidence that it had been reversed. "
1394:                     "If this history is the one to keep, run the trust-reset "
1395:                     "ceremony to decree the recovered head — that is the "
1396:                     "licensed way, and it records the gap"
1397:                 )
1398: 
1399:     def _descent(
1400:         self, known: Head, presented: Head
1401:     ) -> tuple[Head | None, BaseException | None]:
1402:         """Was the presented head reached BY DESCENT from the remembered one?
1403: 
1404:         Answers with the head the ledger vouches for at the remembered
1405:         coordinate, which is the ADVANCED/REWRITE discriminator, or ``None``
1406:         when it will not vouch for anything there.
1407: 
1408:         Any failure of either walk answers ``None``, which classifies REWRITE,
1409:         which refuses — the same one-directional argument :func:`_vouched_at`
1410:         makes. A corrupt log therefore surfaces as a refusal with the
1411:         corruption chained as the cause, so the operator is told both things:
1412:         the comparison would not proceed, and here is what the walk hit.
1413:         """
1414:         try:
1415:             self._evidence.verify(Full(through=presented))
1416:             return (
1417:                 self._evidence.head_at(
1418:                     Watermark(lineage=known.lineage, ordinal=known.ordinal)
1419:                 ),
1420:                 None,
1421:             )
1422:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — see the docstring
1423:             return None, exc
1424: 
1425:     def _degraded(
1426:         self,
1427:         read: JournalRead,
1428:         presented: Head,
1429:         refusal: IndeterminateComparison,
1430:     ) -> Indeterminate:
1431:         """**The IndeterminateComparison posture, and the argument for it.**
1432: 
1433:         The choice: does the seam surface an incomplete journal read as a
1434:         refusal demanding an operator decision, or proceed under an explicitly
1435:         labeled degradation? **It proceeds — after firing every refusal the
1436:         incomplete read still soundly supports.** That is not the two-valued
1437:         question it looks like, and the third answer is the whole of it.
1438: 
1439:         **Why not refuse.** An incomplete read persists until an operator
1440:         acts. The journal is append-only and never rewritten, and the torn-
1441:         tail guard preserves a crashed writer's fragment rather than removing
1442:         it, so a line lost to an ordinary crash sits in ``skipped`` on every
1443:         later read — recorded forever, weighed only until a trust-reset
1444:         ceremony decrees past it, since the epoch-scoped weighting stops
1445:         counting a loss the decree superseded. Until that ceremony, a seam
1446:         that refused on it would make one crashed writer a store that never
1447:         opens again — which is verbatim the argument WP1's amended ruling used
1448:         to REJECT refusing on mid-file damage, one level down: "it made an
1449:         ordinary crash a permanent incident, and it claimed a protection this
1450:         location cannot deliver anyway — anyone able to corrupt the journal can
1451:         delete it instead and be met with trust-on-first-use." Refusing here
1452:         would re-impose at the composition boundary the exact verdict the
1453:         module removed, which is WP1's own write-path lesson generalized: a
1454:         rule relaxed in a module can be re-tightened by its caller, undoing the
1455:         ruling without touching the code it was made about.
1456: 
1457:         **Why "proceed" alone would be dishonest, and what makes it not that.**
1458:         A bound is not nothing. Two of the four refusals are still SOUND
1459:         against it and both are raised here:
1460: 
1461:         * A presented head BELOW the bound is a rollback. The accepted head is
1462:           at least the bound, so it is certainly above what is being presented.
1463:         * A presented head at the bound's ordinal with a DIFFERENT hash is a
1464:           same-height fork. The bound is a real entry — a head this machine
1465:           accepted at that ordinal — and the store presents a different record
1466:           there. The lost lines cannot make that agree.
1467: 
1468:         What remains indeterminate is the region at and above the bound:
1469:         equal is not unchanged (it may be a rollback from the very entry the
1470:         read missed) and higher is not advanced (nothing bounds the accepted
1471:         head from ABOVE, so a lost entry may sit above both). Those two proceed
1472:         answers are the ones that are unobtainable, and the seam does not claim
1473:         either — :class:`Indeterminate` carries no outcome at all.
1474: 
1475:         **How never-silent is satisfied without a refusal.** Three ways, and
1476:         none of them is a field somebody has to remember to read:
1477: 
1478:         * The report's degraded case is its own TYPE with no ``outcome``
1479:           attribute, so no expression reads an answer off it without naming the
1480:           case — WP1's unignorable-by-construction discipline, applied at the
1481:           seam's own boundary.
1482:         * The refusal that was not raised is carried on it, so a caller wanting
1483:           the strict posture raises it and nothing has to be reconstructed.
1484:         * **Nothing is written.** A degraded open journals no entry and records
1485:           no binding, so the degradation never launders itself into a memory,
1486:           and the bound never rises on evidence the read did not have. That
1487:           also keeps ``HeadUnreadable`` clear of BLOCKING-2: a journal holding
1488:           content none of which is readable is NOT granted the bootstrap
1489:           entry that first contact gets, so it is never trusted on sight
1490:           precisely because it became unreadable.
1491: 
1492:         The evidence is durable without being written: ``skipped`` is derived
1493:         from the journal's own bytes, so every future open re-derives the same
1494:         degradation. Nothing is lost by not recording it, and a record would be
1495:         the one thing that could make a lost line look accounted for.
1496: 
1497:         And it stays honest under the adversarial reading. An attacker who can
1498:         corrupt a line can delete the journal instead and get first contact,
1499:         so a refusal here buys nothing against one — while it costs everything
1500:         against a crash. The refusals that survive are the ones an attacker
1501:         cannot evade by damaging the journal, because damage cannot lower a
1502:         bound below what the surviving entries prove.
1503:         """
1504:         known = read.known
1505:         if not isinstance(known, HeadLowerBound):
1506:             # HeadUnreadable: no bound at all, so every comparison declines —
1507:             # rollback included. There is nothing to compare against.
1508:             return Indeterminate(
1509:                 presented=presented,
1510:                 refusal=refusal,
1511:                 skipped=read.skipped,
1512:                 at_least=None,
1513:             )
1514: 
1515:         bound = known.at_least.head
1516:         missed = "; ".join(known.skipped)
1517:         # No lineage check: the journal is keyed by lineage, so every entry in
1518:         # it is this lineage's. Replacement is the binding's question and it
1519:         # was already asked, before this journal was opened.
1520:         if presented.ordinal < bound.ordinal:
1521:             raise HeadRollback(
1522:                 f"{self._canonical} presents ordinal {presented.ordinal}, and "
1523:                 f"this machine accepted at least ordinal {bound.ordinal} for "
1524:                 f"lineage {presented.lineage}. This read of the journal is "
1525:                 f"incomplete — it missed: {missed} — but a head below the "
1526:                 "bound is below the accepted head whatever the read missed. "
1527:                 "Locate a replica or backup at or above the accepted head; "
1528:                 "never move the witness backward to match the store"
1529:             )
1530:         if (
1531:             presented.ordinal == bound.ordinal
1532:             and presented.record_hash != bound.record_hash
1533:         ):
1534:             raise HeadFork(
1535:                 f"{self._canonical} presents {presented.record_hash} at "
1536:                 f"ordinal {presented.ordinal}, and this machine accepted "
1537:                 f"{bound.record_hash} at that same ordinal. Two different "
1538:                 "records claim one height. This read of the journal is "
1539:                 f"incomplete — it missed: {missed} — but the entry the bound "
1540:                 "rests on is one the journal does hold. Freeze both branches "
1541:                 "and collect evidence; never pick the taller branch"
1542:             )
1543:         return Indeterminate(
1544:             presented=presented,
1545:             refusal=refusal,
1546:             skipped=read.skipped,
1547:             at_least=bound,
1548:         )
1549: 
1550:     def _projection(self, presented: Head) -> ProjectionReport | None:
1551:         """Compare what the projection accounts for against the presented head.
1552: 
1553:         Comparing the watermark's ORDINAL is free and gives the whole
1554:         classification — behind (ordinary staleness, catch-up's job), level, or
1555:         ahead of the ledger, which is tail-truncation evidence that survives
1556:         independently of the journal. Only when they disagree does the seam
1557:         call ``head_at``, which turns the coordinate into a head the ledger
1558:         vouches for; on the ahead branch it refuses rather than answering,
1559:         because the log holds no record at that ordinal — and the refusal IS
1560:         the answer.
1561: 
1562:         Behind is never a refusal. A projection that lags is the ordinary
1563:         state of a store between a commit and its next catch-up, and refusing
1564:         it would make the seam an availability problem rather than a witness.
1565:         """
1566:         if self._query is None:
1567:             return None
1568:         watermark = self._query.projected_through()
1569:         if watermark is None:
1570:             return ProjectionReport(
1571:                 agreement=ProjectionAgreement.ABSENT, watermark=None
1572:             )
1573: 
1574:         if watermark.lineage != presented.lineage:
1575:             # `head_at` refuses a watermark from another lineage with the
1576:             # contract's own NotAuthority, which is exactly the right answer:
1577:             # this projection is not a projection of this log. Letting it out
1578:             # keeps the refusal the contract names rather than restating it.
1579:             self._evidence.head_at(watermark)
1580:             raise ProjectionAheadOfLedger(
1581:                 f"the projection beside {self._canonical} reports lineage "
1582:                 f"{watermark.lineage} while the log presents "
1583:                 f"{presented.lineage}, and the ledger vouched for the "
1584:                 "watermark anyway — the projection and the ledger disagree "
1585:                 "about which lineage this store is"
1586:             )
1587: 
1588:         if watermark.ordinal > presented.ordinal:
1589:             cause: BaseException | None = None
1590:             try:
1591:                 self._evidence.head_at(watermark)
1592:             except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — the refusal IS the answer
1593:                 cause = exc
1594:             raise ProjectionAheadOfLedger(
1595:                 f"the projection beside {self._canonical} accounts for "
1596:                 f"ordinal {watermark.ordinal} of lineage {watermark.lineage}, "
1597:                 f"but the log presents only ordinal {presented.ordinal}. A "
1598:                 "projection ahead of its ledger is what a truncated log looks "
1599:                 "like from the outside. Re-derive the projection from the "
1600:                 "ledger; never edit the ledger to match the projection"
1601:             ) from cause
1602: 
1603:         return ProjectionReport(
1604:             agreement=(
1605:                 ProjectionAgreement.LEVEL
1606:                 if watermark.ordinal == presented.ordinal
1607:                 else ProjectionAgreement.BEHIND
1608:             ),
1609:             watermark=watermark,
1610:         )
1611: 
1612:     def _refusal_text(
1613:         self,
1614:         outcome: Outcome,
1615:         known: HeadAttestation | None,
1616:         presented: Head,
1617:         descent_refusal: BaseException | None,
1618:     ) -> str:
1619:         """A refusal that names §11's response, not just the state.
1620: 
1621:         §11's recovery table maps each state to a named response, and carrying
1622:         it in the message is what makes a refusal actionable at the moment it
1623:         fires rather than an incident somebody has to go and look up.
1624:         """
1625:         responses = {
1626:             Outcome.ROLLBACK: (
1627:                 "Locate a replica or backup at or above the accepted head; "
1628:                 "never move the witness backward to match the store"
1629:             ),
1630:             Outcome.SAME_HEIGHT_FORK: (
1631:                 "Freeze both branches and collect evidence under an explicit "
1632:                 "incident procedure; never pick the taller branch"
1633:             ),
1634:             Outcome.REWRITE: (
1635:                 "The chain in front of us may verify perfectly and still be a "
1636:                 "different history than the one accepted. Collect evidence "
1637:                 "before anything writes to this store"
1638:             ),
1639:             Outcome.LINEAGE_REPLACED: (
1640:                 "A different lineage is presented where a known one was "
1641:                 "expected; the licensed way to accept it is the explicit "
1642:                 "trust-reset ceremony, which records the gap"
1643:             ),
1644:         }
1645:         remembered = _head_text(known.head if known is not None else None)
1646:         seen = (
1647:             ""
1648:             if known is None
1649:             else f", accepted {_observed_text(known)}"
1650:         )
1651:         why = (
1652:             ""
1653:             if descent_refusal is None
1654:             else f" The descent walk did not complete: {descent_refusal}."
1655:         )
1656:         return (
1657:             f"{outcome.value}: {self._canonical} presents "
1658:             f"{_head_text(presented)}, and this machine remembers "
1659:             f"{remembered}{seen}.{why} {responses[outcome]}"
1660:         )
1661: 
1662:     # -- custody, witnessed ------------------------------------------------
1663: 
1664: class AttestedLedger(_HeadObservation):
1665:     """An :class:`~engine.arrival_contract.ArrivalLedger` that remembers.
1666: 
1667:     Two things, and no third: it compares at construction, and it journals
1668:     after a successful ``mint``, ``append`` or ``replicate``. Everything else
1669:     is delegation.
1670: 
1671:     **Delegation is by explicit method, never** ``__getattr__``. A catch-all
1672:     would forward ``import_prefix`` — a mutation the contract Protocol
1673:     deliberately does not declare but which is in ``LEDGER_MUTATIONS``
1674:     regardless, because the custody/reads separation must cover every op that
1675:     can change what a lineage holds. Forwarded silently, it would be a mutation
1676:     reachable through the attested handle that the seam does not journal: a
1677:     hole in the witness, opened by a convenience nobody wrote down. It is
1678:     therefore NOT reachable through this wrapper, and a future op added to the
1679:     adapter is not reachable either until somebody decides how it is witnessed.
1680: 
1681:     **The IndeterminateComparison posture** — the WP's flagged design point — is
1682:     in :meth:`_degraded`, with the argument.
1683:     """
1684: 
1685:     def __init__(
1686:         self,
1687:         ledger: ArrivalLedger,
1688:         *,
1689:         location: str,
1690:         query: ArrivalQuery | None = None,
1691:         clock: Callable[[], float] = time.time,
1692:         binding: BindingIdentity | None = None,
1693:     ) -> None:
1694:         """Compare, then write what the comparison earned.
1695: 
1696:         ``clock`` is injected because WP1's module reads no clock — every
1697:         ``observed_at`` there is a caller-supplied argument — and this is the
1698:         caller. It is what keeps staleness reporting testable without freezing
1699:         time inside the journal.
1700: 
1701:         **This is the ONLY place the open path writes**, and that is the whole
1702:         of "nothing writes until every refusal has had its chance". Observation
1703:         is pure with respect to the journal — it returns an :class:`_Earned`
1704:         and writes nothing — so an open that refuses anywhere leaves no memory
1705:         claiming it accepted the thing it refused.
1706: 
1707:         Stating it per-branch was not enough: the first-contact branch deferred
1708:         while the advance branch wrote inline, and a store that passed the
1709:         journal comparison and then failed the projection one kept an
1710:         ``advance`` entry for the head it had just been refused
1711:         (``finding:s3wp3-gate-advance-journaled-before-projection-refusal``).
1712:         The rule is now carried by the return type, and
1713:         ``test_only_the_constructor_and_the_producers_write_to_the_journal``
1714:         pins it against the branch somebody adds next.
1715:         """
1716:         super().__init__(
1717:             ledger, location=location, query=query, clock=clock, binding=binding
1718:         )
1719:         self._ledger = ledger
1720:         report, earned = self._observe()
1721:         if earned is not None:
1722:             self._write(earned)
1723:         self.opened: OpenReport = report
1724:         """What the compare-on-open established. See :class:`OpenReport`."""
1725: 
1726:     def _write(self, earned: _Earned) -> None:
1727:         """Write what an observation earned, once it has earned it.
1728: 
1729:         A bootstrap goes through :func:`bootstrap` rather than straight to
1730:         ``append_entry`` so that the level validation and the binding stay on
1731:         one path — a seam that appended its own bootstrap would be the second
1732:         place the canonical form is applied, which is how two spellings
1733:         diverge.
1734:         """
1735:         if earned.kind is Kind.BOOTSTRAP:
1736:             bootstrap(
1737:                 earned.head,
1738:                 level=earned.level,
1739:                 location=self._location,
1740:                 observed_at=self._clock(),
1741:                 binding=self._binding,
1742:             )
1743:             return
1744:         append_entry(
1745:             HeadAttestation(
1746:                 head=earned.head,
1747:                 kind=earned.kind,
1748:                 level=earned.level,
1749:                 observed_at=self._clock(),
1750:                 location=self._canonical,
1751:             )
1752:         )
1753: 
1754:     def mint(self, options: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Head:
1755:         """Mint through the wrapper, and the bootstrap receipt is a consequence.
1756: 
1757:         Slice 4's sidecar gets its receipt by using the ordinary
1758:         registry-opened ledger: there is no privileged path and no special API,
1759:         which mirrors the sink's own rule that migration appends through
1760:         ordinary ``append``. The level is ``mint`` — this process minted the
1761:         genesis, so the journal is witnessed from genesis forward and slice 6's
1762:         exit criterion can tell it apart from a store trusted on sight.
1763:         """
1764:         head = self._ledger.mint(options)
1765:         try:
1766:             bootstrap(
1767:                 head,
1768:                 level=Level.MINT,
1769:                 location=self._location,
1770:                 observed_at=self._clock(),
1771:                 binding=self._binding,
1772:             )
1773:         except (OSError, AttestationRefusal) as exc:
1774:             raise NotWitnessed(
1775:                 f"the genesis for lineage {head.lineage} is COMMITTED at "
1776:                 f"{self._canonical}, and its bootstrap receipt could not be "
1777:                 f"written: {exc}. The store exists and this machine has no "
1778:                 "memory of it, so its next open is first contact rather than "
1779:                 "the mint-level receipt slice 6 checks for",
1780:                 head=head,
1781:             ) from exc
1782:         return head
1783: 
1784:     def append(
1785:         self, expected: Head | None, drafts: Sequence[RecordDraft]
1786:     ) -> Commit:
1787:         """Append, then journal the commit — §D.3's O(1)-unchanged-open design.
1788: 
1789:         A successful append returns a ``Commit`` whose ``before`` and ``after``
1790:         are full heads, compared under the full-head fence: the writer already
1791:         holds the strongest descent evidence there is, so recording it at
1792:         ``Level.COMMIT`` means the NEXT open sees the presented head equal to
1793:         the remembered one and takes the O(1) unchanged branch. Without this
1794:         the next open would observe an advance and pay a verified walk for
1795:         evidence this process had already gathered and thrown away.
1796:         """
1797:         commit = self._ledger.append(expected, drafts)
1798:         self._witness(commit)
1799:         return commit
1800: 
1801:     def replicate(
1802:         self, expected: Head | None, records: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]
1803:     ) -> Commit:
1804:         """Replicate, then journal the commit. Same fence, same evidence.
1805: 
1806:         Replication assigns no coordinates — it inserts an exact
1807:         pre-coordinated suffix — but it goes through the same full-head compare,
1808:         so the commit it returns is the same evidence an append's is and it is
1809:         recorded at the same level.
1810:         """
1811:         commit = self._ledger.replicate(expected, records)
1812:         self._witness(commit)
1813:         return commit
1814: 
1815:     def _witness(self, commit: Commit) -> None:
1816:         """Journal a commit, or say loudly that it went unwitnessed.
1817: 
1818:         The append has already landed when this runs, so a failure here cannot
1819:         be reported as a failed append — the store has advanced past its
1820:         witness, and §05's ``committed`` versus ``witnessed`` distinction is
1821:         exactly the thing that must not be collapsed into "saved". Raising
1822:         :class:`NotWitnessed` is the never-silent mechanism, and its type says
1823:         the data is safe.
1824:         """
1825:         try:
1826:             append_entry(
1827:                 HeadAttestation(
1828:                     head=commit.after,
1829:                     kind=Kind.ADVANCE,
1830:                     level=Level.COMMIT,
1831:                     observed_at=self._clock(),
1832:                     location=self._canonical,
1833:                 )
1834:             )
1835:         except (OSError, AttestationRefusal) as exc:
1836:             raise NotWitnessed(
1837:                 f"{len(commit.records)} record(s) are COMMITTED at "
1838:                 f"{self._canonical} through {_head_text(commit.after)}, and "
1839:                 f"the journal entry for them could not be written: {exc}. The "
1840:                 "store has advanced past its witness, so the next open will "
1841:                 "observe an advance and pay a verified walk for it",
1842:                 head=commit.after,
1843:                 commit=commit,
1844:             ) from exc
1845: 
1846:     # -- reads, delegated unchanged ----------------------------------------
1847: 
1848:     def head(self, lineage: str | None = None) -> Head:
1849:         """The currently complete head."""
1850:         return self._ledger.head(lineage)
1851: 
1852:     def head_at(self, watermark: Watermark) -> Head:
1853:         """Resolve a projection's watermark into the verified head it names."""
1854:         return self._ledger.head_at(watermark)
1855: 
1856:     def read(self, coordinate: int) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
1857:         """The exact record, after establishing its membership in the lineage."""
1858:         return self._ledger.read(coordinate)
1859: 
1860:     def scan(
1861:         self, *, after: int | None = None, through: Head | None = None
1862:     ) -> Any:
1863:         """An ordered, consistent prefix range and no later record."""
1864:         return self._ledger.scan(after=after, through=through)
1865: 
1866:     def verify(self, scope: VerifyScope) -> Head:
1867:         """Verify through a named head; return the head the claim covers."""
1868:         return self._ledger.verify(scope)
1869: 
1870:     def export(self, *, through: Head, codec: str) -> ExportedPrefix:
1871:         """Deterministic portable records plus a manifest, for a prefix."""
1872:         return self._ledger.export(through=through, codec=codec)
1873: 
1874:     def capabilities(self) -> Capabilities:
1875:         """The wrapped backend's self-report, unchanged.
1876: 
1877:         Not this wrapper's. Everything ``Capabilities`` describes — profiles,
1878:         durability, verification levels, concurrency, codecs — is a property of
1879:         the backend holding the bytes, and the seam changes none of them.
1880:         Amending the report to mention the witness would be advertising a
1881:         guarantee at the layer that does not provide it.
1882:         """
1883:         return self._ledger.capabilities()
1884: 
1885:     def close(self) -> None:
1886:         """Release the wrapped custody handle, when the adapter owns one."""
1887:         close = getattr(self._ledger, "close", None)
1888:         if callable(close):
1889:             close()
1890: 
1891: 
1892: def _observed_text(entry: HeadAttestation) -> str:
1893:     """When and on what evidence a remembered head was accepted."""
1894:     return f"{entry.kind.value}/{entry.level.value} at {entry.observed_at}"
